PP370-T03 前端完整量測接線：完整入口集中執行 contracts、geometry、當前真 Next 操作頁、原 browser components。真 Next 使用同輪核發 session，檢查九個系統頁籤及既有主要工作頁；只讀瀏覽與未儲存表單，來源選取沿用已完成案例。Chromium 原始 V8 ranges、真 source map、source hashes、開始時間及階段結果一同保存。Reporter 只重新轉換同一成功階段的原始 ranges，與原 Node／component counters 合併；完整來源集合及分母不得縮減，不接受手填 hits 或以 standalone UI 結果代替完整 gate。

完整 harness 的 Git 身分只在本輪隔離來源建立工具用 snapshot；僅加入已核對 public inventory 的明確檔案清單，記錄原 checkout HEAD 與逐檔 SHA，不接觸原 `.git`、不建立正式發行 commit／tag 或 remote。後續來源修改仍由正常 dirty fingerprint 及逐檔內容驗證，不把未追蹤的工具輸出或新秘密加入 snapshot。

完整suite先有真前提，僅來源／新失敗使既有結果不適用才再量最終完整收據；不以次數為成果、不用mock/stub/fixture adapter/假token/假時計或假模型成功。過時case不因名稱自動退役，有效意圖一對一保留。高風險未解／未接受及修補包UNKNOWN如實揭露，計畫核准不是風險豁免或原憑證立即操作核准。

Execution rules:

- Pure projection/hash/diff functions may be tested directly. Persistence,
  concurrency, graph reads and API acceptance must use real configured isolated
  PostgreSQL/Neo4j; configured Keycloak/OpenSearch/storage are required whenever
  the corresponding path is exercised. Disposable seeded records are test data,
  not fake service adapters. No live customer/project data is a test target.
- Provider generation is not part of tag graph repair. Do not use a fake LLM to
  claim auto-tag end-to-end success. Validate mutation guards and the real
  post-tag-persistence path without generation; any full tagging/ingestion
  journey requiring a Provider remains separately authorized/blocked.
- Compare a real published Neo4j graph against PostgreSQL assignment identities
  and approved metadata, not only counts or a UI enriched from PostgreSQL.
- Test interrupted dual-store work without claiming distributed atomicity.
  Cleanup must target only uniquely identified disposable services/data; do not
  remove shared resources or broad paths.
- Global Frontend/Backend 80% coverage requirements remain unchanged. Measure
  changed logic as additional evidence; do not present focused coverage as the
  full repository gate.

Before Gate 4, permitted verification is only `spec:doctor`, `spec:trace`,
`plan:doctor`, `plan:approved`, `test:plan` and `git diff --check`. The approval
check must fail while this plan is pending. After Gate 4, use the focused suite
and affected real-service regression/coverage commands in DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md.
Image build, current-environment data repair, Neo4j DDL and Kubernetes deployment
are not test-design authorization.

## Coverage Target

- Minimum total automated test coverage: 80%.
- Apply the 80% threshold to frontend and backend separately when both contain
  application logic.
- Coverage must be measured by CI or the repository harness, not estimated
  manually.
- Coverage reports must be generated in machine-readable form so
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check` can verify the threshold.
- Exclusions must be explicit and limited to generated code, framework bootstrap
  files, type declarations, migrations without logic, and deployment templates
  that are validated by deployment-specific checks.

## Live-Only Verification Policy

`TEST-002` is the controlling test policy for all future NomoSmart v1.0 work.
It supersedes older plan language that allowed mocks, local fakes, fixture
adapters, deterministic adapters, mocked OIDC sessions, static-only E2E success,
or stubbed external services.

- Product runtime, development runtime, unit tests, component tests, API tests,
  integration tests, E2E tests, coverage gates, and release acceptance must use
  real implementations and real configured development/test services.
- Test data may be isolated through disposable schemas, buckets, indexes,
  realms, namespaces, transactions, and cleanup jobs, but the service under
  test must be real.
- Missing PostgreSQL, Keycloak/OIDC, Redis/Celery, S3/RustFS, OpenSearch,
  Neo4j, OCR, AI provider, browser, Docker, Helm, or other required tooling
  must produce failed, blocked, or unavailable results. A harness command must
  not downgrade the result to a mock, fake, fixture, deterministic, or
  static-only success.
- Static scans, lint, schema checks, documentation checks, and traceability
  checks remain useful quality gates, but they cannot satisfy behavioral
  acceptance for a feature that has runtime behavior.

## Test Levels

Unit tests:

- Validate pure business logic, permission evaluation, validation rules,
  configuration parsing, data transformation, chunking helpers, workflow state
  transitions, and UI utility functions.
- Exercise the real code path and real configured service dependencies for any
  behavior that crosses network, filesystem, database, AI/provider, storage,
  search, graph, worker, or identity boundaries.
- Do not use mocks, stubs, fakes, fixture adapters, deterministic adapters, or
  hard-coded success responses as the passing path.

Frontend component tests:

- Cover dashboard cards, navigation, wizards, modals, forms, tables, graphs,
  dropdown-based Header language switching, validation messages, loading states, empty states, and
  disabled/error/success states.
- Verify accessibility basics such as labels, keyboard navigation, focus states,
  and status messaging that is not color-only.
- Run against real frontend/backend/API behavior for data-loading,
  authorization, mutation, export, graph, chat, and workflow states. Mocked
  `fetch`, fixture API payloads, or client-only fake completion may not satisfy
  acceptance.

Backend API tests:

- Cover authentication context, authorization, role permission union logic,
  project owner rules, CRUD behavior, validation errors, pagination/filtering,
  optimistic locking where required, and audit-friendly failure paths.
- Verify `X-User-Id`, `X-Employee-Id`, and arbitrary identity headers are not
  accepted as identity sources in any environment.
- Cover project membership and project role data-scope checks in combination
  with global RBAC permissions.
- Use real development/test PostgreSQL and real configured service
  dependencies with isolated schemas, transactions, namespaces, and cleanup.
- Do not require production credentials. Use dedicated development/test
  credentials for live services and mark tests blocked or unavailable when they
  are not configured.

## Backend Foundation Milestone 1 Test Design

- Runtime/configuration: verify Python settings load safe Development values,
  reject missing/malformed required secrets, keep AI/OCR provider data out of
  environment configuration, parse the 64-hex encryption key and expose no
  credential through errors, health, readiness or logs.
- API contract: verify `/api/v1` routing, absence of an unversioned compatibility
  API, request IDs, the `code/message/details/request_id` error envelope, offset
  administration pagination and stable cursor history pagination.
- Database/migration: apply `V001__initial_schema.sql` to a clean PostgreSQL
  database; verify UUID keys, UTC `timestamptz`, foreign keys, unique/check
  constraints, optimistic locks, default roles/system parameters and agreement
  between Flyway schema and SQLAlchemy models.
- Encryption/audit: cover AES-256-GCM randomized ciphertext, decrypt, tamper,
  wrong-key, malformed-envelope and key-version behavior. Verify audit rows are
  append-only and contain no token, password, API key, private key, LDAP bind
  credential or sensitive document body.
- Idempotency/outbox: replay identical keys, reject key reuse with a different
  request hash, recover in-progress work and prove upload/sync/review/publish
  primitives cannot create duplicate business records after retry or crash.
- Authentication: validate issuer, audience, signature, expiration, not-before,
  required claims and JWKS rotation; reject arbitrary identity headers, disabled
  or unsynced users and users without effective permissions.
- Authorization: cover permission union, default deny, independent
  view/create/edit/delete semantics, project membership/owner intersection and
  cross-project denial for every foundation API.
- Identity/System Management: cover failed-sync preservation, masked identity
  settings, 10-minute user/session/scope-bound unlock state, atomic candidate
  activation, system-parameter validation and role/external-group mappings.
- `OCR-001`: cover OCR CRUD, exactly one active system default, optional project
  default resolution, document-level selection, batch-shared OCR selection,
  masked/encrypted credentials, provider-adapter connection tests, config
  snapshots, text-layer skip, forced-OCR confirmation, required/forced-OCR
  failure/retry, inactive-model denial, referenced-delete denial,
  unreferenced-delete success, permission and audit behavior.
- `IMPORT-006` / `UPLOAD-SEC-001`: stream content hashing, random-salt uniqueness,
  canonical lowercase extension, `.markdown` to `.md`, filename sanitization,
  S3 key construction, no deduplication, orphan cleanup/outbox and quarantine
  scan accept/reject/disabled transitions with no extraction before acceptance.
- `SEARCH-001` / `VERSION-001`: profile/dimension compatibility, deterministic
  vector IDs, staging/published isolation, indefinite published retention,
  Active Version Manifest-only retrieval, fail-closed missing/stale manifests,
  authorized old-version switching, optimistic concurrency and incompatible
  profile re-embedding/review requirements.
- Coverage: Backend application logic must meet 80% or higher; auth,
  authorization, migration, config, encryption and secret handling remain
  mandatory even when aggregate coverage exceeds the threshold.

## Milestone 2 Test Design: AUTH-001 / AUTH-002 / PERM-001 / PROJECT-001

- Live OIDC frontend: verify authorization URL issuer/client/callback/scope,
  cryptographically random state/nonce/PKCE S256 inputs, callback state and code
  validation, safe same-origin return paths, explicit loading/error states and
  logout end-session behavior. Reject missing/mismatched state and external
  return URLs.
- Token boundary: prove access token, refresh token, authorization code and PKCE
  verifier never enter localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, readable cookies,
  URL history after callback, analytics or logs. Verify reload uses Keycloak SSO,
  concurrent expiry produces one refresh, 401 retries at most once, 403 never
  refreshes and failed restoration clears state before returning to login.
- Secure logout: verify the authenticated Header user-name control opens and
  closes a keyboard-accessible menu containing Logout; selecting Logout calls the
  Backend logout API once, clears memory-only tokens and transient OIDC cookies,
  avoids all persistent browser storage, closes the menu, redirects through
  Keycloak end-session, and returns to `/login`. Verify browser back/reload does
  not restore a NomoSmart session after logout.
- Backend logout and denylist: verify `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` requires a
  valid Bearer JWT, stores only an irreversible token identity until `exp`,
  revokes session-bound grants such as authentication-settings unlock, writes a
  token-safe audit record, and causes replay of the same unexpired access token
  against any protected API to return 401. Cover tokens with and without `jti`,
  expired tokens, duplicate logout calls and cleanup eligibility.
- Keycloak Theme: verify the packaged Keycloak 26 account/password and OTP pages
  preserve the approved NomoSmart visual, errors, visible focus, keyboard flow,
  responsive targets and zh/en strings while no credential is submitted to a
  NomoSmart origin.
- Backend authentication: cover valid, expired, not-yet-valid, wrong issuer,
  wrong audience, invalid signature and rotated JWKS JWTs; unsynchronized,
  disabled and no-effective-permission users; missing Bearer token; ignored
  identity headers; and sanitized 401/403 responses.
- Session-expiry reauthentication guidance: verify access-token pre-expiry
  refresh succeeds silently, failed refresh or one failed 401 retry clears
  memory-only tokens/current user/permissions, displays one global
  session-expired re-login prompt and never loops on the loading state. Verify
  the re-login action uses a same-site safe `returnTo` and does not persist
  token material.
- Session-expired form draft recovery: verify only explicitly registered,
  non-sensitive fields are submitted to a database-backed draft API when the
  re-login was triggered by session expiry. The frontend must not store form
  field payloads in `sessionStorage`, `localStorage`, IndexedDB, URL or readable
  cookies; browser storage may contain only short-lived draft id / nonce /
  returnTo metadata. Database payloads must be AES-256-GCM envelope encrypted
  and recovery must require matching user ID, same return path, one-time reauth
  nonce and unexpired `session_expired_form_draft_ttl_minutes`; the UI must ask
  before restoring. Verify decline, successful submit, normal logout,
  direct/new login, different user, different path, nonce mismatch, TTL expiry
  and parameter value `0` delete or ignore drafts. Verify passwords, OTP, API
  keys, secrets, LDAP/AD credentials, tokens, PKCE data and file bodies are
  never stored in plaintext, returned to unauthorized users or written to audit.
- Keycloak snapshot collection: cover user/group pagination, per-user group
  retrieval, empty/optional attributes, invalid employee IDs, duplicate stable
  identifiers, LDAP `manager` DN second-pass resolution against synchronized
  `ldap_dn`, legacy `manager_employee_id` fallback, rate limit, timeout,
  malformed response and secret-safe errors.
- Reconciliation: on complete snapshots verify user/group upsert, removed-user
  disablement, group deactivation, manager links, external group mappings and
  only `external_sync` role replacement. Prove `manual` roles survive, repeated
  runs are idempotent and any partial fetch/validation/database failure preserves
  the prior successful state.
- Worker and schedule: cover outbox claiming, Celery dispatch, daily `0 2 * * *`
  in `Asia/Taipei`, manual/scheduled trigger metadata, PostgreSQL mutual
  exclusion, one active run, retry/backoff, crash recovery, safe run counts and
  no duplicate reconciliation under worker concurrency 2.
- User and role APIs: cover filtering/pagination, immutable synchronized fields,
  editable local supplemental fields, NomoSmart-only status, role CRUD/soft
  deactivation, protected system roles, manual role membership, external group
  mapping validation, independent create/edit/delete permissions and audit.
- Permission matrices: verify role-isolated read/replace, multi-role union,
  default deny, inactive-role exclusion, `can_edit` naming, stale lock rejection,
  atomic validation and immediate authorization effect on the next request.
- Project APIs: cover atomic create with models/members/creator Owner, detail and
  scope-filtered list, update/archive, owner/editor/viewer membership, multiple
  project roles, Owner-table synchronization, disabled-user rejection, last
  Owner protection, RBAC plus Owner checks, stale lock conflicts and historical
  data retention after member removal.
- Migration and integration: apply V001+V002 on a clean PostgreSQL database,
  verify constraints/defaults/indexes and model parity, run deterministic
  Keycloak/Celery fakes, then a bounded Development Keycloak PKCE/admin smoke.
  Tests must not depend on a production identity provider or commit credentials.
- Coverage and regression: frontend and backend application logic each remain at
  least 80%; authentication, authorization, synchronization rollback, permission
  union, last-Owner protection, secret handling and migrations require explicit
  tests regardless of aggregate percentage.

## Milestone 3 Test Design: UI-002 / AUTH-001 / PROJECT-001 / SYS-001 / PERM-001

- Auth session bootstrap: verify protected frontend routes call
  `/api/v1/auth/me` through the memory-only API client, render the synchronized
  display name, preserve access/refresh tokens out of persistent storage, and
  expose effective permissions and visible project IDs to route and component
  gates. Browser-side frontend requests should default to the same-origin
  `/api/backend` proxy, with the Next server forwarding to the configured
  internal Backend URL.
- Permission-aware navigation and actions: cover users with System view/edit,
  Project view/create/edit and no-permission combinations. Verify hidden nav
  entries, forbidden direct-route empty states, disabled mutation buttons with
  explanations, and no fixture data shown for forbidden live pages.
- API error behavior: simulate 401, 403, 409, 422 and safe 5xx envelopes. Verify
  401 performs at most one refresh/reauth path, 403 does not refresh, 409 keeps
  local state unsaved with reload guidance, validation errors map to fields, and
  token/credential/LDAP DN/API key values never appear in DOM or logs.
- Projects live integration: mock and integration-test `GET /projects`,
  `POST /projects`, `GET /users` and `GET /models`. Verify loading/empty/error
  states, model filtering for Chat/Embedding, active-user member candidates,
  creator Owner behavior reflected after backend success, list refresh, and
  route navigation with real project id/title while document lists remain
  explicitly fixture-labeled. Verify Create Project does not render any
  user-search, initial-Owner or role-management section, sends no create-modal
  members payload, and relies on backend creator-as-Owner enforcement; subsequent
  Owner/editor/viewer management is left to the project workspace Permission
  Management modal. Verify Create Project lays out the four create sections as
  top-left basic information, top-right OCR, bottom-left LLM, and bottom-right
  Embedding. Verify Create Project pairs LLM and Embedding models by
  explicit Chat `paired_embedding_model_ids` first and explicit model group
  config keys or provider fallback second, filters the Embedding list when an
  LLM is selected, auto-selects a compatible active Embedding model,
  and blocks create submission with a readable message when no compatible active
  Embedding model exists.
- System Management live integration: verify Users, Roles, Role Users,
  Permissions, External Group Role Mappings, AI/OCR Models, Identity Settings
  and System Parameters read from live APIs. Cover selected safe mutations for
  permission matrix, manual role users, mappings, system parameters and supported
  model operations with optimistic-lock and forbidden failures.
- Manual role user picker: verify the role-user modal provides a localized
  search input that filters active users by name, email, employee id or account
  identity; shows a useful no-results state; distinguishes already-manual
  members, pending additions, pending removals and retained external-sync
  members with text/badges rather than color alone; keeps a draft summary visible
  while search results change; renders retained external-sync and break-glass
  effective members as checked and read-only; and saves only the final manual
  `user_ids` with `lock_version`
  while preserving the backend external-sync relationship contract.
- Fixture/live boundary: assert every still-fixture area, including document
  import lists, Pipeline, Graph, Chat, approvals and reports, retains an explicit
  demonstration/data-preview label and never calls unimplemented production APIs.
- i18n/accessibility: ensure zh/en strings are aligned for loading, empty,
  error, forbidden, retry, disabled-action and fixture-boundary states; verify
  keyboard access and focus visibility for new controls.

## Feature Test Design: SYS-001

- Tab workspace: verify the six system-management Tabs expose the correct panel, support arrow-key/Home/End navigation and focus semantics, preserve independent draft state, and remain horizontally usable on narrow screens.
- Role permissions: switch among NomoSmart roles and verify each role retains an isolated View/Create/Edit/Delete matrix; verify external groups map to roles rather than holding permissions directly and effective multi-role permissions are the union.
- Identity source UI: verify Keycloak OIDC metadata, enabled state, discovery/JWKS validation state, last sync, manual sync and run history are presented with loading/success/error states. Secret values must never appear in DOM text, fixtures, responses or logs; only configured/missing or masked status is shown.
- Federation boundary: verify LDAP and AD appear only as Keycloak User Federation source/health/sync summaries. The UI and API must expose no LDAP/AD host, bind DN, bind password or domain credential editing controls.
- Authentication-setting lock: after first successful validation and activation, verify every Keycloak and LDAP/AD sync-management field is read-only and direct mutation APIs deny requests without a valid server-side unlock. Cover fresh Keycloak authentication, `auth_time`, current edit permission, user/session/scope binding, 10-minute expiry, save/cancel/lock/logout/navigation revocation, disabled users, permission removal and concurrent sessions.
- Candidate activation: verify unlocked edits remain candidates, validation runs before save, failed validation or persistence preserves the last-known-good configuration, successful atomic activation immediately relocks, stale/concurrent writes are rejected, and audit/error payloads contain no token, secret or LDAP/AD credential.
- LDAP/AD same-page sync management: verify source enablement, people/group scope, schedule/timezone, manual sync, health and history are managed beside Keycloak while connection host and bind/domain credentials remain absent from DOM, API contracts, fixtures and persistence.
- Break-glass lifecycle: verify initialization provisions a Keycloak-local emergency administrator from deployment Secret input, leaves it disabled by default, requires OIDC/MFA and the dedicated System Admin role, alerts/audits activation and use, supports post-use disable/credential rotation, and rejects missing, hard-coded, logged or shared default credentials.
- Failure safety and audit: reject activation of invalid OIDC candidates, preserve the last-known-good configuration, sanitize errors, and record actor/time/change summary/result for configuration, validation, sync, mapping and permission changes without secrets.
- System parameters: load the 100 MB upload default, `Asia/Taipei` timezone and configured staging TTL with unit/description/modified metadata; accept valid changes, reject invalid ranges/units/timezones atomically, preserve prior effective values on failure, restore defaults explicitly, audit old/new values and apply changes only to new work.
- Configuration boundary: verify database, Redis, S3, service URLs, encryption keys, credentials and secrets never appear as editable System Parameters fields or fixture values.

## Milestone 5 Test Design: System Management Completion

- Users: cover live search/filter, detail open/close, local field edit, manager
  delegate validation, knowledge-owner toggle, status enable/disable, permission
  denial, safe errors and audit-sensitive no-secret output.
- Roles: cover create/edit/deactivate, system-role protection, stale
  `lock_version`, manual user replacement, inactive-user rejection, preservation
  of `external_sync` memberships and dirty-state prompts.
- External group mappings: cover active group/role selection, duplicate
  rejection, atomic replacement, cancel/save behavior, conflict and forbidden
  states.
- Permission matrix: cover unsaved-change protection, save success, stale
  conflict, role switching, permission union assumptions and disabled controls
  without edit permission.
- AI models: cover create/edit, optional API-key reset, masked responses,
  config-version increment, set-default uniqueness, test status, non-OCR
  deactivate semantics, OCR unreferenced delete success, OCR referenced-delete
  denial and clear frontend messaging.
- Provider-specific AI models: cover OpenAI, Gemini, Claude / Anthropic,
  Ollama, vLLM and Custom / Generic HTTP field rendering, required-field
  validation, config JSON normalization, direct encrypted API-key entry, Secret
  Ref entry, Ollama/vLLM no-key acceptance, edit-without-new-key retention and
  rejection of plaintext secret-looking keys inside `config`.
- Chat/Embedding model pairing: cover Chat model create/edit active Embedding
  dropdown multi-select rendering with selected-count feedback, required
  non-empty selection for Chat submissions, `config.paired_embedding_model_ids`
  payload persistence, no pairing UI for non-Chat model types, and backend
  rejection of invalid, non-Embedding or inactive pairing references.
- Identity settings: cover reauth start/complete, server-side unlock countdown,
  expiry, explicit lock, validate, activate, last-known-good preservation,
  candidate errors, no LDAP/AD credential fields, manual sync queue and sync-run
  history/detail.
- Break-glass: cover read-only status/runbook display, disabled-by-default
  messaging, no enable/disable/password controls and no credential leakage.
- System parameters: cover restore-default staging, explicit save, validation,
  conflict/error messaging and applied-value display.
- Cross-cutting frontend checks: zh/en i18n, loading/empty/forbidden/conflict
  states, keyboard/modal accessibility, responsive dense layout, lint and build.
- Authorization and i18n: deny read/write operations without the declared System Management permissions, keep view/create/edit/delete independent, and provide matching Traditional Chinese and English strings for every new label and state.

## Feature Test Design: PROMPT-001

- Backend schema/API: verify `system_prompts` and `system_prompt_versions`
  enforce UUID keys, scope/model/type constraints, one current effective version
  per prompt scope, optimistic locking, disabled-history retention and 8000
  Unicode-character validation.
- Authorization: verify `System.AIModelSettings.can_view` gates prompt reads and
  `can_edit` gates create, update, activate and deactivate. Unauthorized users
  must receive 403 without prompt content leakage.
- Versioning/audit: verify create, content update, activate, deactivate and
  effective-version switch preserve previous versions and write audit metadata
  without prompt full text, API keys, tokens or provider secrets. Deactivate
  must also mark prompt-version rows inactive so API history does not show a
  disabled prompt with an enabled current version.
- Frontend UI: verify `/system` exposes System Prompt management beside AI
  Models, shows fixed global Chat and global Judge editing sections above a
  separate model-specific Chat/Judge prompt section, lets users enter each
  global editor directly by clicking its global box, does not show separate
  global-add buttons, uses clear scope/model badges and priority/layering
  guidance at page level, opens a popup modal for prompt content editing without
  a version note/change reason input, editor-level layer-order block or duplicate
  body scope/name header, places scope/type/status badges in the popup title row,
  avoids a duplicate editing-summary subtitle in the modal header,
  keeps the main page to summary/list states, follows
  the shared System Management modal header/body/footer layout, shows active
  state, version history, character counter, loading, empty, error and forbidden
  states, supports clicking an old version to load its content into the textarea
  as a new-version draft without editing history, supports close/Escape/backdrop
  behavior, renders the modal header as one horizontal line with right-aligned
  scope/type/status badges and no eyebrow subtitle, uses pointer cursor feedback
  for clickable model-specific prompt rows, and blocks over-8000-character or
  blank / whitespace-only saves.
- Runtime layering: verify Chat layers backend safety default, then enabled
  model Chat prompt, then enabled global Chat prompt; Judge layers backend
  safety default, then enabled model Judge prompt, then enabled global Judge
  prompt. Blank inactive placeholders are ignored by runtime; blank or
  whitespace-only versions cannot be activated or layered.
- Execution evidence: verify chat records and validation run items persist
  ordered prompt source, prompt version id and content hash metadata without
  writing prompt full text to audit or metrics labels.
- Live-only policy: runtime provider verification must use real configured
  Chat/Judge execution paths or report blocked/unavailable when providers or
  credentials are absent; mocks, stubs, deterministic answers and fixture
  provider success do not satisfy acceptance.

## Milestone 6 Test Design: Live Knowledge Extraction Pipeline and Document Version Lifecycle

- Pipeline run/state: verify a single uploaded file creates exactly one
  document-version pipeline, a multi-file manual extraction creates exactly one
  pipeline for the selected document, duplicate starts return conflict without
  partial records, and every run belongs to one project/document/version.
- Step progress: verify canonical steps through parse, OCR, split, chunk,
  Markdown, rule-based tag, embedding placeholder, staging index, graph preview
  and submission preparation report status, percent, timestamps, retry_count and
  sanitized error fields. Later approval/publish/production steps must remain
  modeled but unexecuted in Milestone 6.
- Adapter contracts: verify parser/OCR/chunk/Markdown/tag/embedding/
  graph-preview artifacts through real configured implementations or real
  development/test services with production-compatible schemas. Existing
  deterministic development adapters are historical only and must not be used
  as passing test paths.
- OCR behavior: verify snapshot immutability, reliable-text-layer skip,
  force-OCR execution, inactive/missing OCR rejection and fail-closed behavior
  when the OCR adapter fails.
- Rule-based tags: verify tags can be derived from file name, title, keywords,
  file/source type and chunk metadata; each tag keeps rule/source traceability
  and can be displayed for review.
- Manual chunking: verify text selection in Original and Markdown views shows a
  floating Manual Chunk button only when `manual_edit_enabled` and edit
  permission are true; backend manual chunk creation replaces fully overlapping
  chunks, splits partially overlapping chunks, preserves source offsets and
  lineage, recalculates chunk indexes by source order, rejects blank/unlocatable
  selections and stale versions, and audits the mutation.
- Chunk/document tagging: verify chunk tags and document-version tags support
  LLM auto-tagging through the project's configured Chat LLM with System Prompt
  layering, direct persistence with `source = llm`, manual add with
  `source = manual`, delete for llm/manual tags, source/created metadata,
  permission denial, provider unavailable errors, and no deterministic fake tags
  as passing behavior. Verify document tags and chunk tags reuse the same
  project-scoped canonical `tag_id` for equal normalized tag text, remain
  isolated across projects, and expose document-tag-to-related-chunk summaries
  by `tag_id` for API responses, graph preview, review summary and query
  filtering.
- Pipeline Chat LLM auto-tagging (`TAG-002`): verify every formal extraction
  source runs document-version and chunk-level Chat LLM tagging after
  Markdown/chunk generation and before embedding/staging. Verify canonical tag
  reuse, `source = llm`, model/prompt metadata, request id, retryable `tagging`
  step failure on model/config/provider/tag-write errors, and no rule-based,
  deterministic or fake tag fallback as formal success. Verify chunk-level
  tagging calls are based on each chunk's own content, document-level tags are
  not copied to every chunk, and a valid empty array for a low-signal chunk is
  accepted without adding tags or failing the whole Pipeline. Frontend coverage must
  verify the resulting chunk tags and source are directly visible exactly once
  in the bottom row of Knowledge Detail Chunk cards, `rule` tags are not shown
  as current auto-tagging output, document-level tags are visible in the
  document article area, Chunk content is visually separated from metadata/tag
  rows, and Chunk source/token/confidence metadata sits beside the top-left
  index badge as small gray text. Upload processing progress and Pipeline step
  detail UI must label `auto_tag` as AI auto tagging.
- OpenSearch staging: verify the staging adapter writes to Development
  OpenSearch when available, records index/document references in PostgreSQL,
  and never writes to production index names or aliases. When OpenSearch is
  unavailable in a deterministic test environment, verify a clear adapter error
  or skipped integration result without marking production success.
- Retry and recovery: verify failed steps can be retried up to three times,
  valid upstream artifacts are preserved, downstream artifacts are invalidated
  when an upstream output changes, retry attempts are audited, and the fourth
  attempt is denied with a clear failed state.
- Version lifecycle: verify same-source re-extraction allocates the next
  extraction revision, source-content update allocates the next major version
  where supported by the file-upload contract, prior Active versions remain
  effective, and Active/Working summaries are returned consistently.
- Frontend: verify document cards and knowledge-extraction views render
  ready-for-extraction without fake ETA, running pipeline progress, expanded
  step details, failed retry states, retry-limit disabled state,
  submission-ready staging output, OCR snapshot display and Active/Working
  version labels.
- Security and authorization: verify project view/edit/extraction permissions,
  sanitized errors/logs/audit, no model secrets or document-sensitive content in
  logs, no production index/graph writes, and no data-service synchronization
  endpoints are invoked by Milestone 6 flows.

## Login Fixture Test Design: AUTH-005

- Account step: verify labeled account and password fields, required validation, password show/hide control, Enter-key submission, visible focus and a clear non-production fixture notice.
- OTP step: valid account/password input advances to a labeled six-digit numeric OTP field; invalid length or characters show text plus icon feedback; Back returns to the first step and Verify reaches only an explicit demonstration-complete state.
- Fixture completion: after a valid OTP, verify credential state is cleared immediately, a demonstration-success status is announced, exactly one client-side navigation to `/` occurs after about 0.8 seconds, no early navigation occurs, and unmount cancels the pending redirect.
- Security boundary: spy on fetch and browser storage to prove the fixture sends no authentication request, writes no account/password/OTP to localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, URL or logs, and creates no token or authenticated application session. The allowed `/` navigation must not add auth state.
- Accessibility and responsive behavior: verify semantic headings, labels, error association, status announcement, keyboard-only operation, password-toggle accessible name, minimum 40px mobile targets and no clipping at narrow widths.
- i18n and regression: verify matching Traditional Chinese and English copy for both steps and states; retain the production statement that credentials and OTP are handled only by Keycloak and do not add an identity-header fallback.

## Feature Test Design: IMPORT-001 / IMPORT-002 / DSYNC-001 / CONFIG-002

- Unit: validate `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.txt`, `.md`, and `.markdown`; reject legacy `.doc` for every new-ingestion/update path, extension/content/OOXML-package mismatches, unsupported formats, empty/corrupt inputs, and files over the configured limit. Verify authorized read/download continuity for existing `.doc`, the 100 MB default, valid overrides, invalid units/ranges, and backend-authoritative enforcement.
- Backend API: prove a single upload atomically creates `v1.0` and dispatches exactly one extraction Pipeline; prove multi-file upload returns ordered per-item success/failure results, creates no automatic Pipelines, preserves successful siblings, and creates exactly one Pipeline after an authorized manual extraction action.
- Backend Pipeline handoff: verify initialized Pipeline steps are flushed before
  extraction queries when SQLAlchemy runs with `autoflush=False`, so single-file
  auto-extraction and manual extraction cannot fail with missing canonical steps.
- Concurrency and recovery: cover upload idempotency, duplicate manual extraction, sync locks, worker-dispatch failure, transaction rollback, source fingerprints, unchanged syncs, next-major version allocation, working-version conflicts, retry, and preservation of the prior Active version.
- Data-service protocol adapters: use disposable real FTP, explicit FTPS, SFTP/
  SSH and S3-compatible services. Cover authentication, TLS/host-key failures,
  missing remote file, timeout, unsupported content, size overflow and
  sanitized errors without production credentials or production data.
- Sync lifecycle: confirm the document list item exists before the initial background fetch completes and transitions through waiting, syncing, failed or ready-for-extraction. Verify initial, scheduled, and manual triggers create separate sync-run records; manual sync works for both one-time and recurring sources without changing the schedule.
- Cron: validate friendly controls and advanced standard five-field expressions, explicit IANA timezone with `Asia/Taipei` default, human-readable preview, next-run calculation, invalid expression/timezone rejection, and daylight-saving behavior for timezones that observe DST.
- Security and authorization: verify project import/edit permission boundaries, encrypted credentials or secret references, masked responses, sanitized logs/audits, no private key/password/S3 secret exposure, host-key/TLS verification behavior, and denied sync/extraction actions.
- Frontend component: cover single/multi upload branching, file constraints, progress and per-item summaries, waiting-for-extraction cards without fake Pipeline metrics, service wizard protocol-specific fields, Cron basic/advanced UI, loading/error/retry states, Version Management "Sync now", keyboard/focus behavior, mobile layout, and matching `zh`/`en` strings.
- Integration/E2E: upload one file and enter extraction; upload a mixed-validity
  batch and manually start one successful item; create each service type against
  a disposable real service, observe initial sync, change source contents,
  manually/scheduled-sync to the next major version, then manually start
  extraction while the prior Active version remains effective.
- Deployment/configuration: verify the global size limit is documented and consistently wired through safe example environment configuration, Docker Compose, Helm ConfigMap/values, frontend discovery, and backend validation without committing secrets.

## Feature Test Design: APISRC-001 / Milestone 14 File/API Data Sources

- Remote file adapters:
  - Verify SFTP over SSH fetches exactly one configured file with password and
    private-key credential paths, enforces known-host / host-key verification,
    handles missing file, auth failure, timeout and size/content validation, and
    never executes arbitrary SSH commands.
  - Verify FTP and FTPS fetch exactly one configured file, enforce explicit TLS
    mode for FTPS, handle TLS verification failures, auth failures, missing
    file, timeout, unsupported content and size overflow.
  - Verify S3/RustFS regression remains compatible with existing sync worker
    success, unchanged, changed/new-version and safe-failure behavior.

- HTTP/API document source:
  - Verify HTTP GET only; POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, pagination, workflow chaining,
    cookie-session login, OAuth authorization-code flow and arbitrary API
    orchestration are rejected or not represented by the contract.
  - Verify auth modes none, Bearer token and API key header use encrypted
    credentials or secret references and never return plaintext credentials in
    API responses, preview output, audit, logs or frontend review summaries.
  - Verify safe test fetch preview returns HTTP status, content type, content
    length, inferred filename, size-limit status and truncated non-sensitive
    preview only.
  - Verify SSRF protections block disallowed schemes, loopback, link-local,
    private-network and cloud metadata endpoint targets unless an explicit
    deployment allowlist says otherwise.
  - Verify supported PDF/Office/text/Markdown/CSV/JSON responses create source
    snapshots and document versions; JSON is stored as raw snapshot or
    equivalent text artifact without mapping, join, aggregation or ETL behavior.
  - Verify unsupported content type, timeout, TLS failure, HTTP failure and size
    overflow create safe failed sync runs without partial document versions.

- UI and lifecycle:
  - Verify Data Service Wizard presents Remote File and HTTP/API categories,
    hides SSH command execution, requires successful connection/test fetch,
    invalidates success on field changes and keeps secrets out of review.
  - Verify manual sync, scheduled sync, sync history, unchanged detection,
    changed-content version creation and waiting-for-manual-extraction behavior
    are identical across S3, SFTP, FTP, FTPS and HTTP/API sources.

## UI/UX Test Design: IMPORT-003 / DSYNC-002

- Upload Modal: verify the drop zone is the primary action, constraints and single/multi consequences are visible before submit, file rows show filename/readable size/format/text+icon status, long names truncate safely, long lists scroll independently, and mixed results remain visible with success/failure counts.
- Upload actions: verify sticky footer visibility at desktop/mobile sizes, correct cancel/upload/complete labels, duplicate-submit disabling, explicit discard handling after selection/input, Escape/close behavior, initial focus, keyboard activation, and visible focus rings.
- Data-service stepper: verify exactly three named steps, current/completed state, previous/next navigation, no skipping invalid steps, preservation of entered values when navigating back, and protocol changes invalidating prior connection-test success.
- Connection step: verify FTP/FTPS/SFTP/SSH/S3 display only relevant fields and connection test transitions through idle/testing/success/failure with non-color-only messaging; secret fields never appear in later review text.
- File/schedule step: verify one-file validation, one-time and recurring modes, friendly minute/hour/day/week controls, expandable advanced five-field Cron, timezone, readable description, next run and invalid-state gating.
- Review/create step: verify the summary includes only non-sensitive connection/source/schedule data and explicitly explains immediate list creation, background initial sync and later manual extraction; duplicate create is disabled.
- Responsive/accessibility: verify bounded desktop modal, near-full-height single-column mobile modal, internal body scrolling, always-visible footer, no keyboard/content overlap, semantic labels, focus movement and non-color-only states.

## UI Refinement Test Design: IMPORT-004 / DSYNC-003

- Clear All: verify the action appears only for unsubmitted selections, uses a lucide Trash icon plus accessible text, has a minimum 40px target and secondary-danger normal/hover/focus/disabled styles, aligns with file heading/statistics, and immediately clears files and validation without confirmation or document-side effects.
- Stepper reference state: enter step two and verify step one uses a check plus completed styling, step two uses a solid green numbered circle plus current-step semantics, step three uses a gray outlined numbered circle, and connectors distinguish completed from upcoming segments.
- Stepper content: verify every item shows `步驟 N` and its name, `aria-current` follows navigation, and the right summary pill contains only service protocol and port with no host, username or credential.
- Responsive: verify desktop alignment matches the supplied horizontal reference, while narrow widths preserve order, readable names and state markers with shortened connectors and a wrapped protocol pill without overlap or clipping.

## Project Drop-zone Test Design: IMPORT-005

- Drag lifecycle: verify drag enter/over prevents default navigation, adds a stable highlight through child-boundary movement, and drag leave/drop clears it without flicker.
- Handoff: drop one valid file, multiple mixed-validity files and unsupported files; verify the upload Modal opens once with every dropped file in original order and applies existing metadata/validation UI without silent filtering.
- Entry parity: verify zone whitespace click, Enter and Space open an empty upload Modal and the explicit Select Files button remains equivalent.
- Isolation: verify Data Service and Reference Other Project buttons stop propagation and open only their respective Modal; dropping on the zone never triggers those button actions.
- Workflow regression: verify single valid dropped file retains auto-extraction after submit, multiple files retain per-item/manual-extraction behavior, and cancel/discard creates no document state.

## Report and CSV Export Test Design: REPORT-001 / REPORT-003 / REPORT-004 / REPORT-005 / REPORT-008

- Authorization and data scope: verify users need Report `can_view` for the selected topic and that returned rows are additionally scoped by system role, project membership, Project Owner relationship, reviewer/manager relationship or current-user-only ownership. Direct API calls for unauthorized topics, projects, users or date ranges must return safe denial without leaking counts or names.
- Topic and filter validation: verify `system_overview`, `project_ranking`, `project_reference_ranking`, `document_reference_ranking`, `owner_project_summary`, `document_pipeline_metrics`, `rag_quality_metrics`, `validation_run_metrics`, `model_usage_metrics` and `alert_metrics` accept supported date ranges, project filters and scope values; invalid topic, inverted dates, unsupported scope and unauthorized project IDs are rejected.
- Project rankings: verify project activity rankings aggregate document counts, active documents, pipeline execution, Q&A, validation, active users, success/failure rates and date-window deltas consistently with source tables and exclude unauthorized projects.
- Reference rankings: verify source-project and source-document leaderboards count references, distinct target projects, referenced documents, recent new references, source-update pending items, Q&A hits and quality metrics; users without source visibility receive only authorized safe summaries.
- Project Owner dashboard: verify the default Owner scope includes all and only projects where the user is an Owner, supports authorized single/multiple project filtering, and includes documents, versions, governance, references, quality, model usage summary and alerts.
- CSV format: verify every report download is one topic per file, encoded as UTF-8 with BOM, RFC 4180 escaped, uses header titles localized to the current website language, preserves stable internal field-key mapping and column order, uses ISO 8601 timestamps and keeps numeric cells unit-free.
- CSV safety: verify CSV exports never include plaintext secrets, tokens, internal stack traces, unauthorized document content, unauthorized project/document names, or other users' personal behavior details outside the requester's allowed scope.
- Filename and audit: verify filenames follow `nomosmart_<topic>_<date_from>_<date_to>.csv`; every download records audit metadata for downloader, topic, date range, project scope, row count, generated timestamp and request ID without storing full CSV content.
- Large export path: verify v1 uses bounded keyset/server-cursor streaming for
  datasets beyond the former threshold, never creates a background artifact/job
  or Notification completion path, cancels the query on disconnect and treats
  an incomplete transport as failure. A future background mode requires its own
  approved companion contract.

## Approval Detail Test Design: REVIEW-005

- Routing and identity: select every pending row and verify `/approve/[approvalTaskId]` renders that task's project, document, version, stage, submitter, manager and owners; an unknown task ID shows a clear not-found state and no decision controls.
- Submission-page parity: verify Document/Version and Extraction/Chunks form the desktop pair, Graph Summary and Chat Test Records are full-width, and narrow screens stack all four in source order without horizontal overflow.
- Approval evidence: verify submission reason, pipeline result, source Original/Markdown snapshot, chunk results, tags, staging graph preview, CSV batch validation result and chronological append-only review history are present and distinguish missing/not-evaluated states with text or icons.
- Conversation evidence: verify complete conversation groups start collapsed, support independent simultaneous expansion with `aria-expanded`, show chronological turns/citations/evaluations/suggestions, and export every task-attached turn with UTF-8 BOM, escaping and task/version-identifiable filename regardless of accordion state.
- Decision controls: verify manager and Owner pending tasks show only stage-valid Approve/Reject actions; approval comment is optional, rejection reason is required, cancel/close changes nothing, duplicate submission is disabled, and completed/unauthorized tasks are read-only. Publish appears only for an approved version and authorized publishing context.
- Regression: verify the pre-submission page keeps its existing summary, conversation export, governance flow and Submit action, while `/approve` rows continue linking to their own task IDs.

## Knowledge Graph Node Style Test Design: GRAPH-UI-001 / GRAPH-006

- Shared renderer: verify `DocumentGraphPreview` and `ProjectGraphPreview` both use the shared professional node renderer while preserving accessible button nodes, zoom, pan, node drag, reset, selection and first-degree highlight hooks.
- Type identity: verify Project uses a circular project-icon node, Document uses a compact document-icon node with small radius and pale non-white fold, Chunk uses a capsule with content-type icon support, and Tag uses a diamond with tag icon.
- Label hierarchy: verify readable names remain the primary labels and UUIDs or other technical IDs appear only as gray secondary metadata, never as the main node title.
- Visual regression: verify graph edges, selected halo, dimmed state and label backgrounds remain low-noise; obsolete heavy card-like node styling, decorative orbit rings and oversized document nodes must not return.
- Behavior boundary: verify CHG-171 is a frontend presentation change only; API payloads, Neo4j sync, project/document authorization, active-version filtering and graph relationship contracts remain covered by the existing graph tests.

## Dense Knowledge Graph Progressive Disclosure Test Design: GRAPH-UI-002

- Detail levels: verify zoom maps to structure, focus and detail levels; default zoom does not render every Chunk/Tag label or technical ID, focus reveals selected/hovered paths, and detail zoom still avoids all-label overlap in dense graphs.
- Dense grouping: verify dense document and project graphs build a frontend-only display graph that groups Chunk/Tag nodes into count/range summaries at structure zoom and preserves original source IDs for relationship collapse and later reveal.
- Project layout: verify Project Graph no longer places all live nodes on a single radial ring, adds or preserves a Project core node, places Document/DocumentVersion/Chunk/Tag nodes into readable layers, and does not classify `DocumentVersion` as a Tag visual node.
- Interaction parity: verify grouped and source nodes remain accessible buttons, keep zoom, pan, node drag, reset, hover reveal, selection, dimming and first-degree edge highlighting.
- Regression: verify labels are hidden by default with explicit label-mode hooks, group count badges are visible, technical IDs only appear in full label mode, and the crowded outer label ring/card stack failure mode cannot return.

## Clear Knowledge Graph Workspace Redesign Test Design: GRAPH-UI-003

- Shared graph workspace: verify `DocumentGraphPreview` and `ProjectGraphPreview` use the same clear graph workspace structure, toolbar, legend, zoom controls, selected path highlighting and detail panel behavior.
- Node identity: verify Project, Document/DocumentVersion, Chunk and Tag nodes use visibly different shapes and lucide icons, not color alone; obsolete heavy card-like nodes, decorative orbit rings, purple gradients and low-contrast ghost nodes must not return.
- Zoom information layers: verify zoom out shows high-level Project/Document/group summaries, medium zoom reveals key chunks/tags and selected paths, and zoom in reveals full labels, technical metadata and source trace details.
- Dense grouping: verify large chunk/tag sets use explicit `+N chunks` / `+N tags` or equivalent grouped nodes that are visually different from real data nodes and communicate that zoom/selection can reveal more.
- Edge styling and selection: verify edges are low-noise, can express relationship categories through line style or endpoint markers, support selection, and show source/target/type metadata in the detail panel without inventing unavailable backend fields.
- Detail panel: verify selecting a node or edge opens a right-side or bottom detail panel with type, readable title, technical id, metadata, direct neighbors and relationship details while keeping the graph canvas uncluttered.
- Accessibility and i18n: verify graph controls have accessible labels, clickable nodes/edges have visible hover/focus states, state is not color-only, and Traditional Chinese / English labels are aligned.
- Boundary: verify `GRAPH-UI-003` remains a frontend presentation/interaction change; no Neo4j model, authorization, graph sync or backend API contract is changed unless a later approved spec adds it.

## Full Graph Explorer Frontend Rewrite Test Design: GRAPH-UI-004

- Rewrite boundary: verify document and project graph previews no longer depend on the old patch-style graph renderer constraints, including `ProfessionalGraphNode`, old `graphDisplay` grouping assumptions, grid-heavy canvas styling, radial-only document layout or left-to-right project pipeline layout.
- Shared Graph Explorer: verify both document and project graph surfaces use the same shell model: top toolbar, clean relationship canvas, persistent Inspector, live loading/empty/forbidden/error states and no fixture/demo graph fallback.
- Project overview: verify project-level graph defaults to a document-oriented overview with project scope, document/version cards or groups and visible Chunk/Tag count summaries instead of expanding every Chunk/Tag immediately.
- Project focus: verify selecting a document switches focus to that document's first-level Chunk/Tag relationships and selecting a Chunk/Tag highlights only directly connected entities and paths.
- Document focus: verify document-level graph uses document/version as the subject and renders Chunk relationships in article order or readable groups; Tag nodes/chips connect to the appropriate document/chunk relationships without forcing a radial outer ring.
- Node identity: verify Project, Document/DocumentVersion, Chunk and Tag visuals use distinct structure, icon and text, not color alone; Project cannot become an oversized decorative sphere.
- Edge clarity: verify paths are low-noise, selectable, keyboard reachable where rendered as controls, and show relationship type/direction in the Inspector without permanent edge labels cluttering the canvas.
- Inspector: verify node and edge selection populate type, readable label, technical id, direct neighbors, relationship details and available metadata; missing API fields must render as absent/empty rather than fabricated values.
- Interaction: verify zoom buttons, wheel zoom isolation, bounded pan, reset, node selection, optional local node dragging, keyboard Enter/Space selection, visible focus states, cursor pointers and reduced-motion-friendly transitions.
- Responsive and i18n: verify desktop uses right-side Inspector, narrow view stacks Inspector below the canvas, and Traditional Chinese / English strings remain aligned with no hard-coded visible Chinese in React components.
- Boundary: verify `GRAPH-UI-004` remains a frontend presentation/interaction rewrite; graph API payloads, Neo4j model, graph sync, authorization, retrieval scope and review/publish behavior are unchanged.

## Circular Umbrella Knowledge Graph Refinement Test Design: GRAPH-UI-005

- Layout: verify document and project graph previews use the shared circular umbrella radial layout helper, with Project or Document as the central anchor, related documents/chunks arranged on readable arcs, tags placed on the outer or adjacent layer, and no left-to-right pipeline layout regression.
- Selected node styles: verify Project uses the folder node variant, Document uses the top-bar card variant, Chunk uses the small note variant, and Tag uses the gold strip variant. Type identity must rely on shape, icon and structure in addition to color.
- Relationship labels: verify Project-to-Document labels map only to upload, FTP, SFTP, FTPS, SSH, S3, HTTP API or referenced-project sources; Document-to-Chunk uses the chunking label; Document/Chunk-to-Tag uses the tagging label.
- Canvas scope: verify only Project, Document/DocumentVersion, Chunk, Tag and their relationships render in the graph canvas; source systems remain relationship labels and AI models, conversations, approvals, users, Pipeline steps and tests do not appear as nodes.
- Detail behavior: verify relationship labels stay lightweight on the canvas while the Inspector still shows selected node/edge details, available metadata, source and target without fabricating missing fields.
- Interaction and density: verify zoom, wheel zoom, bounded pan, reset, node/edge selection, keyboard selection and local node dragging remain intact; dense chunk/tag sets avoid overlap through spacing or lower-zoom grouping.
- Boundary: verify `GRAPH-UI-005` is a frontend presentation refinement only and does not change graph API payloads, Neo4j model, graph sync, authorization, retrieval scope or review/publish behavior.

## Center-Radial Semantic Zoom Graph Rewrite Test Design: GRAPH-UI-006

- Layout engine: verify the project graph uses a deterministic center-radial layout model where Project is layer 1 at the visual center, Documents are layer 2, Chunks are layer 3 and Tags are layer 4. Verify document graph uses the same layer vocabulary with the scoped document as the center-equivalent subject.
- Semantic zoom thresholds: verify 100% shows Project and Document as the clear primary layers while Chunk/Tag are present only as low-information hints; 150% reveals Chunk nodes/relationships as readable elements; 200% reveals Tag nodes/relationships as readable elements; 300% preserves at least two adjacent layers in view instead of scaling one object to fill the canvas.
- Non-scale-only behavior: verify zoom changes information density, node size caps, text density and label availability rather than relying only on a full-scene CSS scale. Nodes must define minimum/maximum dimensions and relation labels must remain hidden or Inspector-driven until hover/focus/selection.
- Lower-layer hint quality: verify 100% Chunk/Tag hints do not become unreadable transparent ghost-node piles, overlapping cards or fake data. Hints may be abstract marks, density/count hints or subdued silhouettes without labels.
- Edge clarity: verify every rendered relationship line connects exactly two visible or intentionally hinted endpoints, does not pass through node text, and does not keep permanent floating labels on the canvas. Hover/focus/selection or Inspector must expose relationship type and direction.
- Visual polish: verify the selected Project folder, Document top-bar card, Chunk note and Tag gold strip styles remain consistent with NomoSmart colors, use Lucide icons, maintain contrast and avoid decorative gradients/orbs/heavy shadows.
- Interaction and accessibility: verify zoom buttons, wheel zoom isolation, bounded pan, reset, node/edge selection, keyboard Enter/Space selection, visible focus states, cursor pointer/grab states, reduced-motion behavior and responsive Inspector placement still work.
- Boundary: verify `GRAPH-UI-006` is a frontend presentation/interaction rewrite only and does not change graph API payloads, Neo4j model, graph sync, authorization, retrieval scope, review/publish behavior or live-only data boundaries.

## Milestone 7 Test Design: REVIEW-001 / REVIEW-002 / SEARCH-001 / VERSION-001 / GRAPH-002

- Live service requirement: Milestone 7 integration verification must use the
  prepared Development PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, Neo4j, S3, Keycloak/OIDC and
  worker/Redis services. Deterministic stubs may support unit tests but cannot
  satisfy the milestone acceptance checks for publish, published retrieval or
  formal graph sync.
- Harness command: run `./HARNESS/harness.sh integration:milestone7-live` for
  the live PostgreSQL/OpenSearch/Neo4j acceptance smoke. The command must fail
  when services or credentials are unavailable rather than falling back to stub
  adapters.
- Submit review: verify only `submission_ready` versions with ready staging
  artifacts can submit; duplicate submission, stale version, missing permission
  and missing staging index are rejected without partial `approval_requests`,
  `approval_tasks`, notifications or status changes.
- Manager review: verify assignment to the submitter's active manager or valid
  delegate, manager approval moves to Owner review, manager rejection requires a
  reason, administrators cannot substitute-sign, disabled/unauthorized users are
  denied, and every decision writes append-only `review_records` and audit rows.
- Owner review: verify the Owner stage is a group task, any valid Owner can
  approve/reject, `lock_version` prevents double completion, rejection requires a
  reason, approval moves the version to `approved` plus publish waiting action,
  and completed tasks become read-only.
- Review extraction lock: verify versions in `pending_manager_review`,
  `pending_owner_review` or `approved` waiting-publish reject all extraction,
  re-extraction, manual chunk, tag mutation, auto-tagging, staging-index rebuild
  and graph-preview rebuild mutation attempts from both UI and direct API calls,
  while authorized read-only evidence remains visible. Uploading a new source
  version must create an independent extractable version, and extracting from a
  `review_rejected` version must create a new revision without overwriting the
  rejected evidence.
- Publish: verify only an authorized Project Owner can publish an `approved` version.
  Publish must be idempotent, use prepare/verify/activate, write to the real
  OpenSearch published index, validate chunk count/checksum/dimension/mapping,
  transactionally update Active Version Manifest, supersede the prior active
  version and delete the corresponding staging OpenSearch documents.
- Formal graph sync: verify successful publish creates and executes live Neo4j
  `graph_sync`, writes project/document/version/chunk/tag relationships for the
  active version, excludes approved-unpublished and rejected versions, records
  graph job status and supports safe retry on transient failures.
- Old-version switch: verify only previously published, compatible and index-ready
  versions can be reactivated without re-review; incompatible profile/dimension/
  mapping versions require a new embedding build/revision and cannot be switched
  directly. Switches require impact confirmation, idempotency, optimistic lock
  and audit.
- Retrieval readiness: verify formal RAG/retrieval first resolves Active Version
  Manifest, filters by authorized project and exact `document_version_id`, fails
  closed on missing/stale manifest or missing index readiness, and never queries
  staging or all published vectors as fallback.
- Document Chat Test staging retrieval: verify the document-level Chat Test sends
  `scope_mode=document_staging`, rejects missing or cross-project version scopes,
  retrieves only live PostgreSQL chunks for the requested current document
  version, returns real citation excerpts, and does not require an Active Version
  Manifest. Formal Project Chat must continue to require active manifests and
  published retrieval.
- Chat scope migration/backfill readiness: verify environments using scoped chat
  history have applied the `chat_records.scope_mode` migration before reload
  acceptance; missing schema must be reported as migration incomplete rather than
  accepted as empty history. Verify existing `scope_mode IS NULL` records remain
  hidden by default, and that any operator-approved backfill is idempotent,
  bounded by explicit project/version/user/conversation criteria, reports
  candidate and updated row counts, and restores only matching
  `document_staging` records for the exact `document_version_id`.
- Frontend live behavior: verify `/approve`, `/approve/[approvalTaskId]`,
  submit-review and project document/version controls use live APIs for pending,
  history, approve/reject, publish and active-switch states with Traditional
  Chinese/English text, loading, forbidden, conflict and validation errors.

## Milestone 7.1 Test Design: REVIEW-011 / VERSION-002 / DOC-006 / GRAPH-005 / RAG-006

- Old-version switch: verify a dedicated switch endpoint/UI exists separately
  from publish; only previously published compatible versions with ready
  published index data can switch; incompatible profile, dimension or mapping
  versions fail closed. Require impact confirmation, audit reason, permission,
  project Owner or authorized publisher relationship, optimistic lock and
  idempotency.
- Lifecycle backend: verify active, inactive, superseded inactive, approved
  waiting publish, review rejected and soft delete state guards. Approved
  unpublished, staging, processing and rejected versions must not become formal
  active serving data through UI-only state changes.
- Lifecycle frontend: verify Project Import inactive/delete confirmation calls
  live lifecycle impact/update APIs with `lock_version`, handles API errors
  without committing local state, and exposes soft delete for documents waiting
  for manual extraction or sync where the status dropdown is not rendered.
- Project Graph live API: verify it reads from Neo4j live graph data, filters by
  project and authorization, returns only active published versions and excludes
  approved-unpublished, staging, processing, rejected, inactive, deleted and
  unauthorized nodes/edges.
- Project Chat formal retrieval: verify Project Chat resolves Active Version
  Manifest before querying OpenSearch, filters by exact `document_version_id`,
  uses published index data only, rejects unauthorized/unselected scope and fails
  closed on missing manifest or readiness instead of querying staging or all
  published vectors.
- Approval evidence hydration: verify approval detail document/version metadata,
  chunks, graph preview, chat/CSV evidence and review history load from live task
  evidence APIs. Completed, stale and unauthorized tasks must render read-only
  with clear status.
- Pipeline and notifications: verify publish-stage Pipeline UI states and M7
  notification subset for submit-review, manager pending, Owner pending,
  rejected, approved waiting publish, published and active switched events,
  including read/unread and action links.

## Milestone 8A Test Design: RAG-007 / SEARCH-001

- Manifest and scope validation: verify Project Chat resolves the user's
  project scope and Active Version Manifest before retrieval, accepts only
  selected document-version ids that are a subset of ready active manifests, and
  rejects empty, unauthorized, inactive, staging, approved-unpublished or
  cross-project versions with fail-closed errors.
- OpenSearch published-only retrieval: verify the retrieval adapter queries only
  published index names derived from each active version's Embedding Profile,
  includes exact `project_id` and `document_version_id` filters, never queries
  staging indices and never broadens to all published vectors after missing
  manifests or no hits.
- Request and failure behavior: verify `top_k` bounds, missing manifest,
  index-not-ready, OpenSearch unavailable, malformed payload and inconsistent
  chunk metadata return stable error/no-answer states without fabricated
  answers or citations.
- Citation payload: verify every returned citation is backed by a known live
  chunk and includes document id, document version id, chunk id, readable title,
  score and safe excerpt, plus page/content/source metadata when available.
- Retrieval strategy boundary: verify Milestone 8A can report keyword retrieval
  as the active strategy and does not label results as vector or hybrid unless
  the query embedding / hybrid adapter actually executed.
- Frontend live states: verify Project Chat uses the live query API, shows
  loading, empty, no-answer, forbidden, index-not-ready, OpenSearch unavailable
  and generic error states, and renders citations from the backend payload rather
  than fixture citations.
- Live Development acceptance: seed or reuse controlled Development PostgreSQL
  active manifests and OpenSearch published chunks, then run a focused retrieval
  check against the real services. If those services are unavailable, the check
  must fail or be reported as blocked rather than falling back to stubs.

## Hybrid Retrieval Test Design: RAG-010 / SEARCH-002

- Scope routing: verify document-level Chat Test, Project Chat and CSV
  validation worker all request `hybrid` retrieval by default. Document-level
  tests must query OpenSearch `staging` with exact project/document-version
  filters, while formal Project Chat must query OpenSearch `published` after
  resolving Active Version Manifest scope.
- Query embedding: verify the backend generates query embeddings through the
  configured Embedding Provider, uses encrypted credentials safely, applies TLS
  and timeout settings, records latency/failure metadata, and never hard-codes
  provider secrets or model names.
- OpenSearch vector readiness: verify staging and published writers create or
  verify vector-capable mappings and persist `embedding_vector`,
  `embedding_profile_id`, `embedding_model_id`, `vector_dimension`,
  `mapping_version`, `index_scope` and safe keyword fields for every searchable
  chunk.
- Staging self-heal: verify document-scoped Development Chat Test rebuilds a
  missing staging OpenSearch index from already-authorized PostgreSQL chunks
  only when a live Embedding Provider is configured and invocation is allowed;
  the subsequent answer path must still query OpenSearch hybrid retrieval and
  must not answer from PostgreSQL fallback.
- Hybrid ranking: verify retrieval combines vector similarity and keyword
  relevance through OpenSearch hybrid query or backend fusion, returns stable
  top-k candidates, and reports `retrieval_strategy=hybrid` only after the
  vector portion actually succeeds.
- Fail-closed behavior: verify query embedding failure, provider credential
  failure, OpenSearch vector query failure, missing vector mapping, dimension
  mismatch, missing Embedding Profile and citation scope mismatch all return
  stable errors without keyword-only fallback, PostgreSQL chunk fallback or
  broadened index scope.
- Profile grouping: verify selected document versions using different
  Embedding Profiles are queried in compatible profile groups and are never
  mixed in a single vector similarity query.
- Citation verification: verify every returned hit is rechecked against
  PostgreSQL authorization/scope metadata before it is used as citation context.
- Graph preview Pipeline: verify `build_graph_preview` produces a staging
  preview artifact from PostgreSQL project/document/version/chunk/tag metadata
  without requiring Neo4j, while formal graph sync remains publish-only.
- Pipeline detail layout: verify long artifact refs and error text wrap inside
  each Pipeline step card without overflowing the document card on desktop and
  narrow widths.
- Live Development acceptance: with real Development PostgreSQL, OpenSearch and
  the configured Embedding Provider, index controlled staging and published
  chunks, run document and project chat queries, and prove vector/hybrid results
  are returned. If a real dependency is unavailable, report blocked rather than
  passing with mocks or keyword-only search.

## Milestone 8B Test Design: RAG-008 / VAL-001 / REPORT groundwork

- Model configuration and adapter: verify Project Chat selects the project Chat
  Model or system default active Chat Model, rejects missing/inactive/credential-
  unavailable models with `model_configuration_required` or equivalent, and
  records model id, prompt version, token usage and latency. Tests must use the
  real provider adapter path with configured development/test providers or fail
  closed when configuration is missing.
- Citation-bound answer generation: verify prompts contain only authorized
  retrieval citations/context, answers cite returned chunks, no-citation
  retrieval produces `無法確認`, and deterministic fixture answers are never
  returned as formal success.
- Chat persistence: verify `chat_records` ORM/API contracts align with migration
  fields, including conversation title, selected document version ids, reference
  docs, revision suggestion, model ids, token usage and latency. Query, answer,
  no-answer and failure states must persist safely.
- Conversation scope/history: verify backend APIs create/list/load conversations
  by user/project/scope, keep selected version scope fixed after first turn,
  restore history on frontend load, and deny new turns when an old conversation's
  scope is no longer current active serving data.
- Conversation surface/version isolation: verify project-level Project Chat
  history/list/get/delete/download APIs return only published project-surface
  conversations, while Document Chat Test history, submit-review evidence and
  approval evidence return only document-staging records for the exact current
  `document_version_id`. Same-project, same-user and same-document records from
  other surfaces or versions must remain hidden from normal history and exports.
- Feedback persistence: verify `correct`, `needs_revision`, `not_evaluated`,
  revision suggestion, reviewer and timestamp persist; `needs_revision` requires
  a non-empty suggestion and cancel/close leaves the previous state unchanged.
- CSV validation run: verify CSV parser handles BOM, quoted fields, newlines and
  errors; creates `validation_run` and `validation_run_item` rows with expected
  answers/keywords/category/priority/scope; and rejects rows outside the fixed
  active scope.
- Worker execution: verify Development defaults to one worker with concurrency
  two, updates run/item states through queued/running/completed/partial_failed/
  failed/cancelled, continues other items after a single-item failure, and links
  completed items to persisted chat records.
- Judge behavior: verify active Judge Model produces score/reason when
  configured; without Judge Model, the item/run marks `judge_not_configured`,
  keeps evaluation unscored, and does not fabricate a deterministic pass/fail
  score.
- Report groundwork: verify stored chat and validation records expose enough
  data for later report aggregation: question counts, cited documents/projects,
  no-answer rate, feedback distribution, validation pass/fail, token usage and
  latency. Full report APIs remain separate report requirements.
- Frontend integration: verify Project Chat loads backend conversations,
  displays persisted turns/feedback/CSV runs, handles model-configuration and
  worker states, and labels any remaining fixture fallback explicitly.

## Phase 8B-2 Test Design: RAG-009 Live Provider + Async Validation Worker

- Provider adapter contract: verify OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible,
  OpenAI Responses API, Gemini, Claude/Anthropic, Ollama and vLLM-compatible
  adapters normalize endpoint/model/temperature/max_tokens/timeout and produce
  safe request payloads without logging API keys, tokens, full prompts or
  document content. OpenAI Responses tests must cover `/v1/responses` URL
  detection, no appended `/chat/completions`, `instructions`/`input` payloads,
  `output_text` and structured output-content answer parsing, usage passthrough,
  provider rejection and network-unavailable errors.
- Model configuration: verify active project/default Chat Model selection,
  missing/inactive/credential-missing/provider-timeout/provider-error fail
  closed with stable error codes and persisted safe failure metadata.
- Live acceptance boundary: all tests must either call the configured provider
  successfully through the real adapter path or prove the model-configuration
  fail-closed path. The focused Development smoke command is
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh integration:milestone8b-live`, which uses a local
  OpenAI-compatible acceptance provider while still exercising the live provider
  HTTP adapter, Redis-backed outbox dispatch, Celery worker execution and real
  PostgreSQL/OpenSearch/Neo4j dependencies.
- Worker queue and concurrency: verify validation runs transition queued →
  running → completed/partial_failed/failed/cancelled, Development concurrency
  defaults to two items, and item failure does not stop remaining items.
- Item execution: verify every item performs retrieval + answer generation,
  persists chat record links, citations, token usage, latency, attempts and
  error code/message.
- Retry and cancellation: verify provider timeout retry, max retry count,
  dead-letter/failed final state and user/admin cancellation behavior.
- Judge behavior: verify active Judge Model execution stores score/reason; when
  no Judge Model exists, the run marks `judge_not_configured`, remains unscored,
  and does not use deterministic expected-keyword/answer scoring as a success
  substitute.
- Frontend run status: verify CSV modal shows live run/item status, completed
  answers/citations/scores, partial failure summary and safe retry/cancel states.

## Phase 8C Test Design: REPORT-009 Live Reports Backend + CSV Export

- Authorization and scope: verify System Admin, global report roles, Project
  Owner, Reviewer, Editor, Viewer and general users see only authorized report
  topics and data rows.
- Report topics: verify live APIs for system overview, project ranking,
  reference ranking, document quality, RAG/chat usage, validation metrics, model
  usage/latency/error rate and Owner dashboards.
- Filtering: verify date range, project scope, topic filters, pagination/limit
  and unauthorized project rejection.
- CSV export: verify backend CSV uses UTF-8 BOM, RFC 4180 escaping, stable field
  keys/order, localized zh/en headers, ISO 8601 timestamps, pure numeric values
  and safe filenames.
- Data safety: verify CSV/API output contains no secrets, tokens, prompt全文,
  document全文, unauthorized names/IDs or internal stack traces.
- Audit: verify every report download records downloader, topic, date range,
  project scope, locale, row count, generated timestamp and request id without
  storing full report content.
- Frontend reports: verify `/reports` is live-first with loading, empty,
  forbidden, partial data, export failed and clearly labeled fallback states.

## Phase 8D Test Design: OPS-001 Operations / Observability / Audit Hardening
