- Audit coverage: verify chat query, feedback update, validation run lifecycle,
  report download, model invocation failure, provider readiness check and worker
  retry/final failure write append-only audit records without sensitive payloads.
- Structured logging: verify logs include request/project/conversation/run/model/
  provider/latency/error/result context and exclude API keys, tokens, full
  prompts, document content and citation content.
- Metrics safety: verify latency, error rate, provider failure, retrieval
  failure, queue depth, worker item status and report export metrics use safe
  labels and bounded cardinality.
- Health/readiness: verify PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, Redis, worker heartbeat,
  provider configuration readiness and retrieval/index readiness report healthy,
  degraded or unavailable with specific safe reasons.
- System Management status: verify provider, worker, queue and retrieval/index
  statuses render with masked details, recent safe error summaries and no
  sensitive payloads.
- Retry/failure policy: verify max retry, attempt count, last_error_code,
  last_error_at, dead-letter/final failed states and manual retry authorization.

## Approval Graph Parity Test Design: REVIEW-006

- Evidence derivation: verify the current task document/version creates the center Document node, every supplied staging chunk creates one typed Chunk node, unique tags create deterministic Tag nodes, and edges connect document-to-chunk plus chunk-to-tag without cross-task evidence.
- Interaction parity: verify the approval graph exposes the same legend, content-type icons, continuous wheel/button zoom, bounded canvas pan, node drag with live edges, click-vs-drag suppression, first-degree highlighting, detail fading, reset action and status text as the extraction graph.
- Route isolation: verify each approval fixture passes its own document/version and staging evidence; unknown tasks show no graph; opening, manipulating and closing the graph changes no approval or document state.
- Regression and responsive behavior: verify the knowledge-extraction route keeps its default graph data and controls, while the approval modal remains labeled, closable and usable at desktop and narrow widths without page overflow.

## Approval Bidirectional Evidence Test Design: REVIEW-007

- Source-to-chunk: activate mapped Original text, image, table and Chart sources by click, Enter and Space; verify all matching right-side chunk cards highlight and the independently scrollable list moves to the first match. Unmapped content remains non-interactive.
- Chunk-to-source: activate each chunk and verify the active Original/Markdown pane scrolls smoothly to and highlights its stable source anchor. Activating the same single selected chunk again clears both highlights without a repeat scroll.
- View continuity: switch Original/Markdown while selected and verify the same selection is retained and relocated in the new view; missing anchors show an explicit unavailable-location state without highlighting unrelated content.
- Layout and isolation: verify the Original viewer retains gray workspace, separate white pages, gutters, borders, page numbers and contained wide media, while both left and right panes have bounded independent vertical scrollbars. No edit or manual-chunk action is available and interactions change no approval/document state.
- Regression/responsive: verify the knowledge-extraction viewer retains its existing navigation and actions; approval evidence becomes two columns on desktop and stacked bounded panes on narrow screens without horizontal page overflow.

## Approval Viewer Switch Placement Test Design: REVIEW-008

- Structure and placement: verify the Original/Markdown segmented control is inside the left document-viewer region at the upper-right and no longer appears in the outer evidence identity toolbar.
- Scroll and overlap: scroll both Original and Markdown content and verify the control remains visible, preserves a safe scrollbar inset, and does not cover the first page, Markdown content, source highlights or focus rings.
- Interaction regression: switch modes with and without an active chunk and verify `aria-pressed`, retained selection, source relocation, bilateral highlights and independent right-side chunk scrolling remain unchanged.
- Responsive/accessibility: verify both controls keep at least 40px touch targets, visible keyboard focus, readable labels and no horizontal overflow at narrow widths.

## Reference-aligned Approval Viewer Header Test Design: REVIEW-009

- Structure: verify `文件文章` and the Original/Markdown segmented control share one white header immediately before the gray scroll viewer; the control is no longer an overlay descendant of the scroll container.
- Layout: verify title-left/action-right alignment, subtle border separation, standard Original/Markdown content insets, and equal visual heights between the document and chunk columns.
- Interaction regression: switch modes with an active chunk and verify `aria-pressed`, retained selection, smooth source relocation, bilateral highlights and independent scrolling remain unchanged.
- Responsive/accessibility: verify title/action wrapping preserves order, segmented controls remain at least 40px high with visible focus, and the pane has no clipping or horizontal overflow.

## Approval Evidence Viewer Parity Test Design: REVIEW-016

- Shared presentation: verify Approval Detail uses the same read-only document
  article and chunk-result rendering primitives or equivalent markup contract as
  Knowledge Detail, including structured Original pages, Markdown mode,
  independent pane scrolling and `source-target` / `source-active` highlighting.
- Chunk card parity: verify Approval Detail chunk cards show the left chunk
  index badge, compact metadata, right-side gray technical id, safe Markdown
  content area and read-only tag chips; the old `id · title` primary header
  pattern must not appear.
- Read-only isolation: verify Approval Detail does not render manual chunking,
  chunk editing, document/chunk tag add inputs, delete buttons or auto-tag
  buttons, and does not call mutation APIs from the evidence viewer.
- Safe Markdown: verify document Markdown, text layout blocks and text chunk
  content render through the shared safe Markdown helpers, including headings,
  lists, pipe tables, citations and empty-heading cleanup without executing HTML.
- Live evidence only: verify missing layout, Markdown or source mapping renders
  explicit unavailable / partial states and never falls back to fixture evidence,
  hard-coded sample paragraphs or fake original content built only from chunk
  concatenation.
- Regression: verify Knowledge Detail keeps editable controls and manual
  chunk/tag behavior where allowed; Approval Detail remains read-only and
  approval decisions, graph preview, chat evidence and review history behavior
  are unchanged.

Integration tests:

- Cover database migrations/schema compatibility, import workflow persistence,
  search/index adapters, object storage adapters, notification boundaries, and
  configuration loading.
- Cover Flyway migration execution from `sql/migrations/`.
- Cover Celery worker job state transitions with Redis as broker and PostgreSQL
  as the persisted state source.
- Use real configured development/test PostgreSQL, object storage, OpenSearch,
  graph database, identity provider and related services. Missing services make
  the affected tests blocked/unavailable rather than mock-passed.

  - Verify Original mode renders separate stacked white pages on a gray workspace with consistent width, page gaps, subtle borders/shadows, page numbers, responsive scaling, and intact chunk-to-page source positioning.
  - Verify Original mode keeps every page's top/right/bottom/left padding visible and constrains source highlights, long paragraphs, captions, tables and media inside the white page boundary; page gaps must not be overlapped by content from adjacent pages.
  - Verify Original mode keeps visible top/right/bottom/left gutters with a vertical scrollbar, including the right paper border, and wide tables/charts scroll inside the page without expanding it.
  - Select a chunk, then activate the same chunk again by mouse, Enter, and Space; verify Focus and Original/Markdown highlights clear without another source scroll, while selecting a different chunk switches Focus and relocates normally.
  - Activate mapped Original text, Image, Table, and Chart regions by mouse, Enter, and Space; verify the right chunk pane alone scrolls to and highlights the mapped card, while unmapped document content remains non-interactive.
  - Verify the document graph contains six Chunk nodes matching the sample results, exposes Text/Image/Table/Chart content-type attributes and icons, preserves source metadata, and retains correct Document/Tag edges and first-degree highlighting.
  - Follow the extraction-page Chat Test link, verify the four-stage strip is absent while document/version/staging context and back navigation remain visible, submit a question, inspect citations, judge the answer, and return without changing approval status.
  - Verify Reference Scope appears above Conversation History and shows fixed document version, LLM, Embedding, staging index, and chunk values with no select/dropdown controls.
  - Open every answer citation and verify the modal shows the authorized document/version/chunk/page/type excerpt and closes or returns to extraction correctly; open Needs Revision, verify suggestion is required, cancel preserves judgment, submit records it, and reopening supports editing.
  - At desktop and mobile widths, open citation and revision dialogs from every message position; verify the backdrop covers the full viewport, the dialog is centered, and chat message width rules do not clip or offset either modal.
  - Download the current conversation CSV with correct, needs-revision, and unevaluated answers; verify UTF-8 BOM, escaping, filename, current-session-only rows, timestamps, full citations, and saved revision suggestions.
  - Verify Download Conversation appears at the current chat title row upper right, is absent from page context, remains disabled for an empty conversation, and wraps cleanly on mobile.
  - Verify the chat header has no `v5 · chunks` badge, Download Conversation remains right-aligned, and version/chunk values remain visible only in the left Reference Scope.
  - Open Upload Test Conversations left of Download Conversation; download and inspect the UTF-8 template, upload valid/quoted/malformed/missing-question CSVs, verify confirmation gating, then confirm and verify every valid question produces a timestamped cited Q&A in the current conversation with completed status.
  - Verify chat-header action order is Upload Test Conversations, Download Conversation, New Conversation; assert all three are absent from page context, wrap cleanly on mobile, and New Conversation still clears current messages and evaluations.
  - Verify the extraction-page Chat Test entry is a green text link with a trailing right arrow, visible hover/focus treatment, no filled background, and correct right-side alignment.
  - Verify Knowledge Graph Preview appears exactly once in the Knowledge Chunk Results header, immediately left of Manual Chunking, wraps cleanly on mobile, and still opens/closes the document graph modal.
  - Open the document graph modal, verify Document/Chunk/Tag visibility changes progressively across the continuous zoom range, select every node type, and confirm only first-degree nodes and edges remain highlighted.
  - Verify the graph expands radially and uses bounded continuous zoom: 5% button steps, fine wheel-delta changes, percentage feedback, and progressive Chunk/Tag fading without stepped jumps.
  - Verify the graph canvas has no concentric guide circles and nodes use free radial spacing without overlap at desktop and mobile widths.

  - Approve or reject knowledge.
  - Search, inspect graph relationships, and run chat verification.

  - Switch among project conversation history items and verify the matching fixed document selection, message thread, evaluations, title, message/file counts, and update metadata are restored without creating or mutating records; verify duplicate empty conversations are avoided.

## Milestone 11 Test Design: Release Candidate P0 Fixture Removal

- Data Source / Sync live foundation:

    scope, permissions, required protocol fields, one-file constraint,
    extension policy and safe schedule values.
  - Verify secret-like fields are never returned in API responses, logs, audit
    summaries or frontend error text.
  - Verify successful initial sync creates or queues a live sync run and results
    in a project document/version state that can be manually extracted.
  - Verify failed remote access records a sanitized sync-run error and does not
    create fake document success.
  - Verify frontend Data Service modal calls live APIs, renders loading,
    success, validation, forbidden and retry/error states, and no longer treats
    simulated connection success as formal success.
- Submit Review live evidence summary:
  - Verify `/project/[id]/knowledge/[knowledgeId]/submit-review` loads live
    document/version, extraction pipeline, chunks/tags/source mapping, graph
    readiness and chat/validation evidence.
  - Verify missing required evidence renders a blocked state and disables submit
    instead of falling back to hard-coded policy rows.
  - Verify CSV export contains only displayed live chat evidence with stable
    columns, UTF-8 BOM and correct escaping.
  - Verify submit action preserves idempotency, permission, duplicate/stale and
    error states from the backend.
  - Verify successful submit shows a localized success state, next-stage manager
    review context, backend `current_task_id` / tracking information and
    document/version summary before automatically navigating to `/approve`.
    Verify the success path no longer redirects to the project import/document
    list. Verify failed submit remains on the same submit-review page, displays
    the safe backend error and preserves the loaded evidence summary.
- Approval Detail decision completion:
  - Verify approval/rejection decisions persist the current `approval_task`
    status away from `pending`, write `completed_at`, advance `lock_version`,
    and keep approval request, document version, review record, audit and
    idempotency response consistent.
  - Verify Owner approval cannot be submitted repeatedly after success and does
    not create duplicate success records for the same completed pending task.
  - Verify the repair artifact fixes existing request/version-complete but
    task-pending rows conservatively and idempotently so repaired tasks no
    longer appear in `/approvals/pending`.
  - Verify manager approval success shows localized success text, next Project
    Owner review context and then automatically navigates to `/approve`.
  - Verify Owner approval success shows localized success text, approved
    waiting-publish context and then automatically navigates to `/approve`.
    The copy must not imply the document is already active or published.
  - Verify rejection success shows localized rejected/tracking context and then
    automatically navigates to `/approve`.
  - Verify failed decision, optimistic-lock conflict or already-completed task
    stays on `/approve/[approvalTaskId]`, displays the safe backend error and
    preserves the loaded evidence summary.
- Chat Test live-only cleanup:

    and authorization failures render explicit states without fixture answers or
    citations.
  - Verify document-level Chat Test context uses live document/version data and

## Milestone 12 Test Design: Live Data Source Sync Worker

- Backend data-source sync domain:
  - Verify a queued S3/RustFS sync run moves through `running` to `success`
    when the configured single object is fetched, validated and stored.
  - Verify synchronized files use the same allowed extension and file-size
    policy as upload; unsupported extension or size-limit violation fails the
    run without creating a version.
  - Verify source snapshots are stored through salted hash object naming with a
    canonical extension and that the original remote file name remains only in
    PostgreSQL metadata.
  - Verify changed content creates the next major `DocumentVersion` with
    `extraction_revision=0`, no Pipeline, no chunks and no automatic
    extraction.
  - Verify unchanged content sets `unchanged`, updates sync metadata and does
    not create a new `DocumentVersion`.
  - Verify non-S3 protocol execution in P0 returns an explicit
    `unsupported_protocol` or equivalent safe failed state rather than fake
    success.

- Worker and queue behavior:
  - Verify initial runs created by data-source creation are executable by the
    worker.
  - Verify manual sync creates or dispatches one run and rejects duplicate
    queued/running runs for the same data source with a conflict.
  - Verify worker failure updates `DataSyncRun` and `DataConnection` statuses
    transactionally and writes safe `error_code` / `error_summary`.
  - Verify retry paths do not create duplicate versions after partial failure or
    repeated worker execution.
  - Verify outbox / Celery dispatch routes the data-source sync topic or task
    without breaking existing identity sync and validation-run dispatch.

- Security and audit:
  - Verify decrypted credentials are never returned by API responses.
  - Verify plaintext credentials, private keys, access keys, secret keys,
    tokens and raw sensitive adapter errors are absent from logs, audit summary,
    API errors and frontend messages.
  - Verify permission and project-scope failures do not disclose whether a
    hidden data source exists.

- Frontend sync lifecycle:
  - Verify data-service documents render true `queued`, `running`, `success`,
    `unchanged` and `failed` states from live API data.
  - Verify Manual Sync surfaces duplicate/conflict, unsupported-protocol and
    remote-failure states without fake progress or fake success.
  - Verify successful changed-content sync leaves the document waiting for
    manual extraction.
  - Verify no automatic extraction action is triggered by sync completion.

- Regression:
  - Preserve Milestone 11 data-source create/test APIs, Submit Review live
    evidence summary, Chat Test live-only behavior, notification center,
    upload/extraction, auth/session draft, reports, approval publish and
    deployment checks.
  - Preserve backend and frontend coverage at or above 80%.

## Milestone 13 Test Design: Data Source Sync UI Completion and Scheduler P1

- Backend scheduled sync:
  - Verify enabled Cron data sources with due `next_run_at` create exactly one
    `DataSyncRun(trigger_type="scheduled", status="queued")` and one
    `data_source.sync.requested` outbox event.
  - Verify future `next_run_at` rows are skipped.
  - Verify disabled data sources are skipped.
  - Verify sources with existing `queued` or `running` sync runs are skipped and
    do not create duplicates.
  - Verify `next_run_at` is advanced deterministically using the saved
    five-field Cron expression and IANA timezone.
  - Verify invalid Cron or timezone produces a safe error/skip path without
    leaking secrets or crashing the scheduler task.

- Backend manual/worker regression:
  - Preserve Milestone 12 S3 success, unchanged, changed/new-version,
    unsupported protocol, safe failure and no-auto-extraction tests.
  - Preserve duplicate manual sync conflict.
  - Preserve identity-sync and validation-run outbox dispatch behavior.

- Frontend sync history and polling:
  - Verify recent sync runs render trigger type, status, timestamps, produced
    version id, safe metadata and safe error summary.
  - Verify manual sync starts polling and stops when the latest run reaches
    `success`, `unchanged` or `failed`.
  - Verify `queued` and `running` show in-progress states without fake ETA.
  - Verify `success` shows synchronized / waiting for manual extraction.
  - Verify `unchanged` shows source unchanged and no new version.
  - Verify `failed` shows safe error summary and retry affordance.
  - Verify duplicate conflict shows an already-running message.
  - Verify refresh reloads sync run history.

- Security and regression:
  - Verify no credential, token, private key, access key or secret key appears
    in sync history UI, API response assertions, audit or logs.
  - Preserve zh/en i18n coverage for newly visible labels.
  - Preserve backend and frontend coverage at or above 80%.

## Milestone 15A Test Design: Mock / Fixture Removal for Core Protected Routes

- Project Import live-only rendering:
  - Verify `/project/[id]/import` no longer renders formal fixture/demo banner
    copy for documents, Pipeline, Graph or Chat.
  - Verify an empty live document response renders a real empty state, not
    sample documents or fixed Pipeline progress.
  - Verify live document rows drive title, version, source, lifecycle status,
    Pipeline progress and retry state.
  - Verify live API failure renders an error state and does not substitute
    simulated re-extraction or simulated source update rows.

- Knowledge Detail live evidence:
  - Verify `/project/[id]/knowledge/[knowledgeId]` renders live chunks returned
    by `KnowledgeDetailResponse`.
  - Verify missing original or Markdown artifacts render explicit unavailable
    states.
  - Verify Original Document mode renders live `document_layout` artifacts
    generated by Parser / OCR layout analysis, preserving page order, page
    numbers, headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, images/captions and available
    source positions without embedding PDF/Office viewers.
  - Verify Markdown uploads use the unique inversion rule: Original Document
    mode renders human-readable Markdown, while Markdown mode shows the raw
    Markdown source. Other formats use Pipeline-generated Markdown artifacts in
    Markdown mode.
  - Verify original files remain available only through authorized download for
    audit/manual comparison and the UI never exposes S3/RustFS credentials,
    storage object URLs or unauthorized signed URLs.
  - Verify hard-coded sample article sections, sample Markdown blocks, sample
    image/table/chart evidence and fixed source anchors are not used as formal
    evidence.
  - Verify chunk selection and source-mapping behavior degrade safely when a
    live chunk has no matching source artifact.

- Approval Detail live evidence:
  - Verify `/approve/[approvalTaskId]` uses live approval detail data only.
  - Verify API 403/404/load failure renders forbidden/not-found/error states and
    does not import or display fixture approvals, fixture chunks, hard-coded
    conversations, hard-coded validation summaries or demo review history.
  - Verify approve/reject/publish actions still use live task/version lock
    versions and remain disabled when the live task is not actionable.
  - Verify missing validation/original/Markdown evidence is shown as a missing
    evidence state rather than fabricated proof.

- Guardrail checks:
  - Add frontend regression coverage for protected route text such as
    `Fixture fallback`, `展示資料`, `此為前端展示資料`, and known sample document
    titles in formal rendering paths.
  - Keep allowed demo text explicitly scoped to unauthenticated preview or
    development-only routes.
  - Preserve Traditional Chinese and English locale coverage for new empty/error
    states.
  - Preserve frontend and backend coverage at or above 80%.

    unavailable and error states.
  - Preserve frontend and backend coverage at or above 80%.

## Milestone 15C Test Design: Remaining Protected Route Mock / Fallback Removal

- Home live-only rendering:
  - Verify `/` does not import `@/lib/fixtures`, fixture projects or fixture
    approvals.
  - Verify Home KPI cards are derived from live project, approval and/or report
    APIs, or render explicit unavailable values when a metric cannot be safely
    derived.
  - Verify active-project and approval-queue panels render loading, empty and
    error states without fixed project cards, fixed approval rows or hard-coded
    KPI values.

- Project Chat live-only rendering:
  - Verify `ProjectChatTest` does not define fallback documents or switch the
    active document source to fallback when live document APIs fail.
  - Verify no fixture answer, fixture citation, fake completed validation row or
    client-only success record is inserted into formal chat or CSV validation
    state.
  - Verify no-active-document, no-answer, index-not-ready, provider/model
    missing, forbidden and API-error states disable unsafe actions and do not
    substitute demo content.

- Project Graph live-only rendering:
  - Verify `ProjectGraphPreview` does not define fallback node templates,
    fallback edges or fallback graph status.
  - Verify graph API empty, forbidden, unavailable and error states render
    explicit messages without sample nodes or sample relationships.
  - Verify live graph payload remains the only source for formal graph nodes and
    edges.

- Remaining protected-route guardrails:
  - Add static scans for fixture imports/defaults in Home, Project Chat, Project
    Graph and shared formal graph/pipeline components.
  - Guard against known sample document names, sample users, `fallbackDocuments`,
    `fallbackNodeTemplates`, `fallbackEdges`, default `pipelineRuns`, default
    fixture `chunks`, `Fixture fallback`, `展示資料` and equivalent labels in
    formal protected rendering paths.
  - Keep unauthenticated login fixture and explicitly scoped development-only
    previews allowed.
  - Defer Knowledge Source and Project Reference Modal draft-preview cleanup to
    P1; verify this milestone does not broaden those modal behaviors.
  - Preserve frontend and backend coverage at or above 80%.

Security and configuration tests:

- Verify sensitive settings are loaded from secrets or uncommitted files.
- Verify production Chat/Judge/Embedding/OCR and integration credential
  create/reset/rotation persists only canonical Vault references and omits
  plaintext from responses. PostgreSQL encrypted values are accepted only in
  the typed non-production profile or controlled legacy migration-read cases.
- Verify CORS, OIDC issuer/audience, token validation, password fallback rules,
  and permission checks.
- Verify graph APIs omit unauthorized nodes and edges instead of returning
  masked anonymous IDs.
- Include dependency vulnerability scanning once tooling is selected.

must remain independently verifiable by batch.

  - Verify critical smoke coverage for setup/login/protected-route source
    boundaries; future browser or live-service gaps must use explicit

## CHG-201 Test Design: VAL-001 / REL-007 / AUTH-004 Completion

This section covers the approved-understanding scope for completing existing
`VAL-001`, `REL-007` and `AUTH-004` requirements. It does not introduce a new
product contract; it makes the existing specification testable and traceable.

### VAL-001 CSV Batch Validation

Backend/API checks:

- Creating a validation run persists every CSV contract field:
  `question`, `expected_answer`, `expected_keywords`,
  `selected_document_ids`, `category` and `priority`.
- Row-level `selected_document_ids` must be a subset of the fixed conversation
  scope; otherwise the whole run creation fails with a safe validation error and
  no partial run/items remain.
- Worker execution uses live retrieval plus configured Chat Model. Missing
  retrieval/model prerequisites fail closed or return explicit blocked/error
  status; no fake answer can pass acceptance.
- Judge execution uses configured Judge Model and System Prompt layering. If no
  Judge Model is configured, items become unscored `needs_review` /
  `judge_not_configured` rather than deterministic pass/fail.
- Retry resets only failed/error items and preserves completed item evidence,
  chat links, citations and prompt metadata.

Frontend checks:

- CSV parser supports quoted fields, commas, quotes and newlines for every
  contract column.
- Modal shows valid count, invalid scope errors, full item status, score/reason,
  citations, retry action and localized pass/fail/needs-review/error text.
- Downloaded template still contains the stable contract columns and UTF-8 BOM.

Live acceptance:

- Run at least one validation batch through real PostgreSQL, Redis/Celery,
  OpenSearch retrieval and configured Chat/Judge provider when available.
- If any required live dependency is absent, report blocked/unavailable under
  `TEST-002`; do not substitute a mock/fake/deterministic pass.

### REL-007 Cross-project Reference Event Surfacing

Backend/API checks:

- Source document update, delete, deactivate, reactivate and active-version
  switch create `document_reference_events` for linked, active references only.
- Each unresolved source event creates matching in-app notifications for
  authorized target-project recipients without exposing unauthorized source
  content or live source IDs after source access is lost.
- Event list/read/resolve APIs are filtered by target-project visibility and
  Owner/Editor write rules.
- Detach and successful reference update resolve or stop showing pending events
  without deleting historical reference evidence.

Frontend checks:

- Document cards show unresolved reference event badges/notices with safe source
  snapshot labels.
- Version Management shows source project/document snapshot, current source
  version, latest active version when accessible, unresolved event state and
  update/detach/resolve entry points where authorized.
- Notification Center shows reference source events with correct severity,
  action link/payload, read/resolved behavior and zh/en copy.

Live acceptance:

- Use at least two projects and two users with project-scoped permissions to
  prove event visibility for authorized target-project users and omission for
  unauthorized users.

### AUTH-004 Break-glass

Backend/deployment checks:

- Keycloak break-glass status/provisioning helper verifies a Keycloak-local
  account, not a NomoSmart local password.
- The account is disabled by default, mapped to the dedicated System Admin
  role/group, marked for first-login password update, and has MFA evidence or a
  clear blocked status when MFA verification is unavailable.
- Status/provisioning responses never return credentials, client secrets,
  tokens or plaintext passwords.
- Audit records capture verification/provisioning attempts and sanitized
  failure codes.
- Disable-after-use and credential-rotation runbook evidence is present in
  deployment documentation or returned status metadata.

Frontend checks:

- System Management remains read-only for break-glass lifecycle controls.
- Status/evidence copy distinguishes configured, disabled, attention-required,
  unavailable and blocked states without exposing secrets.

Live acceptance:

- Verify against a development Keycloak realm when admin credentials are
  configured. If Keycloak admin prerequisites are absent, record
  blocked/unavailable under `TEST-002`.

## Required Harness Commands

The rewrite should make these commands meaningful:

```bash
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend
./HARNESS/harness.sh test:e2e
./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check
```

Suggested report outputs:

- Frontend coverage: `frontend/coverage/coverage-summary.json`, produced by
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:frontend`.
- Backend coverage: `backend/coverage.json`.
- E2E report: `test-results/e2e/` or framework-native equivalent.

## Acceptance Criteria

A rewrite is test-ready when:

- Test suites are documented and runnable from the harness.
- Frontend and backend coverage each meet or exceed 80%.
- Critical flows have E2E coverage.
- Deployment checks pass for Docker Compose and Helm.
- Configuration and secret-handling policy checks pass.
- Any skipped tests are documented with a reason and owner.

## CHG-202 Test Design: REL-006 / UPLOAD-SEC-001 / CONFIG-002 / VERSION-002 (Historical)

### REL-006 / GRAPH-001 Historical Global Knowledge Graph

Supersession notice: the global frontend and unscoped API cases in this
historical section must not be executed or counted as current acceptance.
CHG-247 `GRAPH-008` retains only the unified internal model and replaces access
acceptance with explicit authorized Project/Document scopes.

Backend/API checks:

- Global/cross-project graph API returns only `project`, `document`, `chunk`
  and `tag` node types.
- Document version data appears only as document metadata; no `version` node is
  returned.
- Project-to-document relationships use one of the allowed source labels:
  upload, FTP, SFTP, FTPS, SSH, S3, HTTP API or reference project.
- Document-to-chunk relationships are labeled as split.
- Document/tag and chunk/tag relationships are labeled as tagging.
- Authorization is applied before response materialization: unauthorized nodes,
  edges, masked placeholders and anonymous IDs are absent.
- Bounded loading returns node/edge counts, truncation metadata and a stable
  continuation or neighbor-expansion signal without fixture fallback.
- Neighbor expansion uses the same authorization and bound rules as the initial
  load.

Historical frontend checks retained only as removal-regression inputs:

- The former Knowledge Graph popup/global payload expectation must be absent;
  positive rendering acceptance moves to `GRAPH-008` scoped Project/Document
  cases.
- Truncated and expandable states are visible and localized.
- Selecting a node or edge updates the detail panel with metadata only for
  authorized resources.
- API failure, empty graph and forbidden states render explicit live states and
  do not substitute fixture graph data.

Live acceptance:

- Use at least two projects with different project-role membership to verify
  authorized inclusion and unauthorized omission.
- Use at least one referenced document relationship and at least one tag
  relationship to verify cross-project and tag graph edges.

### UPLOAD-SEC-001 Scanner Gate

Backend/API checks:

- New uploads create scanner evidence before extraction dispatch.
- Accepted scan state allows the normal single-file extraction handoff.
- Rejected scan state prevents parse, OCR, extraction, PipelineRun and worker
  dispatch.
- Quarantine, pending scan, scanner unavailable and timeout states fail closed.
- Development disabled scanner mode records explicit disabled evidence and is
  reported as non-production acceptance evidence.
- Production scanner mode rejects disabled/missing scanner configuration.
- Scanner errors returned to users are sanitized and do not include internal
  scanner paths, signatures, raw service errors or infrastructure details.
- Audit logs record scanner outcome and dispatch-blocked decisions without file
  content or secrets.

Live acceptance:

- Run against configured scanner service when available.
- If scanner service is unavailable, report blocked/unavailable under
  `TEST-002`; do not substitute deterministic success.

### CONFIG-002 Global Document Size Runtime Configuration

Backend/API checks:

- Default effective `document_max_upload_size_mb` is 100 MB when no override is
  configured.
- `NOMOSMART_DOCUMENT_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB` overrides the default through typed
  configuration.
- Invalid units, non-numeric values and out-of-range values fail config
  validation.
- Backend rejects file upload and data-source fetch payloads above the effective
  limit before creating documents, versions, objects or Pipeline work.
- Public/effective config API returns the same value the backend enforces.

Frontend checks:

- Upload Modal displays the backend effective limit.
- Client-side oversized-file validation uses the backend value and does not
  hard-code a divergent 100 MB limit.
- Error copy is localized in Traditional Chinese and English.

Deployment checks:

- Docker env example includes `NOMOSMART_DOCUMENT_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB`.
- Helm values and ConfigMap render the same setting.
- Config policy checks detect missing deployment wiring or divergent setting
  names.

### VERSION-002 Old-Version Active Switch UI

Frontend checks:

- Version Management lists eligible previously published versions with
  compatibility and readiness status.
- Eligible versions show a switch action only to authorized project Owner users.
- Ineligible versions show blocking reasons instead of a switch-success path.
- Switch confirmation modal includes impact summary and requires explicit
  confirmation.
- Busy, success and error states are visible and localized.
- Successful switch refreshes current version, history list and active badges.
- Failed switch preserves current UI state and shows safe error text.

Backend/API regression checks:

- Existing switch endpoint still enforces project Owner, readiness,
  compatibility, optimistic lock, idempotency and audit.
- UI contract fields are available without exposing unauthorized reference
  details.

Live acceptance:

- Use at least one document with two published compatible versions and retained
  published index readiness.
- Verify the formal Project Chat / graph serving scope follows the switched
  Active Version Manifest after success.

## CHG-203 Test Design: AUTH-004 and OpenSearch Serving Revalidation

### AUTH-004 Break-glass Lifecycle Evidence

Backend checks:

- Break-glass status identifies the account as Keycloak-local and independent
  of LDAP/AD without returning credentials.
- Status reports disabled/default or emergency-only state.
- Status reports required first-login password update evidence where Keycloak
  exposes it.
- Status reports MFA evidence or an explicit unavailable/attention state without
  treating missing MFA as success.
- Status verifies System Admin role/group mapping.
- Status/provisioning attempts write sanitized audit records.
- API responses and logs do not expose username secrets, passwords, tokens,
  client secrets or raw Keycloak admin errors.
- No NomoSmart local password path or identity-header bypass is introduced.

Frontend checks:

- System Management break-glass panel remains read-only.
- The panel does not render enable, disable, reset password, reset MFA or
  credential management controls.
- Configured, disabled, attention-required, unavailable and blocked states are
  localized and distinguishable without exposing secrets.

Live acceptance:

- Verify against a development Keycloak realm when admin credentials are
  configured.
- If Keycloak admin prerequisites are absent, record blocked/unavailable under
  `TEST-002`.

### OpenSearch Serving / Version-switch Revalidation

Backend/API checks:

- Published OpenSearch documents include environment/profile/scope/mapping and
  project/document/version/chunk metadata required by `SEARCH-001`.
- Physical index grouping remains environment + Embedding Profile + scope +
  mapping version, not per project or per document version.
- Formal retrieval resolves the PostgreSQL Active Version Manifest before any
  OpenSearch query.
- Formal retrieval filters by exact active `document_version_id`.
- Missing manifest, unauthorized selected version, inactive version, staging
  version, incompatible Embedding Profile, missing readiness or OpenSearch
  unavailable fail closed.
- Old-version active switch requires project Owner authorization, compatible
  Embedding Profile, published-index readiness, explicit impact confirmation,
  optimistic lock, `Idempotency-Key` and audit.
- Switching active version changes the Active Version Manifest without deleting
  retained vectors for prior published versions.

Frontend checks:

- Existing Version Management old-version switch UI continues to show readiness,
  blocking reasons, impact confirmation, busy, success and safe error states.
- Project Chat and serving-readiness UI do not show inactive, staging or
  unauthorized versions as selectable formal retrieval scope.

Live acceptance:

- Use Development PostgreSQL and OpenSearch with controlled published test
  versions.
- Publish or seed two compatible published versions, switch active serving to
  the older compatible version, and verify retrieval only returns the active
  manifest version.
- Clean up controlled test rows/index documents or record cleanup blockers.

## CHG-204 Test Design: Remaining Incomplete Feature Completion (Historical)

CHG-247 reopens the conflicting completion claims below. `GRAPH-008` supersedes
global/unscoped graph behavior, `CHUNK-003` requires candidate Chunk editing and
evidence interaction, and their active test cases appear only in the CHG-247
section.

Scope:

- `KDETAIL-001` Knowledge Detail live completion.
- `REVIEW-020` Approval Evidence parity completion.
- `PIPE-010` Upload/OCR Pipeline loading and retry UX completion.
- `GRAPH-007` historical global/cross-project graph expansion, superseded by
  scoped `GRAPH-008`.
- `GRAPH-UI-007` historical rendering characterization; current browser
  acceptance is `GRAPH-008-E01`.

Out of scope:

- Live provider, Keycloak, Helm and full E2E prerequisite configuration gaps
  remain governed by `TEST-002` and may be recorded as blocked/unavailable.
- No mock, fixture, deterministic adapter or client-only success path may be
  counted as completion evidence for this batch.

### KDETAIL-001 Knowledge Detail

Backend/API checks:

- Document detail payload includes live document, current version, artifact
  availability, chunks, tags, source mapping and pipeline state needed by the UI.
- Missing original/Markdown/layout/chunk/tag artifacts return explicit missing,
  processing or failed state metadata, not sample content.
- Pipeline failed-step retry eligibility and retry-denied reasons are exposed
  consistently.
- Forbidden, not-found and stale-version states are distinguishable and do not
  leak unauthorized document metadata.

Frontend/browser checks:

- Original document, Markdown, Tags and Chunk result views render only live
  payload data.
- Loading, processing, missing artifact, failed, retrying, empty and forbidden
  states are localized and visually distinct.
- Chunk/source bidirectional navigation preserves document order and scroll
  focus.
- Historical behavior showed no manual edit controls. This is no longer valid
  completion evidence; `CHUNK-003` requires authorized candidate-only editing.

### REVIEW-020 Approval Evidence

Backend/API checks:

- Approval task evidence is hydrated by the submitted `document_version_id`.
- Original/Markdown/chunk/tag/graph/history evidence is read-only and
  task-scoped.
- Stale, missing-artifact, forbidden and processing states are returned without
  allowing decision actions that rely on incomplete evidence.

Frontend/browser checks:

- Approval evidence uses the same safe Markdown/original/chunk/tag rendering
  semantics as Knowledge Detail.
- Evidence panes remain read-only while preserving scroll, source focus and
  status display.
- Completed, stale and forbidden tasks show localized no-action states.

### PIPE-010 Pipeline Loading and Retry UX

Backend/API checks:

- Pipeline run/step APIs expose stable step order, progress, current step,
  retry count, retry eligibility, safe retry target and sanitized last error.
- Retrying a failed step preserves valid completed artifacts and never marks the
  pipeline successful before the backend reports completion.

Frontend/browser checks:

- Upload/OCR/parse/chunk/Markdown/tagging/embedding/staging/submission-ready
  states are visible in Knowledge Detail and related list surfaces.
- Retry buttons are shown only for eligible failures, show busy state during
  submission and refresh status after completion.
- Processing pages poll on a short interval and stop polling on terminal states.

### PIPE-011 Upload Progress Detail Disclosure

Frontend/browser checks:

- Upload progress overlay defaults to a compact state with current action,
  overall percent and a collapsed detail toggle.
- Before backend Pipeline detail is available, the overlay shows only honest
  pre-Pipeline actions such as validation, upload, document/version creation and
  Pipeline creation.
- After live Pipeline detail is available, the expanded details list follows the
  canonical Pipeline step order and displays localized step label, status,
  progress percent, retry count, error summary and artifact summary where
  available.
- Collapsing and expanding details does not interrupt upload submission, does
  not mark incomplete backend steps as complete and remains keyboard accessible.
- Multi-file upload keeps per-file result behavior and must not imply a single
  shared Pipeline for the whole batch.

Backend/API checks:

- Existing Pipeline run/step APIs remain the source of truth for live step
  detail; no fixture or fake step payload is introduced to satisfy the overlay.
- Auto-extraction responses provide enough document/pipeline identity for the
  frontend to hydrate or poll the corresponding live Pipeline details after
  upload.

### GRAPH-007 Global/Cross-project Graph (Superseded Historical Cases)

Do not preserve these global entry/API expectations. After CHG-247 Gate 4 they
serve only as removal-regression inputs; all positive serving behavior is tested
through `GRAPH-008` scoped cases.

Backend/API checks:

- Global and neighbor graph endpoints return only Project, Document, Chunk and
  Tag nodes.
- Document version is metadata only and never appears as a visible node.
- Project-to-document relationships use upload, FTP, SFTP, FTPS, SSH, S3,
  HTTP API or referenced-project source labels.
- Document-to-chunk relationships use split/chunk semantics; document/chunk to
  tag relationships use tagging semantics.
- Authorization is enforced by omission with no masked placeholder nodes.
- Node/edge limits, pagination or expansion cursors prevent unbounded graph
  payloads.

Frontend/browser checks:

- Global/cross-project entry points use live endpoints and render explicit
  empty, forbidden, loading and unavailable states.
- Neighbor expansion updates the canvas and Inspector without fixture fallback.

### GRAPH-UI-007 Browser Visual Acceptance

Browser checks:

- Desktop and mobile screenshots are captured at 100%, 150%, 200% and 300%.
- At 100%, Project and Document are readable while Chunk/Tag are low-density
  hints.
- At 150%, Chunk nodes and document-to-chunk relationships are readable.
- At 200%, Tag nodes and tagging relationships are readable.
- At 300%, at least two adjacent semantic layers remain visible.
- Node bounding boxes do not overlap in a way that hides labels or controls.
- Relationship lines connect only their two endpoint nodes; labels do not float
  away from the selected path.
- Node and edge selection update the Inspector with first-level details.

## CHG-218 Unified AI Model Usage Statistics

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-13. Gate 4 approved by Peter on
2026-07-13 with `Ok`; implementation and feature tests may proceed.

Backend/API usage-ledger tests:

- Given any Chat, Embedding, OCR or Judge provider adapter is invoked from UI
  chat, Public API chat, validation answer generation, Judge scoring, OCR,
  tagging, embedding build, query embedding or connection test, then exactly one
  non-sensitive usage event is recorded for each real provider call.
- Given a provider call succeeds, fails, times out, is cancelled or completes
  partially, then the usage event records model, provider, project/context,
  purpose, source channel, status, error code where applicable, latency and
  available usage values without prompt, document content, provider raw response
  text, API keys or credentials.
- Given provider usage payloads from OpenAI-compatible, Gemini, Claude,
  Anthropic, Ollama, vLLM, OCR and Embedding adapters, then normalization fills
  input/output/total token, embedding token, OCR page/image, vector count and
  chunk count fields where available while preserving safe raw usage.
- Given a provider reports official per-request cost and currency, then the
  ledger uses that value and records `cost_source = provider_reported`, including
  an official zero cost. Given no provider cost is returned, then estimated cost
  uses configured per-million-token or OCR-unit pricing and its ISO 4217
  currency with `cost_source = estimated`.
- Given an administrator saves any non-null model unit price, including zero,
  then a valid ISO 4217 currency is required. Verify zero is accepted and
  produces a valid zero estimate, null means unavailable, negative prices are
  rejected, and legacy prices without reliable currency remain unavailable
  until confirmed.
- Given no provider cost or complete price/currency setting is available, then
  cost is null with `cost_source = unavailable` and is never coerced to zero.
- Given retry or idempotency replays occur, then every actual second provider
  call is counted as a new attempt, while artifact/idempotency reuse without a
  provider call does not create a duplicate cost event.
- Given historical chat records, public API logs, validation items, embedding
  builds or tag metadata contain usage, then backfill creates best-effort
  `source = backfill` usage rows and does not fabricate missing OCR/Judge/cost
  data.

Report and CSV tests:

- Verify model usage reports aggregate from the unified usage ledger rather than
  only `chat_records`.
- Verify filters and groupings by date range, project, model type, model,
  provider, usage purpose, source channel, status and Integration Client/API Key
  where applicable.
- Verify report authorization follows `REPORT-009`: System Admin global view,
  Project Owner owned projects, Editor/Viewer/Reviewer authorized scope and no
  leakage for unauthorized projects, models, Integration Clients, row counts or
  costs.
- Verify CSV export emits localized headers, stable keys, numeric-only values,
  ISO timestamps, cost currency fields, row-count audit and no prompt/content/
  secret/token/provider-raw-response text.
- Verify UI, API and CSV distinguish official, estimated and unavailable costs;
  group totals by ISO currency and never sum different currencies into one
  amount because CHG-218 v1 performs no FX conversion.

Frontend tests:

- Verify AI model create/edit pricing controls accept zero, reject negative
  values, require an ISO currency whenever any price is non-null, and preserve
  the difference between zero and an empty field in both Traditional Chinese
  and English.

- Verify `/reports` model usage UI exposes the new grouping/filter controls,
  empty/loading/error/forbidden states, cost-unavailable labeling and clear
  separation of connection-test usage from business usage.
- Verify Traditional Chinese and English labels for model type, usage purpose,
  cost fields, status, Integration Client/API Key summaries and CSV controls are
  aligned.

## CHG-232 Keycloak Authentication Experience Redesign Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-14 with `1. A`, `2. B`, `3. A`.
Gate 3 test design is complete. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-07-14 with
`Peter approves CHG-232 Keycloak Authentication Experience Redesign`; the
planned feature acceptance may run.

Requirement under test: `AUTH-005` complete NomoSmart public authentication
Theme, browser-driven `zh-TW`/`en` locale behavior and non-destructive existing
realm Theme/locale reconciliation. Authentication policy and OTP enforcement
must remain unchanged.

### Theme Structure and Security Contracts

- The child theme contains a shared semantic authentication shell plus only the
  focused page overrides needed for credential/OTP behavior; inherited recovery,
  information, error and required-action pages retain Keycloak form contracts.
- Every custom message key exists in both `messages_zh_TW.properties` and
  `messages_en.properties`; `theme.properties` declares only `zh-TW` and `en`.
- Form actions remain `${url.loginAction}` or the appropriate Keycloak-owned
  action; messages remain sanitized and no credential field value is copied to
  custom JavaScript, URL, storage, log or analytics.
- CSS/script/font/icon references are relative same-origin theme assets. Source
  contains no external CDN, remote font, analytics, tracker, inline credential
  logging or NomoSmart credential endpoint.
- Default Keycloak polygon background, blue primary action and unconditional
  `Step 1 of 2` / `步驟 1／2` wording are absent.

### Accessibility and Interaction Cases

- Username, password, OTP and required-action controls have persistent labels,
  correct autocomplete/inputmode where applicable, at least 40px targets and a
  logical keyboard focus order.
- Password visibility is an icon button with localized accessible name, pressed
  state and visible focus. It does not move layout or clear/change the password.
- Invalid/missing credential state links the safe Keycloak message to the
  relevant field and exposes `role=alert` or an equivalent live region without
  relying on color alone.
- Submit enters a stable busy/disabled state and prevents accidental duplicate
  interaction without preventing the native Keycloak form request. A failed
  response restores a usable retry state.
- Hover, focus-visible, disabled, busy, information, warning and error states
  meet contrast and reduced-motion requirements.

### Locale Cases

- A clean browser context preferring `zh-TW` receives Traditional Chinese on
  login and inherited pages; a clean browser preferring `en` receives English.
- An unsupported preference with no explicit/remembered locale falls back to
  `zh-TW`.
- Manual language selection overrides browser preference and persists through
  login, error and required-action navigation using Keycloak's locale mechanism.
- Both locales fit `375px` without clipped labels/actions or horizontal scroll,
  and keyboard users can reach and operate the selector.

### Realm Reconciliation Cases

- A missing realm is created with `loginTheme=nomosmart`, internationalization
  enabled, `zh-TW`/`en` support and `zh-TW` fallback.
- An existing realm with default Theme is updated only in those bounded fields;
  rerunning reconciliation is idempotent.
- Before/after exports show unchanged realm ID, Browser Flow executions, OTP
  policy, required actions, LDAP federation components/mappers, users, groups,
  clients, redirect URIs, roles and role/group mappings.
- An unavailable Admin API, malformed response or incompatible existing realm
  fails closed and does not recreate, partially reset or silently overwrite it.
- Reconciliation request/response logs contain no admin token, LDAP bind secret,
  client secret, credential, OTP seed or user password.

### Real Keycloak Flow Cases

- Opening the real authorization endpoint renders the NomoSmart shell and no
  Keycloak default polygon/blue branding.
- Invalid LDAP-backed credentials return a localized, field-associated error and
  leave the form keyboard-operable without reflecting sensitive provider text.
- Peter completes the existing real LDAP-backed login and returns through the
  unchanged PKCE callback to NomoSmart. NomoSmart requests/logs never contain the
  password or OTP.
- Information, error/session and recovery surfaces use the same shell. A
  disposable Keycloak-local user exercises update-password, configure-OTP or
  other required-action pages and is deleted after acceptance; LDAP is not
  changed.
- A real disposable OTP-capable identity exercises the OTP page when safely
  available. Without that prerequisite, OTP browser acceptance is reported
  blocked and static/theme evidence is not promoted to a live success.
- A user whose current flow does not require OTP is not sent to a synthetic OTP
  screen, and CHG-232 does not alter authentication execution requirements.

### Responsive Visual Cases

- Capture and inspect login, error and one required-action page at `1440x900`,
  `1024x768`, `768x1024` and `375x812` in a real browser.
- Desktop shows a stable brand/context region and bounded form workspace;
  tablet/mobile becomes a readable single column with no nested card, horizontal
  overflow, text overlap, clipped locale menu or off-screen primary action.
- NomoSmart is a first-viewport signal. Surfaces use the approved palette,
  restrained shadows/borders, radii no greater than 8px and no decorative
  gradients, polygons, orbs or unrelated stock imagery.
- Switching language, revealing password, displaying a long error and entering
  busy state does not resize the fixed-format controls or shift surrounding
  content incoherently.

### Regression and Coverage Cases

- OIDC start/callback, state/nonce/PKCE validation, memory-only token handling,
  silent SSO, session-expiry recovery, logout and Popup reauthentication tests
  remain unchanged and pass.
- `/login` remains a NomoSmart redirect/control page and does not begin collecting
  password/OTP fields.
- Existing LDAP federation and `systemadmin` role mapping remain functional;
  Peter's authorization and John's non-admin behavior do not change.
- No API, schema, migration, frontend route, permission or deployment-port diff
  is introduced.
- Frontend/backend aggregate coverage thresholds remain at 80%; a repository
  coverage gap is reported honestly and is not solved by reducing thresholds or
  counting static Theme contracts as unrelated application coverage.

### Acceptance Commands After Gate 4

- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`

### Verification Results

- Focused CHG-232 Theme/realm contracts passed `2/2`; focused OIDC/login

- Complete frontend behavior passed `90` contract cases and `5` rendered

## CHG-217 Permanent Chunk Deletion Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed and Gate 4 approved by Peter on 2026-07-13.
Implementation evidence was recorded after the live verification run below.

Backend mutation cases:

- Owner/Editor with an editable candidate and matching lock permanently deletes
  the requested active Chunk and receives the updated Knowledge Detail payload.
- Viewer, non-member, cross-project ID, locked review/publish state, active
  published version, running conflicting Pipeline and stale lock fail without
  deleting or changing any Chunk.
- Deleted data is absent from `chunks`, `chunk_tags` and every
  `embedding_build_vectors` row for that Chunk. The deleted content, Markdown,
  source mapping, tag text and vector are absent from normal APIs and audit.
- Shared canonical Tag rows remain when another Chunk, another document, another
  version or a document-level assignment uses them. A Tag with no remaining row
  in either assignment table is deleted immediately in the same transaction.
- Concurrent orphan cleanup and a new assignment cannot delete a Tag that has
  become referenced; lock/serialization behavior is verified with live
  PostgreSQL sessions.
- A same-project second document and a same-document second version retain
  exactly the same Chunk rows, assignments, vectors and readiness before/after
  target deletion.
- A repeated DELETE returns `404 chunk_not_found` and never targets the Chunk
  that moved into the deleted index position.
- Remaining active Chunks are reindexed in source order and the document-version
  lock increments atomically. Injected transaction failure preserves all rows.
- Candidate staging chat/validation evidence referencing the deleted Chunk is
  removed or invalidated according to the specified permanent-data boundary;
  submitted approval/published versions are never mutable through this route.

Zero-Chunk and workflow cases:

- Deleting the final active Chunk succeeds and returns count 0,
  `chunk_artifact_status = chunks_required`, `next_stage_allowed = false`.
- Knowledge Detail remains available with Original/Markdown and manual Chunk
  creation; the Chunk panel renders the dedicated localized empty state.
- Frontend buttons are disabled with a reason, and direct backend Chat Test and
  submit-review calls both fail with `chunks_required`.
- Adding a new Chunk changes the state to queued/running until reconciliation;
  next-stage calls fail with `chunk_artifacts_not_ready`, then become eligible
  only after a live successful reconciliation.

Artifact reconciliation cases:

- Manual add, overlap split/replace and permanent delete each invalidate the old
  build/readiness and create one durable reconciliation for the new revision.
- For a nonzero set, live canonical Embedding vectors exactly match active
  Chunks; staging OpenSearch contains exactly that set and no deleted/superseded
  ID; the version graph contains exactly current Chunk/Tag nodes and edges.
- OpenSearch documents, published indices and graph nodes/edges belonging to a
  different document or version are unchanged after target reconciliation;
  shared Tag graph nodes remain while any non-target assignment exists.
- For zero Chunks, no Embedding provider request occurs; staging OpenSearch and
  version-scoped graph Chunk/Tag artifacts are empty.
- Provider/OpenSearch/Neo4j unavailable, timeout or partial write leaves status
  failed/non-ready with safe error and retry. Retry replaces the complete
  current snapshot and does not duplicate vectors, documents, nodes or edges.
- A stale revision completing after a newer mutation cannot publish readiness or
  reintroduce old content. Duplicate outbox delivery is idempotent.
- Real provider success is reported blocked until operator credentials exist;
  no mock, deterministic embedding or hard-coded success may satisfy acceptance.

Frontend and accessibility cases:

- Editable Knowledge Detail cards place Trash2 to the right of technical ID in
  a non-overlapping header action group. The target is at least 40px and has
  localized tooltip/aria text.
- Activating Trash2 does not select/toggle the card or move source focus.
- Confirmation identifies Chunk index and a bounded preview; cancel changes
  nothing; confirm shows busy state, prevents duplicate submission and renders
  safe backend errors without removing the card.
- Successful deletion removes the card and clears its selected/source-highlight
  state. Technical IDs wrap safely on narrow screens.
- Permission-denied and Approval Evidence surfaces show no delete action;
  temporarily locked editable surfaces expose no actionable delete control and
  communicate the existing lock reason.
- Traditional Chinese and English keys remain aligned.

## CHG-216 Security, Runtime Correctness and Release Remediation Test Design

Status: Gate 4 approved on 2026-07-12. Batch A verification is complete; Batch
B-D implementation verification is recorded below with live acceptance gaps.
No CHG-216 runtime behavior may be reported as passing from test design or
guardrails alone.

### Identity and Historical Initialization

- `OIDC-REAUTH-001`: live Keycloak Authorization Code + PKCE tests cover start,
  redirect, callback, state/nonce/issuer/audience/session mismatch, replay,
  expiry, disabled user, permission removal, 10-minute unlock, cancellation and
  atomic last-known-good activation. Existing-token `auth_time` and direct
  start/complete calls must not unlock settings.
- Historical `INIT-006` evidence: table-driven IPv4/IPv6 CIDR tests covered loopback defaults, `/32`,
  `/128`, subnet inclusion/exclusion, malformed CIDR and multiple entries.
  Proxy tests accept forwarded IP only from trusted proxy CIDRs. Bootstrap tests
  cover missing/wrong/correct token, constant-time comparison boundary,
  redaction and completed-system rejection.
- The former live appliance cases are retired by CHG-231. Current acceptance is
  the `DEPLOY-006` Compose/Helm migration/bootstrap design below; no appliance,
  Wizard or initialization API result may satisfy it.

### Connection and Network Security

- `CONNTEST-001`: each supported provider/protocol has live success and
  timeout/auth/TLS/host-key/not-found/invalid-response failures. Schema-only
  validation cannot set connection success. Configuration changes invalidate
  the saved fingerprint and UI state.
- Model/OCR/Embedding acceptance runs only after real provider settings are
  supplied. Missing credentials or unavailable providers are recorded as
  blocked/unavailable, never fixture success.
- `NET-002`: regression proves private/internal endpoints remain valid for
  model/OCR/Embedding/FTP/FTPS/SFTP/S3. HTTP/API tests block disallowed scheme,
  loopback, link-local, metadata, unsafe redirect and DNS destination change
  unless a controlled deployment allowlist applies. Credential-routing tests
  prove an endpoint/provider change cannot silently reuse the prior secret and
  logs/audit contain no secret or query-string key.

### Authorization and Dependency Security

- `PERM-003`: an active user with empty grants can authenticate and access only
  default logged-in surfaces; controlled menus, projects and data remain
  denied/omitted. Create, edit and delete are tested independently, including
  integration-client DELETE denied to edit-only users.
- `DEPSEC-002`: lockfile audits must contain no unaccepted high/critical finding.
  Upgrade regression covers Next.js routing/auth proxy/API docs, cryptographic
  envelopes and live SFTP. If Paramiko remains unfixed, container tests verify
  non-root user, dropped capabilities, restricted filesystem/network/resources
  and narrow secret mount; release readiness must contain owner/expiry/approval.

### Ingestion and Extraction

- `UPLOAD-SEC-002`: real scanner tests cover quarantine upload, accepted promote,
  malware reject, timeout, scanner unavailable, production-disabled startup,
  quarantine download denial, retention cleanup and no extraction/version
  success before acceptance. Upload and remote sync use the same security gate.
- `PIPE-013`: PostgreSQL outbox/Celery tests cover atomic version/pipeline/event
  creation, dispatcher retry, worker crash, duplicate delivery, concurrent
  claim, stale claim recovery, step retry limit and API response latency. A
  duplicate event must not repeat OCR/model/Embedding cost or artifact writes.
- `OFFICE-001` / `CHG-221`: real `.docx` files cover headings, text, lists,
  tables, links, footnotes, Unicode, images, tracked changes, comments and
  image-only content through sandboxed Pandoc-to-GFM conversion. Malformed /
  hostile OOXML, timeout/resource limits, parser crash, media validation,
  cache/temp cleanup and no-LibreOffice-fallback are required. Empty parser
  output cannot be accepted as a reliable text layer or completed artifact.
- `EMBED-003`: provider usage assertions prove one embedding request per valid
  version/profile/fingerprint and zero second call during staging indexing.
  Profile/content changes and invalid builds trigger exactly one rebuild.
- `DSYNC-004`: two isolated S3 services/connections prove endpoint, region,
  bucket, key, TLS and credentials come from the selected connection, not global
  platform storage. Secret-ref failure and cross-connection credential use fail
  closed.

### Public API

- `PUBLIC-API-003`: concurrent multi-process tests prove the configured atomic
  client/project limit cannot be exceeded and rejection occurs before retrieval
  or provider calls. Invalid-key abuse accounting, expiry and distributed reset
  behavior are included.
- SSE tests observe multiple timed events before completion, citation/usage/done
  ordering, mid-stream provider error, client disconnect/cancel and durable
  partial/cancelled records. A completed answer wrapped in one delta fails the
  test.
- Retention tests cover encrypted content, redacted logs/metrics, expiry cleanup,
  legal-hold exception, response/client/project/end-user feedback binding and
  persistent idempotency replay/conflict behavior.

### Migration and Deployment

- `MIGRATE-001`: Flyway runs against fresh and previously-versioned disposable
  PostgreSQL databases; checksum mismatch, failed migration, rerun and forward
  fix are tested. Compose one-shot and Helm migration failure must block app
  rollout and expose safe status.
- Production config tests reject placeholder/all-zero secrets, disabled scanner,
  localhost OIDC/CORS, disabled required live writes and missing required TLS.
  Frontend runtime-config tests prove deployed values reach browser code through
  the selected build-time/server contract.
- Run Compose config, Helm lint/template, ConfigMap/Secret policy, workload
  security context, image scan and SBOM checks when tools are available;
  unavailable tools remain explicit gaps.

### Test Credibility, API Reconciliation and Cleanup

- `TEST-005`: frontend instrumentation includes `.tsx`; statements, functions,
  branches and lines are independently reported at or above 80%. Rendered
  component tests exercise loading/error/forbidden/success interaction. Browser
  E2E phase 2 uses live OIDC/services for submit, approval, publish, scope and
  failure flows. Static source tests are tagged as guardrails and cannot satisfy
  behavioral trace rows.
- `API-COMPAT-001`: a machine-readable or structured inventory covers every
  section 12 API with canonical route, implemented equivalent/alias, status,
  owner and milestone. Contract tests exist for required and alias routes;
  deferred rows must be approved and cannot be counted complete.
- `CLEAN-001`: pre-delete reference/import scan, focused tests and build establish
  no dependency; the same checks after deletion plus repository generated-output
  guard prove cleanup did not remove active entrypoints or assets.
- `ARCH-001`: characterization tests freeze affected API/UI behavior before
  moving shared helpers or splitting workspaces. Authorization, i18n,

- `TRACE-002`: harness fixtures include stale/pending/implemented conflicts,
  historical approval misuse, missing owner/date and missing test/verification

### TEST-002 Live Backend Behavior Coverage Completion

Purpose:

- Raise backend application coverage to at least 80% using real local services
  and real behavior tests.
- Ensure `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend` and
  `./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check` pass without lowering thresholds or
  excluding application modules.

Environment requirements:

- PostgreSQL is reachable through `DATABASE_URL`.
- Backend API is running and reachable through `BACKEND_LIVE_BASE_URL`.
- Keycloak/OIDC is reachable through `OIDC_ISSUER_URL`.
- OpenSearch is reachable through `OPENSEARCH_URL`.
- Neo4j is reachable through `NEO4J_URI`.
- Redis/Celery broker is reachable through `CELERY_BROKER_URL`.
- S3/RustFS is reachable through `S3_ENDPOINT_URL`.
- Tests may load `backend/.env`, but the values must still point to live local
  services.

Test rules:

- Do not use mocks, stubs, fakes, fixture adapters or deterministic success
  paths as passing behavior.
- Use disposable UUIDs, unique names and best-effort cleanup.
- Do not use production data or production credentials.
- Do not relax `--cov-fail-under=80`.
- Do not mark skipped live-service tests as passing coverage evidence.

Backend/API checks:

- Health/readiness, config loading and safe error envelope execute live app code.
- Auth context, permission union, denial and project-role behavior execute live
  backend authorization paths.
- Users, roles and first-level Menu permission matrix execute live route and
  persistence behavior.
- Projects, documents, versions, references and lifecycle updates execute live
  PostgreSQL-backed behavior.
- Pipeline run/step, retry, review-lock and submission/publish transitions
  execute live route/domain behavior.
- System Prompt, AI model and provider validation execute live route/domain
  behavior while avoiding real secret disclosure.
- Serving/chat scope and inactive-document exclusion execute live retrieval
  boundaries where the configured services are available.
- Reports, validation runs, OpenSearch, Neo4j, S3/RustFS, Keycloak and
  Redis/Celery integration boundaries are exercised with real local services.

Acceptance:

- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend` exits 0.
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check` exits 0 and reports backend line
  coverage >= 80%.
- Any remaining uncovered critical workflow is documented with owner and
  follow-up rather than silently accepted.

Current verification result:

- 2026-07-10 focused live suite:
  `backend/.venv/bin/python -m pytest backend/tests/test_live_backend_api_behavior.py --no-cov -q --tb=short`
  passed with `19 passed`.
- 2026-07-10 `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:backend` passed with TEST-002
  live-only policy guard, `65 passed`, backend coverage `80.13%`.
- 2026-07-10 `./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check` passed with frontend
  `96.82%` and backend `80.13%`.

### SEARCH-003 Live Integration Provider Resolution

Backend/script checks:

- Given explicit live-test Embedding provider env vars are configured, integration
  scripts create or use only supported provider/model settings and do not seed
  `provider = acceptance`.
- Given no env provider is configured but explicit local reuse is enabled, the
  resolver selects an existing active supported Embedding Model and logs only
  non-secret identity fields.

  blocked/unavailable with actionable missing-setting text.
- Secret values, API keys, tokens and credential refs are redacted from logs and
  failure messages.

Live acceptance:

- Re-run Milestone 7 and Milestone 8B live integration commands after provider
  resolution is configured.

  unavailable, not as a product publish/index regression.

## CHG-209 / CHG-210 External Public API and API Key Management

Peter approved this scope on 2026-07-11 with `Ok`. The test design covers
`PUBLIC-API-001`, `PUBLIC-API-002`, `FB-001` and `APIKEY-001`.

Backend API and security tests:

- API Key Management endpoints require System Management permission and reject
  non-admin users, missing permissions and inactive users.
- Creating or rotating an API key returns the plaintext key exactly once,
  persists only an irreversible hash plus a short display prefix, and never
  returns the plaintext key in list/detail/usage responses.
- Lifecycle behavior covers active, inactive, expired and revoked clients.
  Revoked clients cannot be reactivated; delete is a soft revoke with audit
  metadata.
- Project allowlists cover one and many projects. Public API requests must fail
  closed when the requested project is not in the Integration Client scope.
- Public Q&A authentication accepts only the configured API key mechanism and
  does not accept internal UI Bearer JWTs as external API keys.
- Public requests require `end_user.employee_id`; `employee_name` and
  `department` are optional audit fields. The end user does not need to be a
  NomoSmart user.
- Public Q&A accepts exactly one `project_id` and optional
  `scope.document_ids`. Document IDs resolve through Active Version Manifest to
  the current active published `document_version_id`; unpublished, inactive,
  stale, staging or unauthorized versions are excluded.
- Public Q&A uses the project Chat model and configured System Prompt layering.
  Request payloads cannot override System Prompt.
- Public JSON and SSE endpoints return equivalent final answer, citations,
  response id, request id and retrieval metadata. SSE emits a clear terminal
  success or error event.
- Public request logs retain request metadata, external identity, project,
  scope, citations, retrieval status, duration, token usage where available and
  a marker that the record originated from the public API.
- Rate-limit and error-envelope behavior is covered without logging API keys,
  tokens, prompt text beyond configured retention rules or sensitive document
  body content.

Feedback tests:

- Public feedback accepts good/bad plus optional comment for a valid public
  `response_id` that belongs to the authenticated Integration Client/project.
- Public feedback is append-only. Repeated feedback creates new
  `chat_feedback_events` rows and the latest projection changes without
  deleting history.
- Existing UI chat feedback also writes append-only feedback events and keeps
  the frontend showing only the latest feedback by default.
- Feedback history preserves source (`ui` or `api`), actor identity, timestamp,
  optional comment and the linked chat/public response.

Frontend and i18n tests:

- System Management exposes an API Key Management tab only to users with the
  required first-level System Management permission.
- The tab supports project selection, optional external system/contact fields,
  lifecycle dates, create, rotate, activate/deactivate, expiry extension,
  revoke/delete and usage summary states.
- The key-created/rotated modal clearly communicates one-time plaintext display
  and does not show plaintext after the modal is closed.
- Empty, loading, error, expired, inactive and revoked states are localized in
  Traditional Chinese and English.

## CHG-219 OIDC Callback Error Recovery Test Design

This test design covers `AUTH-010`. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-07-13;
implementation and behavioral verification may proceed.

Frontend OIDC callback tests:

- Given `/auth/callback` receives `error=login_required`, any other OIDC
  `error`, missing `code` or missing `state`, the route redirects or otherwise
  resolves to `/login?error=oidc` before the user can be stranded on the
  callback loading screen.
- The callback failure path clears transient PKCE / state / nonce / return
  cookies when a response can be issued, does not call `/api/auth/exchange`, does
  not persist access / refresh / ID tokens, and does not accept an external
  `returnTo`.
- The client `OidcCallback` remains a secondary fail-closed guard for malformed
  callback URLs and never performs token exchange when `params.get("error")` is
  present or required parameters are absent.
- The interactive login link on `/login?error=oidc` starts `/api/auth/start`
  without `prompt=none`; protected-route silent SSO restoration may still use
  `/api/auth/start?prompt=none&returnTo=...`.

i18n and UX tests:

- Traditional Chinese and English locale keys cover the login callback failure
  message.
- The login page remains visible and actionable after callback failure; it must
  not render only `正在完成企業登入...` / `Completing enterprise sign-in...`.

Live/browser smoke when services are available:

- With frontend, backend and Keycloak reachable, open a protected route without
  an SSO session and verify the silent SSO failure lands on `/login?error=oidc`
  with a visible login action.
- If local services are unavailable, report the blocked URL/command and keep the
  source/frontend tests as the completed guardrails.
