## CHG-220 Complete Authentication State Routing Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-13 with `ＯＫ`. Gate 3 test design
is prepared. Gate 4 approved by Peter on 2026-07-13 with
`Peter approves CHG-220 Complete Authentication State Routing and Login Recovery`.

This design covers `AUTH-011` and the CHG-220 refinements to `AUTH-009` and
`AUTH-010`.

Auth entry and destination cases:

- Protected `/` or another protected route with no memory token starts exactly
  one silent SSO flow after hydration.
- A valid Keycloak SSO session restores tokens, validates `/auth/me` and reaches
  the state-bound safe internal destination; absent SSO reaches exact `/login`
  without an error notice.
- Safe path/query return destinations are consumed once. Missing, expired,
  absolute, protocol-relative, cross-origin, login/callback/auth API, recursive
  or nonexistent destinations fall back to `/`. A valid unauthorized target
  renders its forbidden state.
- An authenticated user entering `/login` returns to the current valid
  destination or `/` without starting another interactive login.

Callback and notice cases:

- Matching state plus trusted silent marker classifies `login_required` as
  normal anonymous login. Missing/mismatched state, missing/incorrect flow,
  forged `login_required`, missing code, nonce mismatch, exchange failure,
  cancellation and other OIDC errors are fixed safe outcomes.
- Every failure clears PKCE/state/nonce/return/flow transient state, performs no
  forbidden exchange or token persistence, and ends at exact `/login` without
  an error query.
- The HttpOnly login notice accepts only fixed enum codes, uses required cookie
  attributes and short TTL, expires or is consumed, and never contains provider
  messages, URLs, token data, state, nonce, stack traces or secrets.
- Login renders no warning for normal anonymous state, warning copy for
  `session_expired`, success copy for logout, neutral copy for cancellation and
  safe error copy for account unavailable, IdP unavailable and generic auth
  validation failure. Traditional Chinese and English remain aligned.

Runtime session cases:

- Near-expiry refresh success stays on the current page. Refresh failure,
  repeated 401, revoked token or invalid SSO clears auth state and automatically
  reaches exact `/login` with the session-expired notice.
- Eligible non-sensitive opt-in draft capture completes before expiry redirect
  when possible. Capture timeout/failure still redirects; secret fields and file
  bodies remain excluded. Successful re-login preserves existing guarded
  restore/discard/user/path/nonce/TTL semantics.
- `user_disabled` and `user_not_synchronized` end the session with an account
  notice. Permission/project-scope 403 remains forbidden in place. Validation,
  404, 409, 429, non-auth 5xx and domain errors remain page-level errors.
- Explicit logout keeps Backend denylist and Keycloak end-session, clears all
  auth transient state and returns to exact `/login` with logout success rather
  than expiry/error notice.
- Strict Mode, duplicate renders, multiple tabs, concurrent requests and back
  navigation do not create refresh, silent SSO or redirect storms.

Hydration and build-operation cases:

- Server-rendered protected auth shell includes a `/login` fallback that becomes
  usable within five seconds without React and has no-script coverage.
- Development and production Next outputs are distinct and ignored. With dev
  server running, production build is rejected before Next rewrites shared type
  declarations or dev assets; reloading `/` still hydrates and executes auth
  detection. After dev stops, production build completes normally.
- Production build/start uses its production output root and all generated route
  and TypeScript checks remain valid.

Live acceptance cases:

- Use real configured Keycloak and Backend for anonymous silent SSO, existing
  SSO restore, interactive login, safe destination, logout, expiry/account state
  where controllable, and callback-error routing. No mocked IdP success counts
  under `TEST-002`.
- Record IdP or service prerequisites as blocked when unavailable; static source
  checks alone do not claim live auth behavior.

- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`

## CHG-221 DOCX-only Pandoc Ingestion Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed on 2026-07-13; Gate 4 approved by Peter on 2026-07-13
with `OK`. Feature implementation and acceptance may proceed.

Requirements under test: `IMPORT-001`, `OFFICE-001`, `DOC-005`, `UPLOAD-SEC-001`,
`UPLOAD-SEC-002`, `PIPE-013`, `TEST-002`.

### Format And Entry-point Matrix

- Initial single/multi upload, document update and remote-source ingestion accept
  valid `.docx` and reject `.doc` before permanent storage/Pipeline dispatch.
- Extension, MIME, ZIP magic and OOXML Word package must agree. Renamed ZIP,
  renamed `.doc`, malformed OOXML and browser-supplied MIME alone are rejected.
- `.pdf`, `.txt`, `.md` and `.markdown` retain their existing accepted behavior.
- Frontend and backend expose the same DOCX-only format list and localized error;
  direct API calls cannot bypass the backend rule.
- Existing `.doc` source/history remains authorized for read/download and its
  published artifact remains serviceable, but re-extraction is denied. A DOCX
  update creates the next working version and preserves the active version.

### Real Pandoc Fidelity Corpus

- Run a checked-in or controlled real DOCX corpus through the pinned container
  Pandoc binary and verify headings, paragraphs, bold/italic, ordered/unordered
  and nested lists, tables, links, code, footnotes, Unicode and reading order.
- Verify extracted images are present exactly once in the version-scoped S3
  artifact manifest and every Markdown reference resolves through an authorized
  stable artifact reference with no temp path.
- Verify final visible tracked-change content is included; comment text is absent
  from body Markdown while parser metadata records comments/revisions and policy.
- Verify canonical Pandoc Markdown, not reconstructed chunk text, drives layout,
  splitting and generated Markdown artifacts.

### OCR And Failure Semantics

- Image-only DOCX without explicit OCR does not silently OCR or report reliable
  body text. With explicit/forced OCR, only validated extracted images are sent
  to the real configured OCR adapter and results preserve source order.
- Assert there is no DOCX-to-PDF conversion and no LibreOffice invocation or
  fallback in success, retry or failure paths.
- Missing/unsupported Pandoc, timeout, nonzero exit, empty output, malformed
  package, media validation/upload failure and unavailable sandbox fail closed
  with safe stable error codes and no completed blank artifact.
- Retry/outbox replay is idempotent for parser artifacts and media and does not
  duplicate downstream provider work.

### Security And Resource Cases

- Exercise ZIP entry/count/expanded-size limits, `../` and absolute paths,
  symlink-like media, duplicate names, unexpected MIME/magic, oversized media,
  external relationships and command-like filenames.
- Verify subprocess arguments are not shell-expanded, network is unavailable,
  process/memory/time/filesystem limits apply and temp/cache directories are
  cleaned after success, rejection, timeout and worker termination.
- Verify audit/structured logs retain document/version/parser evidence but omit
  document body, comments, credentials, raw command secrets and host temp paths.

### Deployment, UI And Regression Cases

- Typed Pandoc settings reject invalid timeout/memory/cache values and are
  rendered through safe Compose/Helm/config templates without secrets.
- Production backend image runs pinned Pandoc as non-root inside the configured
  sandbox and has no LibreOffice executable/package available.
- Upload/update UI shows DOCX-only guidance, rejects `.doc`, supports DOCX update
  and renders progress/failure/retry states in both zh-TW and en.
- PDF OCR, text/Markdown ingestion, publication, review and existing published
  retrieval remain unchanged.

## CHG-226 Interactive Reports Query, Pagination And Per-Report CSV Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-14 with `OK`. Gate 3 test design is
prepared. Gate 4 approved by Peter on 2026-07-14 with
`Peter approves CHG-226 Interactive Reports Query Pagination and Per-Report CSV`.

Requirement under test: `REPORT-011` with retained `REPORT-008`, `REPORT-009`,
`REPORT-010`, `MOCK-005` and `TEST-002` boundaries.

Verification result on 2026-07-14:

- Focused live Backend report behavior passed with real local identity and
  PostgreSQL services, including 21 temporary Owner projects, two pages,
  fixed 20-row page size, page-boundary rejection and full matching-row CSV;
  all temporary rows were cleaned in `finally`.
- The same focused pytest under coverage executed the behavior successfully and
  measured `backend/app/api/routes/reports.py` at 93%, but the command failed
  the repository-wide 80% threshold because one selected test covered 40.75%
  of the complete Backend application.
- Frontend report contracts passed `3/3`; complete contracts passed `86/86`;
  component tests passed `5/5`; lint, TypeScript and i18n checks passed.
- Authenticated desktop Browser acceptance passed for draft/applied filters,
  Query, system scope, complete multi-topic tabs, two independent 20-row tables,
  per-table page changes and CSV actions, and model-filter placement. Browser
  console errors: zero.
- Repository-wide frontend coverage remains open at 7.08% lines versus 80%; a
  production build was not executed because the active development server
  triggered the approved output-safety guard.

### Backend Query And Pagination Cases

- Summary accepts canonical date, scope, project, model filters, `page` and
  `page_size=20`; invalid ranges/pages/scope IDs fail closed.
- Summary and CSV use the explicitly requested authorized scope; when legacy
  callers omit scope, System Management viewers default to `system` and other
  users default to `accessible`. Filter-options retains `owner_projects` as its
  default selection.
- Every topic returns stable `page`, `page_size`, `total_rows`, `total_pages`
  and at most 20 rows; first, middle, last, out-of-range and zero-row results are
  covered with real PostgreSQL data.
- Stable sort prevents duplicate/missing rows while paging unchanged data.
- Scope/project filters are intersected with the authenticated user's real
  system/Owner/reviewer/member/actor visibility; unauthorized names, IDs,
  prefixes and row counts remain absent.
- Filter-options returns only allowed scopes/projects/API Key prefixes and never
  secrets or options inferred from unauthorized report rows.
- Multi-topic tabs can issue independent requests with the same canonical
  applied filters and produce topic-correct rows and metadata.

### CSV Cases

- Each supported table topic exports all matching authorized rows independent
  of the current page, including a controlled dataset beyond 5,000 rows without
  silent truncation.
- Streaming CSV retains UTF-8 BOM, RFC 4180 escaping, localized/stable headers,
  ISO dates, numeric values and safe fields.
- Audit records the actual emitted row count, actor, scope, project, topic,
  filters, locale, request ID and generated time only after successful export.
- Unauthorized/invalid requests fail before streaming; no partial success file,
  secret, prompt, document content or internal stack is returned.

### Frontend Query-State Cases

- First authorized render automatically queries default applied filters once.
- Editing any common/model draft filter issues no summary request, preserves
  prior applied results and presents the dirty-filter notice.
- Query validates and atomically applies drafts, resets every active-tab topic
  to page 1, disables duplicate submit and ignores stale responses.
- Tab mapping queries exactly the required one or two topics; no table reads a
  response belonging to another topic.
- Model filters render after KPI cards and immediately before the model report,
  and remain hidden from other tabs.

### Loading, Pagination And Export UI Cases

- Initial/full query has a stable accessible report-area Loading animation;
  pagination has topic-local Loading; export has button-local Loading.
- Each table renders at most 20 rows and accessible first/previous/number/next
  controls with correct disabled states and total-row/page information.
- Page activation fetches only that topic with applied filters and does not
  reset sibling tables.
- Every table-backed report Panel has exactly one topic-correct CSV button; the
  top filter bar and non-table panels have none.
- Empty, partial, forbidden, query-error, page-error and export-error states use
  live responses and never fixture fallback.
- Desktop and narrow layouts preserve filter readability, table horizontal
  scrolling, pagination controls and 40px mobile targets; zh/en keys align.

## CHG-229 Full-stack Single-domain Deployment Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-14. Gate 3 test design is
prepared. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-07-20 with
`Peter approves CHG-229 Full-stack Single-domain Deployment`; implementation
and the approved tests may run.

Requirements under test: `DEPLOY-002`, `DEPLOY-003`, `DEPLOY-004`,
`DEPLOY-005`, `AUTH-012` and retained `MIGRATE-001` / `TEST-002` controls.

### Configuration And Policy Cases

- Compose and Helm each declare frontend, backend, worker, Beat, PostgreSQL,
  Redis, RustFS, OpenSearch, Neo4j, Keycloak and ClamAV with pinned images,
  resources, health/probes and required configuration.
- Every peripheral has exactly one effective bundled or external mode; invalid
  both/neither combinations fail values/schema or startup validation.
- Production rejects HTTP public origins, localhost, missing TLS/Ingress,
  placeholder/all-zero secrets, scanner disabled, floating image tags, public
  native service ports, missing stateful persistence and unsafe Keycloak proxy
  settings.
- Non-sensitive values render through env/ConfigMap and credentials only through
  uncommitted Compose env, Kubernetes Secret references or approved external
  secret integration. Rendered manifests and logs contain no plaintext secret.

### Docker Compose Live Cases

- A clean `docker compose up` with the approved env starts every real service;
  app readiness waits for PostgreSQL bootstrap, Flyway, S3 buckets, Keycloak
  bootstrap and all required dependencies.
- Only host ports 80 and 443 are published by default. The debug profile binds
  selected native ports only to `127.0.0.1`; disabling the profile removes them.
- HTTP 80 preserves path/query and redirects to HTTPS 443. HTTPS serves `/`,
  `/api/backend`, Keycloak `/identity/realms/nomosmart` discovery/resources and
  the existing NomoSmart `/auth/callback` without path collision.
- Public Keycloak issuer, authorization, token, JWKS, logout and frontend login
  complete through the same origin. Admin/master paths deny an untrusted source
  and allow only the configured administrator network; health/metrics remain
  internal.
- PostgreSQL contains separate least-privilege NomoSmart and Keycloak databases
  and users. Restart preserves application, realm, object, index and graph data.
- Flyway, S3 bucket and Keycloak bootstrap reruns are idempotent. An intentional
  migration/bootstrap failure prevents backend/worker/edge readiness and emits
  observable, redacted evidence.
- Real upload/scan/worker behavior reaches ClamAV, RustFS, Redis, PostgreSQL,
  OpenSearch and Neo4j. No fake adapter or hard-coded success satisfies the case.

### Helm Static And Live Cases

- `helm lint`, values schema and rendered-manifest tests cover bundled and each
  external-mode branch, one-host Ingress, restricted admin Ingress, ClusterIP
  services, PVCs, Jobs/hooks, init gates, probes, resources, security contexts,
  NetworkPolicies and Secret references.
- A disposable real cluster/namespace with Ingress, DNS/TLS and StorageClass
  installs the complete chart in one command. PostgreSQL becomes ready,
  bootstrap/migration Jobs complete, PVCs bind and all app/peripheral workloads
  become ready before HTTPS acceptance.
- No data service renders a public NodePort/LoadBalancer. External access sees
  only platform 80/443 and the allowed application/OIDC paths.
- Stateful pod recreation and chart upgrade preserve data. A failing upgrade
  migration blocks new app rollout; correcting it allows forward migration.
  Rollback reuses retained state and does not execute a down migration.
- Uninstall removes namespaced stateless resources but preserves stateful PVCs
  by default. Explicit test cleanup removes only the disposable namespace/data.
- Switching one service at a time to a real external test endpoint suppresses
  its bundled workload and keeps NomoSmart healthy through the same typed
  configuration and Secret contract.

### OIDC And Internal Transport Cases

- Browser runtime config uses the public
  `https://<host>/identity/realms/nomosmart` issuer.
- Backend internal discovery/JWKS overrides can reach Keycloak without public
  hairpin routing, but token validation still requires the exact public issuer,
  audience, signature and claims. A mismatched discovery issuer fails closed.
- Edge overwrites forwarding headers and Keycloak accepts them only from the
  trusted edge. Direct internal access cannot spoof external scheme/host/client
  address or create attacker-controlled redirect/action URLs.

### LDAP/AD Administration Cases

- Deployment documentation identifies the restricted same-host admin URL,
  `nomosmart` realm, User Federation flow, LDAPS/StartTLS and truststore setup,
  read-only bind, Users/Groups DN, common AD/LDAP attribute and group mappers,
  connection/authentication test, initial/changed sync, NomoSmart external group
  mapping, disabled-user check, rotation and troubleshooting.
- Examples contain placeholders only and state that NomoSmart never stores or
  edits directory hosts, Bind DN/password, CA or membership.
- When an operator supplies a non-production LDAP/AD service, live acceptance
  proves Keycloak connection/authentication, user/group import, disabled-state
  behavior and subsequent NomoSmart sync/role mapping. Without that prerequisite
  the result is explicitly blocked under `TEST-002`, never replaced by a mock.

### Operations And Recovery Cases

- Backup and restore rehearsal covers PostgreSQL/NomoSmart, PostgreSQL/Keycloak,
  RustFS objects, OpenSearch and Neo4j with checksums/counts and post-restore
  application/OIDC acceptance.
- Existing shared-database Keycloak upgrade rehearsal backs up first and proves
  either database migration or an explicitly authorized development realm
  rebuild without damaging NomoSmart data.
- TLS and application/service secret rotation complete without committing or
  logging old/new values. Old credentials stop working where revocation is
  supported and readiness recovers with the new values.
- Documentation clearly labels the bundled stateful baseline as non-HA and
  records minimum resources, storage retention and external/HA transition.

### Acceptance Commands After Gate 4

- `git diff --check`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh test:plan`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh docker:config`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh helm:lint`
- `./HARNESS/harness.sh deploy:config-policy`
- focused deployment/config security tests
- live Docker Compose full-stack install/restart/failure acceptance
- live disposable-cluster Helm install/upgrade/failure/rollback acceptance
- configured real LDAP/AD federation acceptance or an explicit blocked result
- relevant backend/frontend/OIDC tests and `./HARNESS/harness.sh coverage:check`

### 2026-07-20 Verification Result

- Passed focused deployment/config/live-service tests `31/31`, Backend syntax, Docker
  Compose config with the bundled profiles and loopback debug profile, Helm
  lint plus development/production/bundled/each-external/all-external renders,

## CHG-230 Identity Settings Keycloak Popup Reauthentication Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-14 with `OK`. Gate 3 test design is
prepared. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-07-14 with
`Peter approves CHG-230 Identity Settings Keycloak Popup Reauthentication`.

Requirement under test: `AUTH-013`, with regression coverage for `AUTH-003` and
`OIDC-REAUTH-001`.

### Permission And Presentation Cases

- An active user with `SystemManagement.view` but no edit grant can open the
  Identity Settings Tab and view locked settings, but the DOM contains no
  verification/edit trigger, unlock countdown, save or cancel-lock control.
- A user whose effective role union includes `SystemManagement.edit` sees one
  clear「驗證身分並編輯」/ English equivalent action while locked.
- Direct start, complete, lock, validate and activate API requests without edit
  permission return 403 and create no flow, grant, candidate, setting revision
  or fake frontend success.
- Removing edit permission or disabling the account after start but before
  complete/save prevents unlock/mutation and leaves the setting locked.

### Modal And Popup Cases

- Activating the trigger opens an accessible NomoSmart Modal with protected
  action context, cancel and continue controls, focus handling and no password,
  OTP, Passkey, MFA, LDAP/AD credential input or iframe.
- Continue synchronously creates exactly one bounded Popup before awaiting the
  start API. The parent page URL and component state remain in place and the
  Identity Settings draft is not lost.
- A Popup blocker, start-API failure or missing authorization URL closes any
  incomplete handle, leaves settings locked and shows localized retry feedback.
- Valid Popup callback completion sends only a fixed result to the exact parent
  origin. Parent code rejects a different origin, a different window source,
  unknown result or duplicate result and never calls complete for them.
- Success invokes complete once, closes Popup and Modal, enters the existing
  10-minute unlocked state and countdown without page reload. Save, cancel,
  tab-leave, logout and expiry still revoke and relock.
- User close/cancel, five-minute timeout, provider failure and complete-API
  failure clear timers/listeners/Popup state, remain locked and expose Retry.
- Component unmount removes all message, close-polling and timeout resources.

### OIDC And Backend Security Cases

- Start remains Authorization Code + PKCE S256 with fresh `prompt=login`,
  `max_age=0`, random state/nonce/verifier, five-minute expiry and current
  user/session/scope binding.
- Callback validates state, code exchange, issuer, audience, signature, nonce,
  subject and `auth_time`; a mismatched user/session, stale auth time, malformed
  token, unavailable provider or invalid state fails closed.
- Callback success/error redirects only to the fixed same-origin Popup result
  route with an enumerated result; URL/message/error UI contain no code, token,
  state, nonce, raw provider error, password or secret.
- Completion cookie remains HttpOnly, short-lived, path-scoped and one-time.
  Missing, expired, revoked, replayed or cross-session completion fails.
- Audit records start/callback/unlock/lock/activation result metadata without
  credential, token, provider payload or setting secret values.
- Keycloak frontend client keeps Direct Access Grant disabled; no password grant
  or NomoSmart credential-validation endpoint exists.

### Regression And Compatibility Cases

- Existing identity candidate validation, discovery/JWKS checks, atomic
  activation, last-known-good retention, revision behavior and safe errors pass.
- System Parameters and initial `draft_unvalidated` behavior are unchanged.
- Ordinary login, silent SSO, session-expiry, logout and initialization reauth
  routes do not adopt the Identity Settings Popup behavior accidentally.
- Traditional Chinese and English dictionaries remain aligned; Modal/Popup
  status text fits desktop and narrow viewports and remains keyboard accessible.

### Live Browser Acceptance

- With a real edit-capable user, verify the parent stays on `/system`, Keycloak
  owns credential/MFA UI in a Popup, successful same-user fresh auth closes the
  Popup and unlocks the existing page, then explicit cancel relocks it.
- With a real view-only user, verify the unlock trigger is absent and direct API
  attempts are denied.
- Exercise Popup blocking/closing and safe retry without a false unlock.
- If real credential/MFA input is not operator-provided, report completion
  acceptance blocked under `TEST-002`; do not use a mock/fake password result.

## CHG-231 Deployment-only Initialization and Setup Wizard Removal Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-14 with `1. 是`, `2. 是`, `3. 是`.
Gate 3 test design is prepared. Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-07-14 with
`Peter approves CHG-231 Deployment-only Initialization and Setup Wizard Removal`;
the planned product/deployment tests may run.

Requirement under test: `DEPLOY-006`, superseding active `INIT-001` through
`INIT-006` behavior while preserving historical schema compatibility.

### Retired Frontend Surface Cases

- A real anonymous request to `/setup` receives the standard Next.js 404 page
  and status, with no redirect to `/login`, `/`, an authenticated destination or
  an initialization replacement.
- A request carrying a valid authenticated session receives the same standard
  404. Locale, query string, callback and old unlock parameters cannot restore
  the route.
- Frontend source contains no setup route/component, setup auth-public allowlist,
  hydration exception, setup API client, setup-only style or orphaned zh/en
  initialization key. Unrelated data-service setup and MFA setup wording remain.
- Navigation, sitemap and route inventories contain no `/setup` entry.

### Retired Backend Surface Cases

- `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` requests to
  `/api/v1/system-initialization` and representative `status`, `validate`,
  `apply`, `rollback`, `unlock/start`, `unlock/complete`, `unlock` and `lock`
  subpaths return the normal FastAPI 404 envelope.
- Results remain 404 with no authorization, a valid bearer session, old
  `X-NomoSmart-Bootstrap-Token`, forwarded-address headers or all of them.
- Requests create no initialization row, step, audit entry, file mutation,
  Flyway process, external resource or readiness transition.
- Backend source/runtime imports contain no initialization router/domain/access
  module, schemas, active ORM mapping, configuration settings, token comparison,
  CIDR exception or appliance config-file writer.
- OpenAPI contains no system-initialization operation or schema.

### Compose Migration And Bootstrap Cases

- A clean Compose deployment runs the real Flyway migration once, then the real
  deployment bootstrap once, before backend readiness and worker/Beat startup.
- Re-running bootstrap and restarting the stack is idempotent: no duplicate
  migration/resource, secret overwrite, legacy-table write or user data loss.
- Missing required config, unavailable dependency, Flyway checksum/failure and
  incompatible existing bootstrap resource each fail the responsible one-shot
  service and keep backend/worker/Beat unavailable or not ready.
- Correcting the cause and retrying completes without volume reset or down
  migration. Logs identify the failing stage and safe resource identifier but
  contain no password, token, key, document content or full secret-bearing URL.
- Compose config and example env contain no `SYSTEM_INITIALIZATION_*` key and
  document the migration/bootstrap/retry commands.

### Helm Migration And Bootstrap Cases

- Helm lint, values schema and rendered output include one migration Job, one
  deployment-bootstrap Job and an application workload completion gate using
  the existing chart only. No raw Kubernetes deployment manifests are added.
- A disposable real namespace install against configured real dependencies
  completes migration/bootstrap Jobs before backend/worker/Beat readiness.
- A migration or bootstrap failure marks install/upgrade failed and prevents new
  application readiness. A corrected retry is idempotent and does not require
  data deletion.
- Upgrade preserves application and legacy initialization data. Rollback reuses
  retained state, never performs a down migration and does not report readiness
  from an obsolete release's false evidence.
- Values, ConfigMaps, Secrets and schema contain no initialization bootstrap
  token/CIDR/config-path setting; job credentials come only from approved Secret
  references and rendered/logged output is redacted.

### Legacy Data And Upgrade Cases

- Before upgrade, insert uniquely identifiable historical rows into
  `system_initialization_state` and `system_initialization_steps`. After Flyway,
  bootstrap, app startup, readiness checks and ordinary requests, the rows and
  counts are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- A fresh database may still contain those tables because immutable historical
  migrations run, but application metadata/OpenAPI/ORM access and readiness do
  not depend on them.
- No new migration drops, truncates, rewrites or adds a runtime dependency to
  the legacy tables.

### Development And Documentation Cases

- Operator documentation presents Docker Compose and Helm as the only supported
  installation/upgrade paths and contains no instruction to visit `/setup` or
  call a system-initialization API.
- Direct frontend/backend development instructions require external typed
  configuration and already initialized real dependencies and explicitly state
  that direct execution is not a production deployment artifact.
- Helm is the only Kubernetes delivery path; no raw Kubernetes manifest bundle,
  alternate chart or UI-generated manifest exists.
- CHG-229's pending full-stack bundling, one-domain edge and external-service
  switches are not falsely reported as completed by CHG-231 tests.

### Regression And Coverage Cases

- Authentication routing, Identity Settings reauthentication, runtime config,
  health/readiness, migration and ordinary System Management behavior continue
  to pass after setup-specific code removal.
- Frontend and backend automated coverage is measured independently and remains
  subject to the unchanged 80% release gate. Static source contracts cannot
  substitute for real HTTP, PostgreSQL, Compose or Kubernetes behavior under
  `TEST-002`.

## CHG-233 Local Role and LDAP Group One-to-One Mapping Test Design

Status: designed after Gate 2 confirmation on 2026-07-15. Gate 4 was approved
by Peter on 2026-07-15 with `Peter approves CHG-233 Local Role and LDAP Group
One-to-One Mapping`; focused migration/backend/frontend, real service and
browser execution are complete. The repository-wide coverage gate remains
failed and Helm execution remains deferred by Peter.

### Test Boundary

- Requirement: `ROLE-002` in specification sections 4.2, 6.2.2-6.2.3, 7.4,
  7.6 and 8.4.
- Use real disposable PostgreSQL, Keycloak and OpenLDAP state under `TEST-002`.
  Do not pass mocks, fixture adapters, hard-coded success paths or permanent
  enterprise LDAP mutations as acceptance evidence.
- Preserve the standing Helm runtime-test deferral as a reported gap. Static
  deployment artifacts still require contract review after implementation.

### Migration And Data Contract

- `ROLE-002-M01`: a pristine database completes all forward migrations with
  only `system-admin` marked as the protected default; the three historical
  roles are absent and applied migration checksums remain unchanged.
- `ROLE-002-M02`: an upgrade database containing users, permissions, manual and
  external role membership preserves `project-owner`, `knowledge-editor` and
  `reviewer`, changes them to ordinary Local roles and loses no related rows.
- `ROLE-002-M03`: the known existing mappings keep `system-admin ->
  systemadmin`, remove `system-admin -> users`, immediately reconcile derived
  users and leave the LDAP `users` group and members untouched.
- `ROLE-002-M04`: another duplicate role/group mapping causes the migration to
  fail closed with an operator-safe reason before unique constraints are added.
- `ROLE-002-M05`: independent unique constraints reject a second role for one
  group and a second group for one role at the database boundary.
- `ROLE-002-M06`: `external_groups.identity_origin` accepts only the specified
  origins, and `role_users.source=break_glass` survives identity sync and
  manual membership replacement.

### Backend API And Domain Behavior

- `ROLE-002-B01`: view lists Local roles and groups with authoritative origin;
  only `/ldap/**` children are eligible, while `/ldap` and Keycloak-local
  `/system-admin` are rejected for mapping.
- `ROLE-002-B02`: role-scoped PUT maps, remaps and unmaps with the current
  `lock_version`, increments the version and returns the final mapping and
  derived-member count.
- `ROLE-002-B03`: stale versions, duplicate role ownership and duplicate group
  ownership return `409`; inactive/non-LDAP inputs return safe `404`/`422`;
  every failure leaves mapping, role users, version and audit state atomic.
- `ROLE-002-B04`: mapping rebuilds that role's `external_sync` rows in the same
  transaction. A forced real database constraint failure rolls back both the
  mapping and membership change.
- `ROLE-002-B05`: identity sync after an immediate mapping change converges to
  the same rows, retains `manual` and `break_glass`, and never clears the last
  successful result after an upstream failure.
- `ROLE-002-B06`: a user with both manual and LDAP-derived rows keeps both
  provenance records and one effective permission union; removing either source
  leaves the other effective.
- `ROLE-002-B07`: soft-deleting a normal Local role unmaps it, removes current
  LDAP-derived rows and preserves the role, manual rows, permissions and audit.
  Deleting, disabling or renaming `system-admin` is rejected.
- `ROLE-002-B08`: break-glass bootstrap creates or repairs only the protected
  source membership; role-user PUT cannot remove it, and LDAP mapping remains
  optional.
- `ROLE-002-B09`: `view`, `create`, `edit` and `delete` are exercised
  independently, including disabled users and unioned roles. Denials create no
  side effects and sensitive DN/token/credential values do not enter audit.
- `ROLE-002-B10`: the retired bulk mapping PUT is absent according to the
  recorded compatibility decision while mapping GET remains available.

### Keycloak And LDAP Integration

- `ROLE-002-I01`: deployment verification compares
  `KEYCLOAK_LDAP_GROUP_PATH` with the real mapper `groups.path`; mismatch fails
  closed before role origin is guessed or changed.
- `ROLE-002-I02`: moving the mapper root from `/` to `/ldap`, followed by a full
  sync, preserves LDAP group membership and stable DN identity, maps
  `systemadmin`, leaves `users` unmapped and keeps `/system-admin` local.
- `ROLE-002-I03`: mapper/sync failure does not deactivate prior groups or revoke
  prior successful role memberships; successful retry converges once and is
  idempotent.
- `ROLE-002-I04`: a deployment-protected, disabled-by-default break-glass user
  can obtain `system-admin` through real OIDC/MFA evidence without an LDAP group
  mapping, and lifecycle/audit controls remain those of `AUTH-004`.

### Frontend And Browser Behavior

- `ROLE-002-F01`: Local Roles and LDAP Groups are separate, accessible views;
  Local roles expose permission-appropriate actions and LDAP rows expose none
  of add/edit/delete/member-edit.
- `ROLE-002-F02`: the mapping dialog excludes groups mapped elsewhere, supports
  explicit unmap, submits role ID/group ID/current version once and refreshes
  authoritative state after `409`.
- `ROLE-002-F03`: normal role Delete shows the localized impact warning;
  `system-admin` has no rename/disable/delete control and backend rejection is
  still handled safely if called directly.
- `ROLE-002-F04`: role members display Manual, LDAP Group and Emergency
  Administrator text badges, including simultaneous Manual+LDAP badges on one
  person; LDAP Group and Emergency Administrator membership is checked and
  read-only, while manual-only membership remains selectable.
- `ROLE-002-F05`: loading, empty, forbidden, validation, conflict and service
  error states contain no fixture fallback and preserve unsaved modal state
  where safe.
- `ROLE-002-F06`: Traditional Chinese and English labels, focus order,
  dialog/alert semantics, non-color-only status, 40px mobile targets and
  desktop/mobile non-overlap pass component and real-browser checks.

## CHG-234 Identity Settings Truth, Directory Filter and Sync Recovery Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-15 with `ＯＫ`. Gate 3 test design
prepared on 2026-07-15. Gate 4 approved by Peter on 2026-07-15 with
`Peter approves CHG-234 Identity Settings Truth, Directory Filter and Sync
Recovery`; feature tests may execute.

Requirements under test: refined `AUTH-013`, new `AUTH-014` and `AUTH-015`,
with regression coverage for `AUTH-003`, `AUTH-012`, `SYS-001`, `SYS-002`,
`MOCK-006`, `DEPLOY-004`, `DEPLOY-006`, `SEC-001`, `I18N-002`, `I18N-003`
and `TEST-002`.

### Test Environment And Evidence

- Use disposable PostgreSQL schema/data, Redis queue namespace, Keycloak realm
  and frontend/sync clients, plus an isolated OpenLDAP subtree/provider. Do not
  modify permanent enterprise directory users or filters.
- Use a real Celery worker and Beat process for passing lifecycle cases. A
  deliberately stopped real worker is required for unavailable/timeout cases;
  mocks, eager tasks and hard-coded success adapters do not pass.
- Capture safe before/after hashes of Keycloak client redirects and LDAP
  component fields. Never print token, bind credential, full component payload
  or LDAP Filter original value in test output.
- Browser acceptance uses a disposable edit-capable identity and a view-only
  identity. Password/MFA input remains inside real Keycloak.
- Clean disposable realms, clients, providers, LDAP entries, Redis namespace,
  database rows and browser sessions after success or failure.

### Reauthentication And Deployment Cases

- `AUTH-013-R01`: a fresh bootstrap client contains exact normal and Identity
  Settings callbacks, exact Web Origin, public Standard Flow, PKCE S256 and
  disabled Direct Access Grant; no wildcard redirect exists.
- `AUTH-013-R02`: an existing compatible client missing only the reauth callback
  receives only that URI. Existing valid redirects/mappers remain byte-equal.
- `AUTH-013-R03`: wrong-origin, wildcard or incompatible client state fails
  bootstrap/readiness with a safe code and no partial destructive rewrite.
- `AUTH-013-R04`: real same-user fresh authentication returns through the exact
  callback, closes Popup/Modal and grants 10 minutes without page reload.
- `AUTH-013-R05`: cancel, close, provider unavailable, callback mismatch,
  different user, replay and expired flow remain locked and show distinct safe
  localized errors without raw provider values.

### Effective Settings And Provider Cases

- `AUTH-014-B01`: no current database row returns actual typed deployment OIDC
  and sync fields with `configuration_source=deployment`; secret is a boolean.
- `AUTH-014-B02`: a validated current row takes precedence and is labeled
  `database`; invalid/absent fields do not revive frontend defaults.
- `AUTH-014-B03`: Backend provider response exposes only ID, name, vendor,
  enabled, Filter, concurrency hash and safe evidence. Host, URL, DN, bind,
  credential, TLS/truststore and mapper fields are absent from JSON/log/audit.
- `AUTH-014-B04`: one real OpenLDAP provider returns one provider; adding an
  isolated AD-vendor provider returns two actual providers with one common sync
  policy and distinct Filters.
- `AUTH-014-B05`: unreachable Keycloak and missing provider return explicit
  unavailable/not-found evidence and never synthetic health or counts.

### LDAP Filter Cases

- `AUTH-014-L01`: accept representative RFC 4515 equality, presence, substring,
  AND, OR, NOT and escaped UTF-8 filters plus empty-value removal.
- `AUTH-014-L02`: reject unbalanced/multiple filters, invalid escape, NUL,
  control characters and more than 2,048 UTF-8 bytes with field-level 422 and
  no Keycloak mutation.
- `AUTH-014-L03`: view-only, missing fresh auth, expired grant, disabled user and
  lost edit permission return 403/423 with no component write.
- `AUTH-014-L04`: stale concurrency hash returns 409 and the latest provider
  summary; no operator change is overwritten.
- `AUTH-014-L05`: successful update changes only `customUserSearchFilter`,
  read-back matches and all other component fields equal the pre-change hash.
- `AUTH-014-L06`: Keycloak write failure, provider disappearance and read-back
  mismatch return safe errors and do not claim success; any compensating write
  preserves the latest externally changed fields.
- `AUTH-014-L07`: audit records actor, provider, result, old/new hash and length,
  with no raw Filter, component config, token or credential.

### Sync Migration And Lifecycle Cases

- `AUTH-015-M01`: fresh migration creates timestamp/heartbeat/lease constraints
  and indexes; rerun is idempotent under Flyway.
- `AUTH-015-M02`: populated upgrade backfills queued time from outbox/started
  evidence, preserves terminal runs/statistics and marks only truly stale active
  rows failed without deleting successful identity data.
- `AUTH-015-M03`: rollback documentation preserves new columns/history; no down
  migration truncates runs or identity data.
- `AUTH-015-B01`: healthy worker plus no active run returns one 202 run/outbox;
  duplicate concurrent requests produce one accepted run and structured 409s.
- `AUTH-015-B02`: zero worker heartbeat returns 503 and creates no run/outbox.
  Redis reachability alone cannot produce a healthy result.
- `AUTH-015-B03`: accepted task transitions queued -> running -> succeeded with
  timestamps/heartbeat and true reconciliation counts.
- `AUTH-015-B04`: queued beyond 300 seconds and running without heartbeat beyond
  1,800 seconds become failed with safe codes/audit; the next healthy request can
  queue a new run.
- `AUTH-015-B05`: duplicate delivery, worker crash/restart, retry and a late task
  carrying an old lease cannot run twice or overwrite terminal/current state.
- `AUTH-015-B06`: Keycloak unavailable/parser error marks only the current run
  failed and preserves the prior successful users, groups, roles and history.
- `AUTH-015-B07`: scheduled and manual queueing use the same stale-recovery and
  single-active-run transaction; Beat absence is visible separately from worker
  absence.

### Frontend And Browser Cases

- `AUTH-014-F01`: source contains no live-rendered `sso.nomosmart.local`,
  `Corporate LDAP`, fixed LDAP/AD user/group counts, fixed healthy/check time or
  unconditional secret-configured copy.
- `AUTH-014-F02`: loading, deployment/database source, unconfigured, unavailable
  and unknown states render from API evidence without fixture fallback.
- `AUTH-014-F03`: common enabled/scope/schedule/timezone controls render once;
  provider rows and Filter inputs match the actual provider count.
- `AUTH-014-F04`: Filter edit visibility follows edit permission plus unlock;
  syntax, conflict, unavailable and successful read-back states preserve focus
  and do not expose hidden component fields.
- `AUTH-015-F01`: manual sync immediately loads/disables, prevents duplicate
  submission, polls only its run, refreshes history and stops at terminal state.
- `AUTH-015-F02`: worker unavailable, active conflict, queue timeout, running
  timeout and Keycloak failure use distinct zh/en text, icon and retry behavior.
- `AUTH-015-F03`: desktop and narrow layouts avoid overlap, controls meet touch
  target requirements, status is not color-only and Popup focus returns to the
  trigger.

## CHG-235 AI Model Lifecycle, Pagination And Type Filter Test Design

Gate 2 was confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-15 with `ＯＫ`. Gate 4 was approved by
Peter on 2026-07-15 with
`Peter approves CHG-235 AI Model Lifecycle Pagination and Type Filter`.
Test cases remain planned until their commands and results are recorded.

### Migration And Data Integrity

- `MODEL-002-M01`: apply V029 to a real database containing active and inactive
  Chat, Embedding, OCR and Judge rows; verify UUIDs, credentials, defaults,
  configs, connection evidence and foreign keys remain unchanged before any
  explicit delete.
- `MODEL-002-M02`: verify fresh schema, upgrade and repeated Flyway validation
  create nullable `deleted_at` / `deleted_by`, the user foreign key and the
  active-row partial unique index exactly once.
- `MODEL-002-M03`: verify two non-deleted rows cannot share
  `name + model_type`; after one is tombstoned, a new UUID may reuse the pair
  while the historical row remains queryable directly for evidence.
- `MODEL-002-M04`: retain real historical document-version, completed Pipeline,
  Prompt-version and usage-event foreign keys after tombstoning; verify reports
  still resolve the historical model name and never expose credentials.
- `MODEL-002-M05`: record the rollback incompatibility once a name is reused and
  verify release/operations guidance does not claim an unsafe code-only rollback.

### Backend List And Pagination

- `MODEL-002-B01`: `GET /models` returns active and inactive rows, excludes every
  tombstone and preserves the array body contract.
- `MODEL-002-B02`: `X-Total-Count` equals the filtered authorized total before
  offset/limit, including zero results, and is visible through the live frontend
  route/proxy.
- `MODEL-002-B03`: offsets at 0, 20, last full page, partial last page and beyond
  the end return the correct rows with no duplicate or omitted IDs under stable
  `model_type, name, id` ordering.
- `MODEL-002-B04`: All/Chat/Embedding/OCR/Judge filters return only the requested
  type and matching totals; unknown/case-invalid type values fail validation
  rather than silently producing misleading data.
- `MODEL-002-B05`: permission union permits System Management and approved
  Knowledge Project selectors according to existing rules without leaking
  deleted rows or System Management-only dependency evidence.
- `MODEL-002-B06`: project creation, Prompt configuration and other selectors
  request sufficient active rows and do not become limited to the management
  table's default 20 rows.

### Backend Lifecycle And Security

- `MODEL-002-B07`: `PUT is_active=false` makes an active model inactive and
  keeps it listed; `PUT is_active=true` restores it. Both require edit and never
  set tombstone fields or clear credentials.
- `MODEL-002-B08`: a valid DELETE requires delete permission, exact
  `confirmation_name` and current `config_version`; missing/wrong name returns
  422, stale version returns 409 and all failure paths leave the row unchanged.
- `MODEL-002-B09`: an unreferenced delete atomically sets inactive/non-default,
  writes tombstone actor/time, clears encrypted key and Secret Ref, invalidates
  connection evidence and appends a redacted audit record.
- `MODEL-002-B10`: defaults, current project Chat/Embedding/OCR assignments,
  queued/running OCR Pipelines, active Chat pairings and active model Prompt each
  return 409 with only authorized dependency category/count details and no
  partial state, credential, UUID-list or unauthorized project-name leakage.
- `MODEL-002-B11`: completed/failed Pipeline, historical document version,
  inactive/historical Prompt and usage-event references do not block soft delete
  and remain intact afterward.
- `MODEL-002-B12`: deleting an Embedding model removes it from inactive Chat
  configs in the same transaction; active Chat pairing or any zero-valid-pair
  result blocks the transaction.
- `MODEL-002-B13`: list/update/test/set-default/enable/disable/repeated-delete on
  a tombstone consistently returns the specified not-found/gone safety response
  without model contents.
- `MODEL-002-B14`: a concurrent assignment/default/pairing or config edit between
  Modal open and delete is caught by row lock/version/dependency revalidation;
  one transaction succeeds or both fail safely, never an invalid partial state.
- `MODEL-002-B15`: audit/log/error/metrics inspection contains no API key,
  Secret Ref value, authorization header or unrestricted dependency identifiers.

### Frontend Behavior And Accessibility

- `MODEL-002-F01`: first entry to the Models Tab requests page 1 with 20 rows,
  renders total/result range and does not render more than 20 body rows.
- `MODEL-002-F02`: selecting 50 or 100 reloads from Backend, resets to page 1 and
  maintains a stable table while loading; invalid/missing total is an explicit
  error instead of fabricated pagination.
- `MODEL-002-F03`: All, Chat, Embedding, OCR and Judge selections call Backend,
  reset to page 1 and render filtered empty/loading/error states correctly.
- `MODEL-002-F04`: previous/next and page indicators handle first, middle, last,
  zero and one-page results; deleting the sole last-page row returns to the
  previous valid page.
- `MODEL-002-F05`: active rows expose Disable and Delete as independent commands;
  inactive rows expose Enable and Delete. Disable/Enable call PUT, Delete calls
  DELETE, and permission-disabled commands cannot mutate state.
- `MODEL-002-F06`: Delete opens the shared popup Modal with Trash icon,
  destructive styling, consequences, credential revocation, model metadata and
  exact-name input; confirm remains disabled until the name matches.
- `MODEL-002-F07`: 409 dependency data is rendered as clear category/count and
  remediation guidance inside the Modal; 403/404/409/422/network errors preserve
  the current row/page and do not show a fake success message.
- `MODEL-002-F08`: deleted rows disappear after successful refresh from the
  management table, Project/Prompt/Pipeline selectors and Chat pairing choices;
  inactive rows remain visible only where lifecycle administration requires.
- `MODEL-002-F09`: zh/en keys align for labels, filters, page sizes, result range,
  lifecycle states, confirmation, dependency conflicts, errors, aria labels and
  tooltips; no hard-coded user-facing copy is introduced.
- `MODEL-002-F10`: keyboard focus, Escape/cancel, label association, alert/live
  regions, non-color state cues, 40px narrow targets, table horizontal scrolling
  and desktop/narrow layouts pass Browser inspection without overlap.

### Live Acceptance And Cleanup

- Use an authenticated Peter System Management session against the configured
  Backend and real PostgreSQL. Create isolated `codex-live-chg235-*` models only.
- Prove disable remains visible, enable restores, type filtering and 20/50/100
  paging use live HTTP results, and one unreferenced model disappears after
  exact-name delete while direct authorized historical evidence remains.
- Create a bounded current-reference conflict and verify 409/no partial mutation;
  remove the test relation and delete the isolated model.
- Run repository test-data cleanup and verify no CHG-235 model, Prompt, pairing,
  audit helper row or credential remains beyond audit evidence explicitly
  required by the product contract.

## CHG-236 Identity Reauthentication Popup Lifecycle Repair Test Design

Gate 2 was confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-15 with `ＯＫ`. Gate 4 was approved by
Peter on 2026-07-15 with
`Peter approves CHG-236 Identity Reauthentication Popup Lifecycle Repair`.
These cases are approved for implementation and verification.

### Frontend Lifecycle Cases

- `AUTH-013-L01`: with one active locale, an unrelated render of a real frontend
  page retains the same `t` and `format` callback identities and translations;
  changing locale updates the translated values without stale-locale output.
- `AUTH-013-L02`: opening reauthentication and changing status from `ready` to
  `opening` and `waiting` must not call `close()` through message-listener Effect
  cleanup; only the event listener may be replaced or removed.
- `AUTH-013-L03`: actual workspace unmount, explicit Modal dismissal, timeout,
  callback error/cancel and successful completion each clear the current Popup,
  interval and timeout exactly once.
- `AUTH-013-L04`: starting a retry clears stale watchers and replaces the prior
  Popup reference; a late message from the old window fails the existing exact
  source check and cannot unlock or close the current attempt.
- `AUTH-013-L05`: blocked or genuinely user-closed Popup returns the Modal to an
  actionable localized error state, preserves the locked settings and restores
  keyboard focus to the initiating control.

### Live Keycloak And Browser Cases

- `AUTH-013-E01`: as an authenticated edit-capable Peter user against the real
  frontend, Backend and Keycloak, click the confirmation action and verify the
  Popup remains open beyond initial rendering, navigates from the same-origin
  waiting page to Keycloak and displays Keycloak-owned credential controls.
- `AUTH-013-E02`: complete fresh authentication as the same user and verify the
  fixed callback posts only the enumerated result, the existing complete API
  succeeds, the Popup closes and the original `/system` page unlocks without a
  full-page reload or navigation.
- `AUTH-013-E03`: close the real Keycloak Popup before completion and verify the
  original page remains locked, reports the localized closed state and can open
  one functional retry Popup.
- `AUTH-013-E04`: cancel at Keycloak where supported and verify the safe
  cancelled result remains distinct from success; no flow row gains an
  authenticated/completion value and no unlock grant is issued.
- `AUTH-013-E05`: leave the Identity Settings workspace with a Popup open and
  verify teardown closes the Popup and watchers without affecting ordinary
  login, silent SSO or session-expiry recovery.

### Security And Regression Cases

- `AUTH-013-S01`: NomoSmart pages, API requests, logs and audit continue to
  contain no password, OTP, authorization code, token, state, nonce or raw
  provider error; credential input remains Keycloak-owned.
- `AUTH-013-S02`: event origin and source mismatch, wrong user/session,
  permission removal, replay and expired flow remain fail-closed under the
  existing Backend tests.
- `AUTH-013-R06`: the current CHG-230 source assertions remain guardrails only;
  acceptance requires the rendered lifecycle and live cases above so a future
  Effect-cleanup regression cannot pass on string presence alone.

## CHG-237 Local Role Lifecycle And Card UX Test Design

Gate 2 was confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-15 with `1A, 2B, 3B, 4A`. Gate 3 test
design is recorded below. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-07-15 with
`Peter approves CHG-237 Local Role Lifecycle and Card UX`; implementation and
feature-test execution may proceed against this approved scope.

### Migration And Data Integrity

- `ROLE-003-M01`: V030 upgrades real active and inactive roles without changing
  their IDs, status, mapping, manual/external membership, permissions or audit.
- `ROLE-003-M02`: fresh install, V029 upgrade and repeated Flyway validation
  create nullable tombstone columns, user foreign key, inactive-tombstone check
  and undeleted-name partial unique index exactly once.
- `ROLE-003-M03`: two undeleted roles cannot share a name; after one is soft
  deleted a new UUID may reuse the exact name while all historical relations
  remain attached only to the old UUID.
- `ROLE-003-M04`: a tombstone with `is_active=true` is rejected and a failed
  migration or constraint violation rolls back without partial schema/data.
- `ROLE-003-M05`: migration/release documentation records the unsafe legacy
  code-only rollback once a deleted name has been reused.

### Backend Lifecycle And Authorization

- `ROLE-003-B01`: `GET /roles` returns undeleted active and inactive roles in
  stable order and excludes every tombstone from list, counts and selectors.
- `ROLE-003-B02`: active metadata editing remains edit-permission guarded; a
  lifecycle transition mixed with name/description returns 422 without change.
- `ROLE-003-B03`: standalone disable requires edit, correct `lock_version`, row
  and advisory locks; it retains/reserves the mapping, removes `external_sync`,
  preserves manual/permissions and writes redacted `role.disable` audit.
- `ROLE-003-B04`: disabled role metadata, manual-member, permission and mapping
  writes each return `inactive_role_read_only`, while their view routes remain
  available to a view-authorized administrator.
- `ROLE-003-B05`: standalone enable requires edit and current version, retains
  the mapped group, immediately rebuilds `external_sync` from current
  `external_group_users` and writes `role.enable` without stale members.
- `ROLE-003-B06`: identity sync concurrent with disable/enable serializes under
  the shared advisory lock; final mapping and membership match exactly one valid
  lifecycle state with no duplicate or partial `role_users` rows.
- `ROLE-003-B07`: Delete requires delete permission plus query parameters for
  current `lock_version` and exact case-sensitive `confirmation_name`; missing
  or wrong values return 422 and a stale version returns 409 with no partial
  mutation. A JSON/body-only confirmation is not accepted.
- `ROLE-003-B08`: valid Delete on an active or inactive role atomically writes
  actor/time tombstone and inactive state, releases mapping, removes derived
  members, increments version and emits `role.delete`, while retaining metadata,
  manual membership, permissions and historical references.
- `ROLE-003-B09`: repeat Delete and normal read/update/member/permission/mapping
  access to a tombstone return the specified safe not-found response without
  exposing deleted contents.
- `ROLE-003-B10`: after Delete, another role can map the released LDAP group and
  a newly created same-name role has a new UUID and no inherited members,
  permissions, mapping or audit identity.
- `ROLE-003-B11`: every disable/delete attempt for `system-admin`, including a
  direct API call with edit/delete permission, is rejected and changes nothing.
- `ROLE-003-B12`: effective permission union ignores inactive/tombstoned roles;
  re-enable restores only current manual/break-glass and freshly reconciled LDAP
  sources without double-counting a user with multiple sources.
- `ROLE-003-B13`: database uniqueness/concurrency errors, mapping release and
  audit failures roll back the complete lifecycle transaction.
- `ROLE-003-B14`: logs, audit summaries and errors contain no token, credential,
  full LDAP DN or unrestricted user lists; lifecycle metrics use bounded IDs and
  counts only.

### Frontend Card And Interaction

- `ROLE-003-F01`: Local-role search matches name/description; All/Enabled/
  Disabled filtering and result count compose correctly and deleted rows never
  appear as cards, options or counts.
- `ROLE-003-F02`: active card header shows icon, wrapping name, status text and
  Switch; normal cards omit redundant Local badge and system-admin alone shows
  protected status with non-operable lifecycle control.
- `ROLE-003-F03`: mapping and manual/LDAP/break-glass counts render as unframed
  metadata rows rather than a nested card; long paths/names wrap or truncate
  accessibly without resizing controls.
- `ROLE-003-F04`: active role exposes Edit, Users and Mapping icon+text commands;
  Delete appears only in the labelled keyboard-accessible Ellipsis menu and is
  absent for `system-admin` or users without delete permission.
- `ROLE-003-F05`: switching active to disabled opens a confirmation dialog with
  permission/mapping consequences; cancel preserves state, confirm prevents
  double submit and refreshes Backend truth on success/conflict/error.
- `ROLE-003-F06`: disabled card remains readable, Switch can enable, and detail,
  member, permission and mapping views are read-only; no edit control or Modal
  can submit a write. Delete remains available when authorized.
- `ROLE-003-F07`: enabling shows stable per-card loading, calls standalone PUT,
  refreshes mapped/member counts and reports localized success/error without
  card-grid layout shift.
- `ROLE-003-F08`: Delete alertdialog contains role/status/mapping/member impact,
  exact-name label/input, Trash icon, destructive command and disabled confirm
  until exact match; Escape/cancel restores focus to Ellipsis.
- `ROLE-003-F09`: successful Delete waits for Backend refresh before the card
  disappears; 403/404/409/422/network failures retain the card/input and render
  a safe actionable error rather than fake success.
- `ROLE-003-F10`: no nested cards, status-by-text-not-color, visible hover/focus,
  reduced motion, 40px narrow touch targets, aligned zh/en keys and no hard-coded
  Traditional Chinese outside locale files.
- `ROLE-003-F11`: 1440/1024/768/375px Browser checks prove three/two/one-column
  behavior as applicable, no horizontal overflow, no overlapping text/actions
  and usable toolbar/menu/dialog focus order.

### Live Acceptance And Cleanup

- `ROLE-003-E01`: create an isolated mapped `codex-live-chg237-*` role in real
  PostgreSQL/Keycloak/LDAP, disable it through authenticated UI/API and verify
  visible read-only state, retained mapping and absent effective derived access.
- `ROLE-003-E02`: change real test-group membership or reconcile the current
  snapshot, re-enable the role and verify immediate current membership rather
  than the pre-disable snapshot.
- `ROLE-003-E03`: exact-name soft delete the isolated role, verify normal API/UI
  absence and mapping availability, recreate the same name under a new UUID and
  prove historical isolation.
- `ROLE-003-E04`: run the existing Peter/John governance and system-admin paths
  to prove protected access and unrelated project/review behavior did not
  regress, then remove all CHG-237 non-audit test rows and external artifacts.

## CHG-238 Identity Reauthentication Same-tab Redirect And System Tab Persistence Test Design

Gate 2 was confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-15 with `ＯＫ`. Gate 3 test design is
recorded below. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-07-15 with
`Peter approves CHG-238 Identity Reauthentication Same-tab Redirect and System Tab Persistence`.

### System Tab URL Cases

- `SYS-004-F01`: each allowlisted `tab` value renders the matching selected Tab
  and panel on the first server/hydration render without first exposing users.
- `SYS-004-F02`: mouse selection and Arrow/Home/End keyboard selection update
  component selection, focus and the canonical `tab` query without reloading.
- `SYS-004-F03`: Tab selection uses replace semantics; browser Back does not
  traverse earlier Tab clicks and unrelated safe query parameters are retained.
- `SYS-004-F04`: reload and a directly pasted URL retain each representative
  Tab, including roles, models, identity and parameters.
- `SYS-004-F05`: missing, repeated, array-like, case-invalid and unknown Tab
  values select users and canonicalize to exactly one `tab=users` value.
- `SYS-004-F06`: source and runtime evidence contain no localStorage,
  sessionStorage, cookie or Backend write for active Tab persistence.
- `SYS-004-F07`: switching away from an unlocked Identity Tab still invokes the
  existing lock behavior before changing URL; ordinary locked Tab changes make
  no lock request.
- `SYS-004-F08`: reload preserves only the top-level Tab; searches, pagination,
  unsaved forms and Modals are not serialized into the URL or storage.

### Same-tab Frontend Cases

- `AUTH-013-T01`: edit-capable users retain the confirmation Modal; its command
  starts the live reauth API and uses current-tab navigation, with no
  `window.open`, opener, postMessage, close polling or iframe.
- `AUTH-013-T02`: before navigating, the current URL is canonicalized to
  `tab=identity&reauth=pending`; only allowlisted enums are written and the
  authorization URL is supplied by the Backend.
- `AUTH-013-T03`: after returning with `success`, the protected route completes
  normal silent SSO/token installation first, preserves the full query return
  path and calls complete exactly once.
- `AUTH-013-T04`: complete success removes only `reauth`, retains identity,
  closes the Modal, renders the Backend expiry and enables authorized controls.
- `AUTH-013-T05`: fabricated success, missing completion cookie, wrong user/
  session, replay, expiry and permission removal never set local unlock state.
- `AUTH-013-T06`: cancelled and error results return to identity, remove the
  transient result, stay locked and show distinct localized retry feedback.
- `AUTH-013-T07`: browser Back/pageshow to pending converts to an interrupted
  locked state, removes pending and allows one fresh retry without a loop.
- `AUTH-013-T08`: start failure never navigates; silent-SSO or complete failure
  uses existing session/account recovery where applicable and otherwise remains
  a safe locked error.
- `AUTH-013-T09`: `/auth/identity-reauth` accepts only the legacy enumerated
  result and server-redirects to the canonical System URL; invalid/missing input
  becomes error and no client Popup script runs.
- `AUTH-013-T10`: zh/en text says the current tab will continue to Keycloak and
  contains no promise of a Popup, local password input or unchanged-page flow.

### Backend Callback And Security Cases

- `AUTH-013-B01`: start keeps the existing authorization URL contract, exact
  callback, prompt/max_age/state/nonce/PKCE and stores the new success return
  path without code/token/state/nonce in it.
- `AUTH-013-B02`: callback success sets the same one-time HttpOnly completion
  cookie and redirects only to `tab=identity&reauth=success`.
- `AUTH-013-B03`: access_denied maps to cancelled; malformed/provider/AppError
  outcomes map to error; raw provider values are absent from URL/log/audit.
- `AUTH-013-B04`: complete still requires current edit permission and matching
  user/subject/session/scope/fresh auth_time; valid consumption grants ten
  minutes and replay fails closed.
- `AUTH-013-B05`: pre-upgrade flows whose stored return path references the old
  result route reach the canonical System result through the compatibility shim
  without changing database rows or callback registration.

### Live Browser Acceptance

- `AUTH-013-E06`: authenticated Peter selects identity, sees the canonical URL,
  continues in the same tab to real Keycloak and no second tab/window appears.
- `AUTH-013-E07`: valid fresh authentication returns through normal auth
  recovery, consumes completion, removes the transient query and unlocks the
  same System page for ten minutes.
- `AUTH-013-E08`: Keycloak cancel or browser Back returns to a locked identity
  state with retry; retry creates one new flow and reaches Keycloak once.
- `SYS-004-E01`: after each representative Tab click, reload and direct URL
  opening retain the Tab at desktop and narrow widths without content flash,
  overlap or focus regression.

## CHG-239 Knowledge Project Archive Lifecycle And Unfinished Content Purge Test Design

Gate 2 was confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-16. Gate 3 test design is recorded
below. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-07-16 with
`Peter approves CHG-239 Knowledge Project Archive Lifecycle and Unfinished Content Purge`.

### Lifecycle And List Cases

- `PROJECT-004-F01`: `/projects` renders exactly 「專案清單」 and 「已封存」
  (plus aligned English), defaults active and contains none of the superseded
  all/active/processing labels.
- `PROJECT-004-F02`: each Tab requests the corresponding live Backend status,
  applies loading/empty/error/retry independently and never client-filters a
  partial mixed list.
- `PROJECT-004-F03`: active cards remain navigable; archived cards contain no
  Link or action into project, chat, graph, documents, members or settings.
- `PROJECT-004-F04`: only a current Owner sees Archive; opening it loads live
  impact and shows irreversible/Public API warnings plus retained/deleted counts.
- `PROJECT-004-F05`: confirmation is disabled until the exact Project name
  matches; submit is single-flight; stale/name/permission/error stays on page
  with safe localized feedback.
- `PROJECT-004-F06`: accepted archive removes the active card, exposes an
  archived-list result and displays cleanup state without a third lifecycle.
- `PROJECT-004-F07`: desktop/tablet/mobile card and Modal layouts are accessible,
  keyboard operable and free of text/control overlap.

### API, Permission And Concurrency Cases

- `PROJECT-004-B01`: list defaults active; explicit active/archived filters run
  before pagination and preserve scope; invalid/repeated values return 422.
- `PROJECT-004-B02`: impact/archive require visible Project plus current Owner;
  non-Owner/removed Owner/unauthorized callers fail without mutation.
- `PROJECT-004-B03`: exact name and current lock version are required; mismatch/
  stale requests return specified errors without archive or dispatch.
- `PROJECT-004-B04`: archive metadata, schedule disablement, Integration Client
  scope revocation, one cleanup run/outbox and audit commit atomically.
- `PROJECT-004-B05`: duplicate idempotent submission returns the same safe result;
  concurrent requests create one cleanup run and no partial state.
- `PROJECT-004-B06`: legacy DELETE cannot bypass confirmation; no PUT/direct
  status or restore endpoint returns archived to active.
- `PROJECT-004-B07`: authorized first-party archived access returns
  `project_archived`; unauthorized remains 404; every Project read, mutation,
  file, review, publish, graph, chat, sync and compatibility route is covered.
- `PROJECT-004-B08`: Public API JSON/SSE returns safe 404 before retrieval,
  model/provider use or new request-content persistence.

### Migration And Classification Cases

- `PROJECT-004-M01`: V031 fresh/upgrade adds archive metadata, lifecycle
  constraint, cleanup table/indexes and preserves existing active data.
- `PROJECT-004-M02`: illegal historical status is rejected/reconciled; rerun,
  checksum and schema rollback behave as documented without data-restore claims.
- `PROJECT-004-C01`: published active/inactive versions retain PostgreSQL, source/
  derived objects and formal serving artifacts.
- `PROJECT-004-C02`: draft/quarantine/queued/running/processing/submission-ready,
  review-pending, approved-unpublished, rejected, failed, cancelled and malformed
  unpublished active/inactive versions are purge candidates.
- `PROJECT-004-C03`: mixed Document retains completed versions and deletes only
  unfinished versions; no-completed-version Document is fully deleted.
- `PROJECT-004-C04`: staging chat/validation, approval/review, Pipeline/steps,
  scans/sync/graph/outbox, chunks/tags/embeddings and notifications/references
  tied to purge versions are deleted without dangling FK/JSON IDs.
- `PROJECT-004-C05`: shared Tag and S3 object references used by retained content
  survive; purge-only orphans are removed.

### Live Cross-store Cleanup Cases

- `PROJECT-004-I01`: real S3/RustFS purge objects are absent while retained
  completed-version objects remain byte-identical.
- `PROJECT-004-I02`: real OpenSearch purge staging/version IDs and unpublished
  vectors are absent; completed published artifacts remain but archived retrieval
  returns no application hits.
- `PROJECT-004-I03`: real Neo4j preview/unpublished relations are absent; retained
  completed graph remains physical but unavailable through archived APIs.
- `PROJECT-004-I04`: provider outage produces failed/retryable cleanup; retry
  completes without retained-data damage or double counting.
- `PROJECT-004-I05`: completion requires external absence verification and
  PostgreSQL integrity checks, not only queued task/adapter success.

### Worker And Audit Cases

- `PROJECT-004-W01`: queued work cancels before claim; claimed work rechecks
  before external/final write and cannot recreate data.
- `PROJECT-004-W02`: stale lease recovery is idempotent; simultaneous cleanup
  workers cannot own one run.
- `PROJECT-004-W03`: late Celery/outbox completion after purge cannot recreate
  rows, objects, indices or graph nodes.
- `PROJECT-004-S01`: audit/cleanup evidence retains actor/time/UUID/count/hash/
  result only, with no document/chunk/question content, credential, token, object
  body or raw provider error.
- `PROJECT-004-S02`: completed Public API logs obey retention/legal hold; new
  requests after archive create no answer/citation data.

### Browser Acceptance

- `PROJECT-004-E01`: Peter archives a disposable mixed-version Project, reviews
  impact, enters exact name and sees immediate archived placement plus cleanup;
  John/non-Owner never receives the action.
- `PROJECT-004-E02`: archived card cannot be entered at desktop/narrow widths;
  direct old URL returns archived handling and archived-list navigation.
- `PROJECT-004-E03`: configured Public API JSON/SSE loses access immediately;
  retained and purge objects are respectively present/absent after cleanup.
- `PROJECT-004-E04`: controlled provider interruption shows failed/retry and
  keeps Project unusable, then completes without retained-data damage.
