## CHG-241 Project Archive Execute Permission And Project Card Discovery UX Test Design

Gate 2 was confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-16. Gate 3 test design is recorded
below. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-07-16 with
`Peter approves CHG-241 Project Archive Execute Permission and Project Card Discovery UX`.

Requirements under test: `PERM-004`, `PROJECT-005`, and unchanged destructive
behavior from `PROJECT-004`.

### Migration And Permission Model

- `PERM-004-M01`: V032 fresh/upgrade creates non-null default-false
  `can_execute`; every existing permission value and role membership is
  byte/row-equivalent except the new column.
- `PERM-004-M02`: only active `system-admin` receives
  `Project.ProjectArchive.can_execute=true`; existing/custom/project-owner/
  knowledge-editor/reviewer roles remain false unless later granted.
- `PERM-004-M03`: Flyway checksum/rerun passes, rollback warning is documented,
  and code does not reinterpret execute as delete.
- `PERM-004-B01`: auth/me and grant union serialize/resolve execute; multiple
  active roles use OR semantics while inactive, deleted or removed memberships
  do not grant it.
- `PERM-004-B02`: permission matrix GET/PUT round-trips the three Menu rows plus
  ProjectArchive; only the exact supported actions persist and all disabled
  cells normalize false.
- `PERM-004-B03`: duplicate/unknown module/function or unsupported execute on a
  Menu row returns 422 without partial replacement; unrelated historical
  non-managed rows survive a managed-matrix save.
- `PERM-004-B04`: stale role lock returns 409, missing System edit returns 403,
  and audit records actor/changed key/result without tokens or group claims.

### Archive Authorization

- `PERM-004-A01`: a visible Project Owner can impact/archive/retry without a
  global execute grant, preserving inherent governance authority.
- `PERM-004-A02`: a visible non-Owner with active Execute and Knowledge Projects
  view can impact/archive/retry using the unchanged name/lock contract.
- `PERM-004-A03`: a visible non-Owner without Execute receives 403 and no Project,
  run, outbox, scope, schedule, credential or audit-success mutation occurs.
- `PERM-004-A04`: Execute without Knowledge Projects view, disabled account or
  outside membership/scope cannot disclose or archive the Project; outside
  scope remains safe 404.
- `PERM-004-A05`: removing/disablement of the granting role between impact and
  submit denies submit; stale Frontend visibility cannot bypass current Backend
  permission.
- `PERM-004-A06`: legacy DELETE still cannot archive; exact confirmation,
  optimistic lock, idempotency, cleanup and no-restore behavior remain unchanged.

### Project List Query And Summary

- `PROJECT-005-B01`: q searches scoped name/description case-insensitively,
  trims whitespace, escapes `%`, `_` and backslash, rejects over-limit input and
  never searches outside visible scope.
- `PROJECT-005-B02`: repeated owner/editor/viewer role filters use OR and validate
  enum values; multi-role members appear once.
- `PROJECT-005-B03`: complete requires non-null Chat/Embedding/OCR ids;
  incomplete returns any missing model and combines correctly with status,
  search and role filters.
- `PROJECT-005-B04`: updated descending/ascending and name ascending/descending
  are deterministic with UUID tie-break; invalid/repeated singleton values
  return 422.
- `PROJECT-005-B05`: `X-Total-Count` equals post-scope/filter and pre-pagination
  rows for nonempty and zero results, is CORS-exposed, and existing array-body
  clients remain compatible.
- `PROJECT-005-B06`: offset/12-limit pages have no duplicates/gaps under stable
  data; changing a predicate produces the expected first page and total.
- `PROJECT-005-B07`: summary exposes only current-user Project roles, correct
  retained document count, PROJECT-004 published active/inactive count and true
  max persisted activity with Project fallback.
- `PROJECT-005-P01`: representative query plan/index use is bounded and one list
  request does not issue per-card document/version/role queries.

### Permission Matrix Frontend

- `PERM-004-F01`: matrix displays the bilingual Execute column and Project
  Archive row; only its Execute checkbox is enabled, and every permission label
  remains visually separated from its compact help text.
- `PERM-004-F02`: existing Menu row labels, supported checkboxes, values and save
  behavior are unchanged; Execute cells there are disabled/false.
- `PERM-004-F03`: selecting roles loads independent values; toggling/saving uses
  live API, lock version and read-back, with unsaved/403/409/error states.
- `PERM-004-F04`: inactive role remains read-only and keyboard/screen-reader
  labels identify role, permission row and Execute action.

### Project Card And Discovery Frontend

- `PROJECT-005-F01`: card renders live name, last activity, authority badge,
  two-line description, document/published/model metrics, state and actions with
  no fixture count/time.
- `PROJECT-005-F02`: badge priority is Owner, Archive Permission, Editor, Viewer;
  Owner and Execute users see text+icon Archive, unauthorized members have no
  button or placeholder, and all retain the Enter action for active Projects.
- `PROJECT-005-F03`: Archive loads the existing impact API directly, preserves
  irreversible/name/lock/busy/error states and introduces no extra confirm step.
- `PROJECT-005-F04`: search debounces 300ms, supports clear/loading/no-match,
  cancels/ignores stale responses and resets page one.
- `PROJECT-005-F05`: Filter popover supports role multiselect, model-state single
  selection, apply/clear/count, Escape/outside close/focus return and combines
  params correctly.
- `PROJECT-005-F06`: sort offers the four specified modes, defaults Recent Update,
  persists through page navigation and resets page one when changed.
- `PROJECT-005-F07`: 12-card pagination uses live total, is hidden for one page,
  exposes current/total page accessibly and handles the current page becoming
  invalid after filter/archive.
- `PROJECT-005-F08`: archived cards remain non-enterable; cleanup state is clear;
  failed retry is visible only to Owner/Execute and uses the same guard.
- `PROJECT-005-F09`: no-project and no-filter-match states differ; clearing active
  criteria restores results without a full page reload.
- `PROJECT-005-F10`: AppShell/Menu component markup, navigation order, icons,
  geometry and responsive behavior are unchanged by source and screenshot
  regression.

### Responsive And Browser Acceptance

- `PROJECT-005-E01`: at 1440/1024/768/375 widths, long zh/en title, description,
  badges, three metrics and one/two actions have no overlap, cutoff, horizontal
  page scroll or layout shift; cards are two columns then one column.
- `PROJECT-005-E02`: keyboard users can search, open/apply/clear Filter, change
  sort/page, enter a Project and open/close archive impact with visible focus;
  reduced motion and 40px mobile targets are respected.
- `PROJECT-005-E03`: authenticated Peter Owner, a disposable non-Owner granted
  Execute and a non-authorized member observe the three exact action states;
  grant/revoke is reflected after auth refresh and Backend denial is immediate.
- `PROJECT-005-E04`: live search/filter/sort/page combinations match PostgreSQL
  truth and total header; no console error, fixture fallback or stale-response
  reversal occurs.
- `PROJECT-005-E05`: a disposable authorized non-Owner completes the unchanged
  CHG-239 archive flow and physical cleanup; all destructive evidence and test
  data are cleaned after the run.

### Package CLI And Secret Generation

- `DEPLOY-007-C01`: fresh `init` creates one generation, safe state metadata,
  directory mode `0700` and secret-file mode no wider than `0600` without
  writing a plaintext receipt.
- `C02`: all password/client/encryption values satisfy their typed format and
  entropy requirements and are pairwise distinct; usernames are not treated as
  Secret values.
- `C03`: development plus explicit `factory_acceptance` produces break-glass
  username/password `nomosmart / nomosmart` and marks it temporary; no other
  service receives that password.
- `C04`: production, missing profile, contradictory APP_ENV/profile,
  placeholder, empty, `nomosmart` password, repeated Secret or derived value is
  rejected before any resource or existing file changes.
- `C05`: a second `init` returns the same safe generation/status without
  redisplaying values or overwriting files. Explicit `rotate` creates a new
  generation and retains the previous one until verification.
- `C06`: interruption before atomic rename leaves no partial credential set;
  retry is safe. Existing foreign files/symlinks and permissive paths fail
  closed.
- `C07`: one-time output requires an interactive TTY, appears once after
  successful generation and includes service, username, temporary status and
  reference. Redirected output/CI/log/status JSON never contains values.
- `C08`: direct password-manager/Vault or Kubernetes Secret delivery produces
  the same fingerprint inventory without exposing `--from-literal`, command
  arguments, shell trace or temporary plaintext artifact.

### Compose And Typed Configuration

- `DEPLOY-007-D01`: committed Compose/env examples contain only placeholders,
  usernames, non-sensitive settings and Secret references; real generated
  values remain ignored.
- `D02`: each service receives only its declared `/run/secrets` files. Frontend,
  edge, ClamAV and unrelated workloads cannot read database, OIDC, storage,
  search or graph credentials.
- `D03`: Backend/worker/Beat/bootstrap typed `_FILE` resolution accepts
  correctly permissioned files, rejects missing/empty/symlink/conflicting
  values in production and never includes values in validation errors.
- `D04`: wrappers for upstream environment-only images disable tracing, read
  only declared files and do not expose values through rendered Compose,
  healthchecks, process arguments or container logs.
- `D05`: `docker compose config`, support-bundle/status output and failure logs
  contain Secret names/fingerprints only. A bounded scanner checks every
  generated value against captured stdout/stderr and artifacts.

### Peripheral Identity And Least Privilege

- `DEPLOY-007-I01`: fresh PostgreSQL contains separate `postgres`,
  `nomosmart-migration`, `nomosmart` and Keycloak roles; only the intended
  bootstrap/admin role is superuser. Flyway owns migration/schema work,
  application DML succeeds and app DDL/admin-database access fails.
- `I02`: Redis rejects anonymous/no-password and wrong-password clients;
  `nomosmart-service` supports required broker/result operations without admin
  commands not required by the application.
- `I03`: RustFS accepts only the generated `nomosmart` access pair for required
  buckets; wrong/old secrets fail after verified rotation.
- `I04`: OpenSearch bootstrap admin creates/verifies `nomosmart-service` with
  bounded index/health access. App containers lack the admin Secret and cannot
  perform security-admin operations.
- `I05`: Neo4j initial `neo4j` admin creates/verifies `nomosmart-service` with
  required database access. App containers lack the initial admin Secret and
  unauthorized DBMS administration fails.
- `I06`: Keycloak `kc-bootstrap-admin` creates the realm/clients/service
  account, then is disabled after `nomosmart-sync` bounded management is
  verified. Upgrade bootstrap remains possible without restoring a shared
  permanent human admin password.
- `I07`: ClamAV/Nginx render and run without invented credential fields.

### Break-glass Onboarding And Finalization

- `AUTH-016-B01`: empty bundled Keycloak onboarding creates exactly one local
  `nomosmart` account, disabled self-registration, `/system-admin` membership,
  temporary password and required `UPDATE_PASSWORD` plus `CONFIGURE_TOTP`.
- `B02`: factory acceptance performs real browser OIDC login using
  `nomosmart / nomosmart`, cannot enter NomoSmart before completing required
  actions, then changes password, configures real TOTP and receives System
  Admin authorization through normal JWT/user synchronization.
- `B03`: production one-time output supplies a generated temporary password;
  the fixed factory value is rejected at CLI, config-schema and bootstrap
  boundaries.
- `B04`: NomoSmart requests, browser storage, callback URL, Keycloak Theme,
  Backend logs, audit, installer status and support artifacts contain neither
  temporary/new password nor OTP seed/code.
- `B05`: LDAP absent leaves deployment explicitly `onboarding`; administrator
  login works, but federation/operational readiness remains false and no fake
  provider/sync result is created.
- `B06`: production `finalize` fails without any one of successful OIDC login,
  completed password action, TOTP credential, protected role, one valid LDAP
  provider/group mapper, successful initial sync or a non-break-glass active
  System Admin. Failure does not disable the only admin.
- `B07`: after all real evidence exists, finalize disables `nomosmart`, revokes
  sessions/tokens as applicable, removes initial credential delivery, records
  only safe evidence and marks operational. Old session and both old/updated
  break-glass passwords cannot start a new application session.
- `B08`: emergency re-enable uses a new random temporary credential, alert/runbook
  evidence and the same required actions; use and second disable are audited
  without secrets. NomoSmart System Management remains read-only.

### Zero-to-login Compose Acceptance

- `DEPLOY-007-E01`: from a unique project name and empty volumes, `init` plus the
  documented Compose command builds/pulls all pinned images and starts the real
  PostgreSQL, Redis, RustFS, OpenSearch, Neo4j, Keycloak and ClamAV stack.
- `E02`: Flyway applies V001..V032 once, onboarding bootstrap succeeds without
  LDAP production claims, edge exposes only 80/443 and HTTPS OIDC/login works
  at the configured single host.
- `E03`: the first break-glass browser journey, System Admin home/API access,
  LDAP configuration/sync, replacement-admin login and finalize all pass.
- `E04`: full stack restart retains database/realm/object/index/graph data,
  operational state and normal-user login while break-glass stays disabled.
- `E05`: migration/bootstrap/service/secret failure blocks readiness with a
  redacted diagnosis; correction and retry recover without volume deletion or
  credential replacement.
- `E06`: backup/restore and staged secret rotation preserve access and reject
  the revoked generation. Cleanup targets only the disposable project after
  evidence has been exported.

### Helm Acceptance

- `DEPLOY-007-H01`: base/dev/prod lint/schema/render validate onboarding,
  factory and operational combinations; production rejects inline/generated
  values and requires existing/external Secret references.
- `H02`: a disposable real cluster with Ingress/TLS/StorageClass/Secret
  protection installs from empty namespace/PVCs, completes migration,
  onboarding, real browser login and production finalize.
- `H03`: Pod inspection proves least-scope Secret mounts and no public native
  peripheral ports. Logs, Events, Helm status/history and notes are redacted.
- `H04`: restart, upgrade, failed upgrade/retry, rollback and uninstall retain
  state/PVCs and never resurrect an initial credential or disabled break-glass.

### Regression And Release Gates

- Preserve exact OIDC issuer/PKCE/JWT/session/logout behavior, AUTH-012 LDAP
  ownership, read-only break-glass System UI and DEPLOY-006 404/no-Wizard
  behavior.
- Run spec/plan/traceability, Backend/Frontend behavior, E2E, Docker/Helm,
  dependency/static/image/container scans, SBOM and independent 80% coverage
  gates. Missing real LDAP, TOTP, cluster or service prerequisites are blocked,
  never replaced by mock success.

## CHG-243 Community Neo4j Production Exception And CHG-244 Local-first Packaging Test Design

Status: test design recorded after Gate 2 confirmation on 2026-07-20. Gate 4
was approved by Peter on 2026-07-20 with the combined CHG-243/CHG-244 approval;
the planned cases may run, but must not be reported passing without real evidence.

Requirements under test: refined `AUTH-016`, `DEPLOY-003`, `DEPLOY-005`,
`DEPLOY-007`, new `DEPLOY-008`, `TEST-002`, and the 80% coverage gate.

### Package, Break-glass And Secret Cases

- `AUTH-016-C01`: real factory `init` writes the first-use break-glass Secret as
  exactly `nomosmart`, identifies username `nomosmart`, and keeps every peripheral
  Secret independently random and distinct.
- `AUTH-016-C02`: real production `init` uses the same fixed first-use credential
  while keeping all non-break-glass entropy, uniqueness, placeholder and file-mode
  validation unchanged.
- `AUTH-016-C03`: status/manifest/JSON/log/Compose render/Helm render/audit/support
  output contains only safe fingerprint/source/temporary evidence and never emits
  a plaintext credential receipt, TOTP seed or unrelated Secret.
- `AUTH-016-C04`: production onboarding rejects the fixed credential when phase is
  not onboarding, the edge allowlist is absent/empty/overbroad, required actions
  are missing, or a listener exposes the entry point beyond localhost/admin CIDRs.
- `AUTH-016-C05`: live Keycloak accepts the initial credential only during the
  bounded onboarding journey, forces `UPDATE_PASSWORD` and `CONFIGURE_TOTP`, and
  the original value no longer authenticates after the password update.
- `AUTH-016-C06`: production finalize remains denied without successful OIDC,
  password/TOTP, LDAP mapper/sync and non-break-glass System Admin evidence; a
  successful finalize disables/revokes break-glass and removes initial delivery.
- `AUTH-016-C07`: operational emergency enable/rotate creates a new random
  temporary credential and rejects reuse of `nomosmart`; factory/production
  first-use compatibility does not weaken the operational rule.
- `AUTH-016-C08`: interrupted/no-overwrite/retry/import/rotation workflows retain
  the prior generation and never silently replace a consumed or active Secret.
- `AUTH-016-C09`: fresh and existing blank-profile break-glass users receive the
  non-personal `nomosmart@nomosmart.local` / `NomoSmart` / `Administrator`
  defaults without overwriting existing operator values. First login has no
  extra `VERIFY_PROFILE`, and finalize rejects any remaining required action.
- `AUTH-016-C10`: every scalar file used by Helm `Secret --from-file` contains
  the exact manifest-hashed bytes with no trailing CR/LF. Real Redis ACL,
  OpenSearch, PostgreSQL and Keycloak startup proves Kubernetes did not alter or
  split the credentials; PEM and manifest files retain valid structured format.

### Neo4j Community Exception Cases

- `DEPLOY-007-N01`: Compose and base/dev/prod Helm renders use the pinned Neo4j
  Community image and no longer require or falsely accept an Enterprise license.
- `DEPLOY-007-N02`: a real Community bootstrap creates/verifies separate `neo4j`
  and `nomosmart-service` credentials; application workloads mount only the
  service Secret and can complete required graph operations.
- `DEPLOY-007-N03`: status/readiness exposes only the non-secret
  `neo4j_community_admin_equivalent` accepted-risk evidence and never claims that
  the runtime user has role-level least privilege.
- `DEPLOY-007-N04`: Compose publishes no Neo4j native port; Kubernetes creates no
  public NodePort/LoadBalancer/Ingress for HTTP/Bolt; external connection attempts
  are denied.
- `DEPLOY-007-N05`: rendered and live NetworkPolicy permits only the explicitly
  required Backend/Worker/bootstrap paths. An overbroad/missing policy or runtime
  admin-Secret mount fails production validation.
- `DEPLOY-007-N06`: real service-password rotation, restart and retained graph
  operations succeed without giving the application bootstrap credentials.
- `DEPLOY-007-N07`: real Neo4j backup/restore reproduces the required graph state
  and accepted-risk evidence; missing/unavailable tools are reported blocked.
- `DEPLOY-007-N08`: PostgreSQL, Redis, RustFS, OpenSearch and Keycloak retain their
  existing independent least-privilege/ACL/service-identity negative tests; the
  Community exception cannot satisfy or skip those checks.

### DNS, TLS And Runtime-exclusivity Cases

- `DEPLOY-008-T01`: base/dev/prod package/Compose/Helm defaults resolve every
  public origin, callback and issuer from exactly `nomosmart.local`; a single FQDN
  override changes all derived values and SANs without mixed-host residue.
- `DEPLOY-008-T02`: the local preflight finds exactly
  `127.0.0.1 nomosmart.local`, detects conflicting mappings without rewriting
  unrelated entries, and repeated application is idempotent.
- `DEPLOY-008-T03`: real package init for Compose and Helm in factory/production
  creates non-overwriting edge, RustFS and OpenSearch self-signed material with
  matching private keys, correct CA/basic constraints, expected SANs, expiry and
  mode-`0600` private-key protection.
- `DEPLOY-008-T04`: operator-provided trusted files/existing TLS Secret take
  runtime precedence while generated fallback remains unchanged; safe status
  shows active source/fingerprint/subject/SAN/expiry only.
- `DEPLOY-008-T05`: a client that trusts the bundled CA succeeds against real
  HTTPS/OIDC/S3/OpenSearch endpoints. Untrusted client, wrong SAN, expired cert,
  `curl -k`, browser warning bypass or verify-false cannot pass acceptance.
- `DEPLOY-008-T06`: Compose binds public 80/443 only to `127.0.0.1`; a non-loopback
  listener or public peripheral port fails config and live port-scan evidence.
- `DEPLOY-008-T07`: Docker-driver `nomosmart-acceptance` exposes node 80/443 only
  through explicit `127.0.0.1:80:80` and `127.0.0.1:443:443` host port mappings,
  Ingress serves `/` and `/identity` on the same host, and no unqualified
  all-interface mapping, random-port or second-host substitution is used.
- `DEPLOY-008-T08`: preflight and live inspection prove full Compose is stopped
  before minikube starts and minikube is stopped before Compose restarts. Any
  simultaneous complete NomoSmart workload set or port collision fails.
- `DEPLOY-008-T09`: ordinary runtime switching retains Compose volumes and Helm
  PVCs; only a separately authorized exact cleanup removes named state.
- `DEPLOY-008-T10`: browser authorization/callback/logout and token issuer retain
  the exact public `https://nomosmart.local/identity/realms/nomosmart` value while
  Next.js server-side discovery, code exchange and refresh reach bundled Keycloak
  through its internal service URL. Compose and Helm NetworkPolicy allow only the
  required Frontend path; public hairpin failure cannot break first login.
- `DEPLOY-008-T11`: frontend, backend and migration images plus Helm application
  Pods use the same deterministic numeric non-root UID/GID; the official ClamAV
  container retains only the documented ownership/drop-user capabilities.
- `DEPLOY-008-T12`: RustFS/OpenSearch readiness uses certificate-valid loopback
  resolution and succeeds under the live default-deny NetworkPolicy without an
  overbroad self-ingress exception.

### Sequential Live Acceptance

- `DEPLOY-008-E01`: from empty Compose volumes, generate Secret/TLS material,
  trust the CA, start the complete stack, validate all 32+ current Flyway
  migrations, complete first login/password/TOTP and NomoSmart System Admin access,
  then restart with retained state and revalidate health/login.
- `DEPLOY-008-E02`: stop Compose without deleting its retained state, verify no
  NomoSmart Compose workload/80/443 ownership remains, then create the isolated
  Docker-driver minikube profile with the approved CPU/memory/disk/port settings.
- `DEPLOY-008-E03`: load the exact local images, install Helm into an isolated
  namespace with generated Secret/TLS material, trust the CA, and repeat real
  migration/bootstrap/HTTPS/OIDC/password/TOTP/System Admin acceptance.
- `DEPLOY-008-E04`: real Helm restart, upgrade, rollback, uninstall and PVC
  retention behave as documented; no test substitutes a mock service, fake
  certificate success or hard-coded ready state.
- `DEPLOY-008-E05`: production finalization additionally requires a real
  operator-supplied LDAP/AD provider, mapper, initial sync and replacement
  non-break-glass administrator. If unavailable, finalization is blocked rather
  than weakened.
- `DEPLOY-008-E06`: run backup/restore, dependency/static/container/image scans,
  SBOM, full Backend/Frontend/E2E and separate >=80% coverage gates. Record every
  unavailable prerequisite with its exact command and do not mark release ready.

### 2026-07-20 Sequential Live Evidence

- `DEPLOY-008-E01` passed for Compose: fresh migration/bootstrap, trusted-CA

- `DEPLOY-008-E02` passed: Compose was stopped without removing state; no Compose

- `DEPLOY-008-E03` passed: Helm revision 3 is deployed; all eleven long-running

## CHG-245 Identity Settings Form Alignment And Validation Presentation Test Design

Gate 2 was confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-20 with `ＯＫ`. Gate 3 test design is
recorded below. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-07-20 with
`Peter approves CHG-245 Identity Settings Form Alignment and Validation Presentation`.

Requirement under test: `IDENTITY-UI-001`.

### Layout And Responsive Contracts

- `IDENTITY-UI-001-F01`: the Identity OIDC form uses a scoped class; Prompt,
  Model and unrelated `.identity-form-grid` consumers retain their current
  selectors and layout.
- `IDENTITY-UI-001-F02`: desktop fields use two equal columns, top-aligned field
  groups and stable 40px controls; one inline error does not stretch or move the
  paired control.
- `IDENTITY-UI-001-F03`: Discovery / JWKS occupies the complete row and long
  valid values remain readable without clipping or escaping their container.
- `IDENTITY-UI-001-F04`: directory Cron, timezone and action controls align;
  provider Filter sections retain their established hierarchy and behavior.
- `IDENTITY-UI-001-F05`: at the existing narrow breakpoint the form becomes one
  column with full-width controls, 40px touch targets and no horizontal page
  overflow at 768 and 375 CSS pixels.

### Validation State And Localization

- `IDENTITY-UI-001-V01`: the initial unloaded settings state renders no empty-
  value validation errors and does not announce false failures.
- `IDENTITY-UI-001-V02`: after a valid Backend effective configuration loads,
  Issuer and Discovery plus every other field are revalidated from that exact

- `IDENTITY-UI-001-V03`: invalid Issuer, Realm, Client ID, Audience, Discovery /

  existing validation predicates and accepted values remain unchanged.
- `IDENTITY-UI-001-V04`: each invalid control exposes `aria-invalid` and an

  the error state includes text and border/icon treatment, not color alone.
- `IDENTITY-UI-001-V05`: validation messages have aligned Traditional Chinese
  and English keys with no hard-coded display-language regression.
- `IDENTITY-UI-001-V06`: API loading, reload, error and retry do not combine a
  prior response's errors with a later response's values.

### Regression And Browser Acceptance

- `IDENTITY-UI-001-R01`: locked and temporarily unlocked rendering, permission-
  gated edit entry, Secret configured state, save/cancel and reauthentication
  query behavior remain unchanged.
- `IDENTITY-UI-001-R02`: no Backend route, payload, validation rule, persistence,
  permission, synchronization or audit contract changes.
- `IDENTITY-UI-001-E01`: authenticated 1440 and 1024 CSS-pixel screenshots show
  aligned paired controls, independent error rows and orderly section spacing.
- `IDENTITY-UI-001-E02`: authenticated 768 and 375 CSS-pixel screenshots show a
  readable one-column form with no overlap, clipping or horizontal scroll.
- `IDENTITY-UI-001-E03`: keyboard focus order follows visual order; labels focus

## CHG-246 Application-tier High Availability Test Design

Gate 2 was confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-21. Gate 3 test design is recorded
below. Gate 4 was never independently approved; before implementation or
feature-test execution this design was absorbed unchanged into CHG-247 and is
now controlled by the CHG-247 Gate 4 decision.

Requirement under test: `DEPLOY-009`.

### Static, Values And Render Contracts

- `DEPLOY-009-T01`: production values enable application-tier HA and define at
  least two replicas each for Frontend, Backend API and Celery Worker; Beat is
  rendered at exactly one replica.
- `DEPLOY-009-T02`: production values/schema reject any application replica
  count below two or disabled HA, while development and factory acceptance may
  render one application replica without claiming HA.
- `DEPLOY-009-T03`: Frontend, Backend and Worker each render a
  PodDisruptionBudget whose selector matches only the same release/component
  and whose two-replica baseline has `minAvailable >= 1`.
- `DEPLOY-009-T04`: all three HA workloads render hard same-component separation
  across `kubernetes.io/hostname`; a missing/relaxed topology control fails the
  production policy test and optional zone spread cannot replace node spread.
- `DEPLOY-009-T05`: all three HA Deployments render rolling updates with
  `maxUnavailable: 0`, `maxSurge >= 1`, existing bootstrap/readiness gates and a
  bounded termination grace/drain contract.
- `DEPLOY-009-T06`: Services do not require sticky session/session affinity;
  Frontend OIDC transient state and Backend authorization/configuration do not
  use pod-local durable correctness state.
- `DEPLOY-009-T07`: Worker commands and health probes support multiple unique
  worker nodes; existing lease/idempotency/terminal-state controls remain
  enabled and no worker identity is hard-coded to one Pod.
- `DEPLOY-009-T08`: Beat stays single-active with no PDB or status text that
  falsely identifies it as HA; increasing application replicas never increases
  Beat replicas.
- `DEPLOY-009-T09`: Docker Compose config remains valid and documented as
  single-host non-HA; scaling Compose containers is not accepted as CHG-246 HA
  evidence.
- `DEPLOY-009-T10`: runbooks, notes and release readiness use the exact
  Application-tier HA boundary and list peripherals, ingress/platform and Beat
  as excluded from end-to-end HA.

### Live Multi-node Acceptance

- `DEPLOY-009-E01`: on a disposable cluster with at least two schedulable
  application worker nodes and adequate surge capacity, install production
  values and prove at least two ready Frontend, Backend and Worker Pods, one Beat
  Pod, correct PDBs and different node names for each same-component replica.
- `DEPLOY-009-E02`: send continuous authenticated browser/API traffic through
  the public Service while deleting one Frontend Pod and then one Backend Pod;
  the remaining ready replica serves the same login/session/authorization state
  without sticky routing, unsafe replay, 5xx or operator-visible interruption.
- `DEPLOY-009-E03`: start a real background job, terminate one Worker and drain
  one application worker node while respecting PDBs; a remaining Worker
  continues or safely receives the task, and PostgreSQL/external evidence shows
  exactly one terminal transition, publication and external side effect.
- `DEPLOY-009-E04`: perform a compatible rolling upgrade with continuous
  authenticated traffic. No application Deployment has zero ready endpoints;
  surge/readiness behavior is observable and the migration/bootstrap gates
  remain authoritative. The traffic set includes only endpoints declared
  compatible by both release identities; deliberate unscoped-graph retirement
  is tested separately by `CHG-247-A02`.
- `DEPLOY-009-E05`: roll back to the compatible prior release under the same
  traffic and worker checks; PDB, placement, state and Secret references remain
  intact and no code-only rollback is attempted across a documented
  incompatible migration or security-contract boundary. An image that would
  restore an unscoped graph route is rejected rather than exercised as a
  successful rollback.
- `DEPLOY-009-E06`: a single-node production cluster or insufficient surge
  capacity fails preflight/acceptance rather than weakening placement. A
  deliberate bundled-peripheral or Beat outage is reported outside the HA
  claim and may correctly make dependent application readiness fail closed.

## CHG-247 Release Gap Remediation, Scoped Knowledge Graph And Bundled Vault Integration Test Design

Gate 1 audit and Gate 2 decisions were completed on 2026-07-26. Gate 3 test
design is recorded below. Peter additionally confirmed `DEPLOY-011` with
`接受 DEPLOY-011 隨包 Vault 建議`: Compose and Helm bundle Vault by default
while retaining an explicit external mode. No CHG-247 implementation, migration
execution, feature test or live acceptance had been authorized when this Gate 3
test design was recorded. Peter approved Gate 4 on
2026-07-26 with
`Peter approves CHG-247 Release Gap Remediation, Scoped Knowledge Graph And Bundled Vault Integration`;
the planned implementation and verification may now proceed.

Requirements under test:

- `REPORT-014`, `PROJECT-006`, `DEPLOY-009`, `DEPLOY-010`, `DEPLOY-011`,
  `NOTIF-003`
- `IMPORT-001`, `IMPORT-002`, `DOC-002`, `PERM-005`, `DOC-005`, `CHUNK-003`
- `GRAPH-008`, `RAG-019`, `REVIEW-022`, `REVIEW-023`, `APIKEY-002`
- `OPS-002`, `IDEMP-001`, `SECRET-001`, `OCR-003`, `API-PAGE-001`,
  `WEBHOOK-001`, `I18N-004`

### Test Policy And Evidence Freshness

- All live acceptance follows `TEST-002`: real isolated services and disposable
  namespaces/schemas/buckets/indexes/realms are required. Mock, stub, fake,
  deterministic adapter, hard-coded readiness and fixture-only success cannot
  close a CHG-247 requirement.
- Authorization checks exercise multiple-role union semantics, disabled users,
  Owner relationships, empty grants, explicit denied actions and cross-project
  scope. Frontend hiding is tested only as presentation; Backend denial is the
  security result.
- Concurrency tests use real competing transactions/workers and controlled
  crashes/redelivery. A sequential unit test cannot substitute for a race,
  lease, generation or idempotency acceptance case.
- Frontend and Backend coverage are measured separately from their complete
  suites and must each reach at least 80%. The evidence record includes source
  commit, dirty-diff fingerprint, exact command, start/end time, suite manifest,
  report path and SHA-256. Reports from a different source state,
  focused-only runs or manually edited summaries fail the gate.
- `TEST-005-G01`: upgraded `coverage:check` or `coverage:evidence` regenerates a
  machine-readable full-suite manifest and rejects stale commit, dirty-diff
  mismatch (including untracked source/test files), missing suite, timestamp
  inversion, altered report hash and percentage-only legacy JSON.
- Each test creates traceable identities and performs bounded cleanup. Cleanup
  must not delete production/user data, hide a failed result or rely on broad
  prefixes without an exact dry run.

### Reports And Project Archive

- `REPORT-014-B01`: every report topic uses one Backend policy projection for
  visible scope, selectable filters and field-level disclosure; direct route,
  CSV and options calls cannot return fields excluded by that projection.
- `REPORT-014-B02`: `Report.ModelReport` is independent of general Reports
  access. Authorized users receive model/cost details; unauthorized users may
  receive the permitted owner summary but no model name, token, unit-cost,
  provider or reconstructable total detail.
- `REPORT-014-M01`: the permission migration grants `Report.ModelReport` only
  to the system-admin baseline and introduces no grant for existing custom
  roles; fresh/upgrade/rerun evidence proves no privilege expansion.
- `REPORT-014-B03`: multi-role union, Project Owner and explicit no-grant cases
  return the exact permitted project/document rows, including direct-ID and
  forged filter denial. Removing a grant during a session takes effect on the
  next request across summary/options/export.
- `REPORT-014-B04`: each large report queries the datastore with stable
  server-side pagination. Query/row-count evidence proves the Backend does not
  load all matching rows and slice in memory.
- `REPORT-014-B05`: CSV export covers all authorized matching rows using bounded
  keyset/server-cursor streaming, validates authorization and query shape before
  headers, cancels iterator/query on disconnect/timeout, never treats a partial
  file as success and records secret-safe start/result/row-count audit evidence.
  No background job/artifact/status/cancel/expiry contract exists in v1.
- `REPORT-014-F01`: report controls, disabled/denied states, independent cursors
  and export status use live Backend results and bilingual accessible labels.

- `PROJECT-006-M01`: with old Workers drained, the forward migration assigns an
  archive-generation baseline to active Projects; validated unclaimed queued
  jobs/outbox receive that baseline. Running/leased work is expired and either
  becomes `needs_reconciliation` for ambiguous external effects or is retried
  through the same idempotent command when no effect is proven. Archived
  Project work is cancelled/superseded, and fresh/upgrade/rerun/checksum cases
  preserve retained published rows.
- `PROJECT-006-I01`: archive increments/captures a generation atomically,
  prevents new commands and cleans/disables every unfinished Data Connection,
  credential reference, schedule, Integration Client scope, Notification,
  Idempotency/command evidence, document reference/event, validation, chat,
  review, Pipeline, graph, sync and outbox row plus S3, OpenSearch, Neo4j and
  provider-side temporary asset. It removes local Vault references/scopes but
  the read-only workload role cannot delete Vault KV; a path/value-free operator
  cleanup notification is emitted for runbook rotation/deletion.
- `PROJECT-006-I02`: Workers paused before an external write and before terminal
  commit observe a changed generation/cancel state and cannot recreate rows,
  objects, indexes, graph nodes, notifications or success state.
- `PROJECT-006-I03`: repeated archive/cleanup and crash/retry are idempotent;
  partial external failure remains observable/retryable and never reports a
  false completed archive.
- `PROJECT-006-I04`: published active/inactive serving artifacts and required
  non-content audit evidence are retained exactly as specified; incomplete or
  candidate content is not. Late legacy messages without a generation still
  fail the Project-state/generation fence after migration.
- `PROJECT-006-E01`: an authorized Owner receives the named-impact confirmation
  journey; concurrent readers/writers and unauthorized users are denied as soon
  as archive begins, and the UI never displays resurrected late-worker state.

### Deployment High Availability And Production Fail-closed

The absorbed `DEPLOY-009-T01..T10` and `DEPLOY-009-E01..E06` cases above remain
mandatory and are executed as part of CHG-247, not as a separate approval.

- `DEPLOY-010-T01`: `values.schema.json` rejects production with missing/invalid
  external endpoints, TLS/CA, Vault auth/reference configuration, Secret
  references, readiness dependencies, resource/storage values, HA replicas,
  PDB/anti-affinity/rollout or surge capacity.
- `DEPLOY-010-T02`: Helm templates call `fail` or equivalent for invalid
  cross-field combinations that JSON Schema alone cannot express; no
  default/empty value silently weakens production.
- `DEPLOY-010-T03`: a live preflight Job checks cluster nodes/capacity, required
  Secret/config objects, DNS/TLS and dependency/Vault reachability before
  migration/bootstrap/application rollout.
- `DEPLOY-010-T04`: development/factory and Compose profiles remain renderable
  under their documented non-production boundaries and cannot emit a
  production-ready or HA success marker.
- `DEPLOY-010-E01`: a valid disposable production cluster passes all three
  layers; deleting or corrupting one prerequisite makes the earliest applicable
  layer fail with an actionable, secret-safe result.

### Durable Notifications And Idempotent Commands

- `NOTIF-003-M01`: migration creates source-event identity, per-recipient
  dedupe uniqueness and resolved lifecycle without duplicating legacy rows.
- `NOTIF-003-I01`: Pipeline failure, Validation completed/partial-failed,
  manager/Owner review assignment, rejection, manager/delegate missing,
  approved-waiting-publish, published/switch-active, source
  update/delete/disable/enable/version-switch, model/config anomaly and critical
  graph-sync failure each create the specified source event/outbox atomically;
  transaction rollback creates neither.
- `NOTIF-003-I02`: recipient expansion uses current authorized scope and event
  rules. Unauthorized, disabled or unrelated users receive no row or side
  channel, while one user with multiple roles receives only one notification.
  The matrix proves creator, manager/delegate, Project Owners, authorized
  referencing-Project recipients and workflow administrator/owner fallbacks for
  their exact event types; a fallback is notified but never gains approval
  authority.
- `NOTIF-003-I03`: duplicate delivery, Worker retry and concurrent consumers
  preserve one row per source event/recipient; title/body/link/created time and
  source identity remain stable.
- `NOTIF-003-I04`: read/unread is independent of business resolved/unresolved.
  Approval assignment resolves only on task approve/reject/cancel; waiting
  publish resolves on publish/switch-active; source/graph/model critical rows
  resolve only on verified recovery or the specified user action. Read alone,
  unrelated events and retryable failure never resolve them.
- `NOTIF-003-F01`: Notification Center uses real cursor/filter results, renders
  read and resolved states with text/icon rather than color alone, and never
  fabricates counts.

- `IDEMP-001-B01`: switch-active and graph retry reject a missing or malformed
  `Idempotency-Key` with a stable 4xx before mutation.
- `IDEMP-001-B02`: same actor/scope/operation/key/request hash replays the exact
  stored response and resource identity; a different request hash conflicts and
  performs no additional effect.
- `IDEMP-001-B03`: raw keys are never persisted/logged. Records have bounded
  retention and do not collide across actor, scope or operation; only a
  one-way request fingerprint and safe response metadata are auditable.
- `IDEMP-001-B04`: replay while the original request is still in progress
  returns the stable documented conflict/retryable envelope and `Retry-After`
  policy; expired leases are recovered by one claimant without duplicating the
  external effect.
- `IDEMP-001-I01`: concurrent switch-active requests create one manifest switch
  and one event/outbox; crash after commit and retry returns the completed
  result without a second switch.
- `IDEMP-001-I02`: graph retry HTTP creates one durable retry attempt/outbox and
  returns without calling Neo4j. Competing Workers claim once; crash/redelivery
  yields one terminal attempt/external effect.

### Import, Re-extraction, Update And Chunk Lineage

- `IMPORT-001-B01`: upload, update, FTP/FTPS/SFTP-over-SSH/S3 and other
  file-source paths accept only PDF/DOCX/TXT/`.md`/`.markdown` and reject
  `.doc`, CSV, JSON, disguised extensions, MIME/magic mismatches, malformed
  DOCX packages and oversize files without rows, objects or Pipelines. Generic
  SSH command/scp sources are unavailable and cannot bypass this policy.
- `IMPORT-001-B02`: HTTP/API response ingestion accepts the canonical file/text
  formats plus CSV/JSON and rejects unsupported content types; this exception
  cannot be reached through file upload or remote-file services.
- `IMPORT-001-B03`: the typed global size/format policy is reflected identically
  in Backend errors, frontend accept/help text and data-source validation. The
  default is exactly 100 MB; zero, negative, non-numeric and out-of-range typed
  configuration fail before the workload reports ready.
- `IMPORT-001-L01`: real PDF/DOCX/TXT/MD corpus, hostile/malformed corpus and
  legacy `.doc` read-only compatibility execute through the live parser/object
  store; no LibreOffice or content-type fallback passes.

- `IMPORT-002-B01`:
  `POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/documents/upload` requires
  `Idempotency-Key` and ordered multipart `files`. Every parseable,
  request-authorized single/multi-file request returns exactly
  `200 {request_id,success_count,failed_count,results}` in input order. Each
  valid item commits its own Document/`v1.0`; each invalid item has the exact
  index/safe filename/stable error fields and cannot roll back successful
  siblings.
- `IMPORT-002-B02`: database failure after object upload compensates that exact
  object; object-store failure creates no row; compensation failure remains
  visible/retryable with no false success.
- `IMPORT-002-B03`: retries and concurrent duplicate batches derive per-file
  identity from Project, actor, key, input index and content hash, creating at
  most one Document/version per item while replaying the original complete
  response. Same key with a different ordered fingerprint conflicts without
  mutation.
- `IMPORT-002-F01`: multi-file UI renders every success/failure independently
  and leaves successful documents waiting for manual extraction. A request-wide
  4xx is reserved for a malformed/unauthorized whole request.

- `DOC-002-B01`: re-extract requires live capability, source fingerprint,
  `lock_version`, completed/eligible state and `Idempotency-Key`; stale,
  source-changed, locked or duplicate-working requests return stable 409 with no
  new state.
- `DOC-002-I01`: concurrent valid requests lock Document/max version and at most
  one atomically creates the unique `vM.(R+1)`, immutable same-source link,
  Pipeline and outbox. Existing active serving stays unchanged.
- `DOC-002-I02`: rollback/queue failure leaves no version, Pipeline or orphan
  object; retry safely produces one command result.
- `DOC-002-F01`: completed documents show Re-extract, other states show only
  their valid action/retry. The client never reports success before the live
  Backend version/Pipeline exists.
- `DOC-002-F02`: confirmation shows current and predicted `vM.(R+1)`, immutable
  source identity and that Active serving remains unchanged. Open/select/cancel
  creates no version; success shows the returned Pipeline, and failure keeps the
  previous state plus a safe error. Both success and failure create the
  specified redacted audit evidence.

- `PERM-005-B01`: Backend capability response reflects permission unions,
  Project Owner governance, version/archive/lock state and independent
  create/edit/delete/execute semantics for the fixed keys `can_upload`,
  `can_update_source`, `can_start_extraction`, `can_reextract`,
  `can_edit_chunks`, `can_create_reference`, `can_sync_source`,
  `can_view_graph`, `can_submit_review` and `can_manage_lifecycle`. Owner/Editor
  and Viewer baselines match the specification.
- `PERM-005-B02`: every mutation independently reauthorizes at execution time;
  forged/old capabilities, role removal, archive/state change and direct API
  calls fail closed.
- `DOC-005-F01`: Update Document displays immutable source identity, Active and
  Working versions, expected version, impact and live capability before an
  explicit confirmation. Opening, selecting or canceling creates no state.
  When a capability is false, its button, file input and hidden interactive
  target are absent rather than merely visually disabled.
- `DOC-005-I01`: source-type conversion is denied; identical content creates no
  version; valid changed content creates exactly one next major `.0` version and
  leaves active serving untouched until approval/publication.

- `CHUNK-003-M01`: migration records append-only chunk edit lineage, actor/time,
  source spans/references and artifact reconciliation identity without mutating
  published history.
- `CHUNK-003-B01`: only mutable candidate versions permit edit; review-locked,
  approved, active, inactive, archived and unauthorized versions are denied.
- `CHUNK-003-I01`: concurrent edits serialize on version/revision. One accepted
  revision rebuilds canonical chunks, tags, candidate index and graph preview as
  one fail-closed reconciliation; partial external failure cannot mark ready.
- `CHUNK-003-I02`: one source artifact/page/span may map to multiple chunks and
  one chunk may carry multiple evidence references without invented one-to-one
  assumptions; version/source lineage remains navigable.
- `CHUNK-003-F01`: PDF/DOCX/text/Markdown source and output previews are
  sanitized, bounded and content-type safe; unavailable/failed evidence is
  explicit and no unsafe HTML/script/download URL is rendered.
- `CHUNK-003-F02`: Chunk index remains the primary card identity and editable
  title stays secondary. Real Image/Table/Chart artifacts render through their
  safe preview contract. Activating one source anchor highlights every mapped
  Chunk and scrolls to the first without discarding later mappings.

### Permission-scoped Knowledge Graph

- `GRAPH-008-B01`: only
  `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}/graph`,
  `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}/graph/neighbors`,
  `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}/graph/paths` and specified version-evidence
  routes return graph content after Project/Document authorization. Project
  graph default/range is `120`/`10..500`; neighbors requires `node_id` and uses
  `80`/`10..200`; paths requires `source_id`/`target_id` and uses
  `max_depth=4`/`1..8`, `node_limit=120`/`10..500`.
- `GRAPH-008-B02`: former `/api/v1/knowledge-graph`,
  `/api/v1/knowledge-graph/neighbors` and
  `/api/v1/knowledge-graph/paths` routes are not registered and return normal
  404 for every role, including System Admin.
- `GRAPH-008-B03`: direct IDs, neighbor expansion and path traversal omit an
  edge/node unless the caller can view both endpoint Projects/Documents.
  Unauthorized IDs, counts, degree, truncation flags, hidden-path length and
  error text are not disclosed.
- `GRAPH-008-B04`: multiple-role union and Project Owner rules grant only their
  actual content scopes; `SystemManagement`/System Admin alone grants none.
- `GRAPH-008-B05`: request size, depth, result count and execution time are
  bounded. The fixed `{project_id,nodes,edges,truncated,node_limit}` envelope
  computes truncation only over authorized results; hidden nodes never change
  count/degree/path length/flag. Forbidden/missing cases have equivalent
  envelopes and a documented timing tolerance under controlled load.
- `GRAPH-008-I01`: active published graph synchronization uses the unified
  Neo4j `Project`, `Document`, `DocumentVersion`, `Chunk` and `Tag` node model,
  active-version relationships and stable provenance IDs, while the historical
  four-node staging preview remains Document-scoped candidate evidence and
  cannot leak into formal serving.
- `GRAPH-008-F01`: no global graph menu/page/component/count/search remains.
  Project/Document graph UI uses only scoped endpoints, handles omitted
  relationships cleanly and exposes no all-project aggregation affordance.
- `GRAPH-008-E01`: authenticated Peter/John/System Admin browser journeys prove
  positive own-scope views and negative cross-scope/direct-navigation behavior
  at desktop and narrow widths.

### Conversation, Validation, Submission And Approval

- `RAG-019-B01`:
  `POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/chat/query` and scoped conversation
  list/detail/delete require `scope_mode=published|document_staging`; Document
  mode also requires the exact version identity. Records have
  non-interchangeable scope identities, active-version/manifests and authorized
  history; a caller cannot move IDs or messages between surfaces/projects.
- `RAG-019-B02`:
  `GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/chat/conversations` persists and pages
  history with stable cursors; exact detail/delete and
  `.../{conversation_id}/export.csv` enforce deletion/retention and bind
  citations to the serving version. Browser refresh/device change does not rely
  on local-only state or a Frontend-built partial export.
- `RAG-019-I01`: readiness and model lists come from live configured,
  authorized providers and real dependency state. No typed fixture,
  deterministic answer or hard-coded model/readiness path can return success.
- `RAG-019-I02`: real provider success, timeout, disconnect, retry, inactive
  version and provider-unavailable cases preserve exact message/citation/usage
  evidence without cross-conversation contamination. Eligible in-flight work
  can be cancelled to one terminal state; completed/ineligible work cannot be
  rewritten by cancel.
- `RAG-019-V01`: scoped
  `POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/chat/validation-runs` creates the run;
  each accepted input receives immutable client-or-server UUID identity,
  one-based ordinal and canonical content hash, while the run persists a hashed
  execution manifest that freezes Project/surface/version/generation,
  Chat/Embedding/Judge model identities, prompt hashes and content, retrieval
  settings and maximum attempts. Public responses omit prompt content; corrupt,
  changed or explicitly legacy-unavailable manifests fail closed. Retries retain
  the original input identity/order/hash and cannot exceed the manifest limit;
  canonical `GET /api/v1/validation-runs/{run_id}` and `/items` return
  authorized metadata and cursor-filtered persisted evidence. Canonical
  `/retry-failed`, `/cancel` and `/export.csv` create one traceable eligible
  attempt/terminal result and a bounded UTF-8 BOM export with stable ordering,
  correct escaping and every specified result/evidence column. CSV import
  validates schema/row identity, and no retry reruns successful siblings.
- `RAG-019-V02`: conversation download contains exact conversation surface,
  document/project scope, serving version, question/answer times, complete
  document/version/chunk/page citations, evaluation and suggested correction;
  it cannot mix Document staging with Project published history.
- `RAG-019-F01`: Document Chat, Project Chat and Validation UI display their
  actual scope/model/readiness/history and complete loading/empty/error/partial
  states in both locales.

- `REVIEW-022-B01`: Submission Evidence response is assembled by Backend from
  exact candidate version; source/artifact references; Pipeline; actual
  LLM/OCR/Embedding metadata; average confidence; Document/Chunk/Tag and
  Text/Image/Table/Chart counts; true graph nodes/edges/coverage/traceability;
  conversation and validation state; lock/revision/time; and stable readiness
  reasons. Graph values cannot be inferred from chat, citations or chunk+tag
  counts.
- `REVIEW-022-B02`: authorization and readiness cannot be overridden by client
  fields. Missing/failed/stale evidence blocks submission without mutation.
- `REVIEW-022-I01`: submit transaction locks/revalidates version,
  `lock_version`, evidence revision/hash and readiness. A concurrent edit,
  re-extract, validation change, archive or permission removal causes stable
  conflict/denial and leaves no approval, notification or partial status change.
- `REVIEW-022-F01`: Submission UI renders the Backend projection and blocking
  reasons only; it has no client-calculated ready/success shortcut.

- `REVIEW-023-M01`: migration creates immutable evidence manifest and
  decision/snapshot identities while preserving existing approval history.
  Completed legacy rows that cannot be reconstructed are explicitly
  `legacy_evidence_unavailable`; pending rows backfill only when the locked
  version and every required hash/reference verify, otherwise they fail closed
  and require resubmission.
- `REVIEW-023-I01`: successful submit stores exact version/evidence/content
  hashes, references, graph/validation/conversation identities, submitter,
  manager, Owner and timestamps. Later source/artifact/role changes cannot
  mutate the reviewer snapshot.
- `REVIEW-023-B01`: My, Pending, History and Rejected workspaces use real
  Backend project, document, editor, time, priority, source, stage and result
  filter matrix plus stable cursors with correct counts/empty states and no
  placeholder UUIDs, local-only decisions or fabricated evidence.
- `REVIEW-023-B02`: manager/Owner sequencing, reject/resubmit, disabled users,
  missing reviewer, permission unions and direct action denial are enforced
  against the immutable task/evidence identity.
- `REVIEW-023-F01`: My, Pending, History and Rejected render as a compact,
  horizontally scrollable NomoSmart Tab strip with a non-color-only active
  indicator, count badges, subtle hover feedback, visible keyboard focus and
  at least 40px touch targets.
- `REVIEW-023-E01`: two-user authenticated browser flow submits, reviews,
  rejects/resubmits or approves/publishes while each workspace and evidence
  view remains consistent across refresh and concurrent updates.

### API Keys, Operations, Vault And OCR

- `APIKEY-002-B01`: authorized
  `POST /api/v1/integration-clients` returns `201` and
  `POST /api/v1/integration-clients/{client_id}/keys/rotate` returns `200`;
  each successful response returns its new plaintext `api_key` exactly once.
  Storage contains only the approved verifier/hash, old rotated keys fail
  immediately, and list/detail/reopen responses never return plaintext or a
  reversible value.
- `APIKEY-002-F01`: within the application, plaintext exists only in component
  memory while the reveal surface is open and is masked by default. Explicit Copy writes the OS
  clipboard, provides accessible copied feedback and a warning that the app
  cannot reliably clear that clipboard. Close prompts that the value cannot be
  recovered; close/unmount/navigation clears app memory/DOM, and reopen/refresh
  cannot retrieve it. Copy audit contains only actor/key/request/time/action.
- `APIKEY-002-F02`: masked and after-close screenshots plus browser storage,
  URL, logs, analytics, error reports and accessibility announcements contain
  no plaintext. While reveal is active, automation/error tooling disables or
  redacts screenshot, video, trace and failure artifacts; it never persists an
  authorized plaintext reveal as evidence.
- `APIKEY-002-B02`: Backend filter/cursor covers lifecycle/status/owner fields
  under authorization and remains stable under create/revoke/delete activity.
- `APIKEY-002-B03`: a view-only principal can query only authorized metadata and
  cannot create, rotate, reveal, copy through an API response, revoke or mutate
  lifecycle state.

- `OPS-002-B01`: `/api/v1/health` reports process liveness without requiring
  remote dependencies; `/api/v1/ready` checks all platform dependencies
  required to accept work and fails closed with secret-safe component
  identities.
- `OPS-002-B02`: scoped operational status applies authorization and returns
  only allowed service/business detail; System Admin status never grants
  knowledge-content scope.
- `OPS-002-B03`: `APP_ENV=test` or equivalent cannot hard-code readiness
  success. Deliberately unavailable PostgreSQL, Redis, S3, OpenSearch, Neo4j,
  Keycloak or Vault produces the specified degraded/not-ready response.
- `OPS-002-B04`: one Project's missing model credential/index marks only that
  `/api/v1/system/status` scope `blocked` while platform `/api/v1/ready`
  remains successful; loss of PostgreSQL, Redis or required Worker heartbeat
  makes `/api/v1/ready` fail and recover from live evidence.
- `OPS-002-I01`: metrics individually expose bounded API latency/error,
  provider latency/failure, retrieval failure, validation queue depth, Worker
  success/failure/retry/final state and report export row-count/latency without
  credentials/tokens/document content.
- `OPS-002-I02`: redacted audit cases cover Chat query, feedback, Validation
  create/execute/cancel, provider/model failure, Worker retry/final failure,
  report export, Graph retry and readiness-affecting configuration changes;
  raw provider errors, prompt/citation/document content and secrets are absent.
- `OPS-002-D01`: Compose health checks and Helm liveness/readiness/startup probes
  call the correct layer and gate dependent rollout/traffic.

- `SECRET-001-U01`: canonical reference parser accepts only
  `vault://<mount>/<path>#<field>`, rejects ambiguous/malformed/traversal forms
  and never includes values in errors.
- `SECRET-001-I01`: real Vault KV v2 over certificate-valid HTTPS resolves the
  exact field with least-privilege policy; wrong CA/hostname, missing version,
  denied path/field or unavailable Vault fails closed. Live resolution and
  rotation/cache invalidation are exercised separately for Chat, Judge,
  Embedding, OCR, FTP, FTPS, SFTP password/private-key/passphrase, HTTP Bearer/
  API-key header and S3 access/secret-key consumers.
- `SECRET-001-I02`: Helm Backend and Worker authenticate with their own
  ServiceAccount JWT/Kubernetes Auth roles, receive bounded short-lived tokens,
  renew/re-authenticate safely and cannot read each other's unneeded paths.
- `SECRET-001-I03`: Compose Backend and Worker authenticate with distinct
  least-privilege AppRoles using separate non-secret Role IDs and separate
  uncommitted read-only Secret ID files. Cross-role/path reads, a shared
  overbroad role, root/dev/long-lived tokens, plaintext environment Secret IDs
  and TLS bypass fail config/security policy.
- `SECRET-001-S01`: resolved values are held only in bounded memory and absent
  from database/plaintext config, persistent filesystem, rendered manifests,
  logs, audit, metrics, traces, exception bodies, core artifacts and repository
  scans. The sole SFTP adapter exception proves `0700` owner directory, `0600`
  file, no backup/core capture and no file remaining after success, failure,
  timeout or cancellation.
- `SECRET-001-C01`: production create/reset/rotation stores only `vault://`
  references for Vault-capable runtime consumers. Legacy encrypted rows are
  read-only only in the typed migration mode, each with status/owner/deadline;
  no code auto-copies values or treats a missing Vault target as plaintext
  fallback.
- `SECRET-001-C02`: operators create references and validate every consumer
  class with real Vault before marking migration complete. Production preflight
  rejects active legacy rows or legacy-read mode after
  `vault_migration_complete`; a non-production legacy profile cannot generate
  production-ready evidence.
- `SECRET-001-D01`: chart/Compose examples contain placeholders only. Bundled
  mode permits Backend and Worker to reach only the internal Vault TLS service;
  external mode permits only the configured certificate-valid external Vault
  endpoint. Neither mode exposes Vault through the NomoSmart edge, shares an
  auth identity or stores a root/dev/long-lived token.

### Bundled Vault Deployment Lifecycle

- `DEPLOY-011-D01`: Compose and Helm expose one typed
  `vault.mode=bundled|external` selector and reject bundled/external
  simultaneously enabled, neither selected, empty external address, unpinned
  image/chart, disabled TLS or persistence, placeholder seal configuration and
  incompatible auth mode. External mode renders no Vault server, Service,
  StatefulSet, volume/PVC, initialization/bootstrap Job or public route.
- `DEPLOY-011-D02`: the release pins the official HashiCorp Vault image by
  immutable tested version/digest and vendors the pinned official Helm chart
  archive with a reproducible `Chart.lock`, verified checksum/provenance and
  release-package presence. The normal package does not claim that a
  disconnected container-image archive is included.
- `DEPLOY-011-D03`: bundled Compose starts one non-dev, non-HA Vault server with
  certificate-valid HTTPS, Integrated Raft and a named persistent volume.
  Restart preserves cluster identity, initialization state, policies and KV
  values; status and documentation never label this topology HA or production
  unattended-recovery capable.
- `DEPLOY-011-D04`: bundled Helm production starts exactly three Vault servers
  with Integrated Raft, per-server persistent storage, persistent restricted
  audit storage, hard worker-node anti-affinity, a quorum-safe PDB and
  immutable rolling-upgrade settings. Scheduling/preflight rejects insufficient
  nodes, storage or surge/quorum capacity instead of silently weakening
  separation or availability.
- `DEPLOY-011-D05`: Vault client port `8200` and cluster port `8201` are
  internal-only. Compose publishes neither port on any host interface, including
  loopback and debug profiles; Helm creates no public Service, Ingress,
  `/vault` edge path or NomoSmart application API/UI. Operator management is
  limited to the documented restricted CLI or bounded port-forward workflow.
- `DEPLOY-011-S01`: production seal mode is explicit. Auto-unseal uses only an
  operator-provided KMS, HSM or independent Transit seal and validates its
  reference without committing seal credentials. The portable self-contained
  Shamir mode uses five PGP-encrypted shares with threshold three, documents
  manual unseal after restart and cannot claim unattended recovery.
- `DEPLOY-011-S02`: factory/development acceptance may use disposable operator
  PGP identities, but Shamir still uses five encrypted shares with threshold
  three and must not use Vault dev mode, persist a plaintext share/root token
  or present the disposable ceremony as production-ready custody evidence.
  Every production profile rejects reduced-share or reduced-threshold settings.
- `DEPLOY-011-S03`: initialization runs exactly once. Unseal/recovery shares and
  the initial root token are encrypted to operator PGP recipients and never
  enter a Kubernetes Secret, Compose env/secret generation, CLI argument,
  generated package/workload file, rendered manifest, receipt, log, audit,
  trace, backup or repository artifact. PGP ciphertext is delivered only to an
  explicitly selected owner-controlled destination outside all those surfaces,
  the package retains no copy, and plaintext/package-decryptable material is
  never persisted. Re-running package initialization against an initialized
  cluster returns redacted status and never reinitializes, rekeys or overwrites
  it.
- `DEPLOY-011-B01`: a one-time operator-controlled bootstrap enables the
  approved KV v2 mount, audit device and Kubernetes Auth or distinct Compose
  AppRoles, installs separate least-privilege Backend/Worker policies and
  verifies cross-path denial. It is idempotent, records only non-sensitive
  fingerprints/status and revokes the initial root/bootstrap token after a
  successful handoff.
- `DEPLOY-011-B02`: package bootstrap never reads and copies legacy encrypted
  values or business/integration plaintext into Vault. `SECRET-001-C01..C02`
  remains the only controlled per-consumer reference migration; absence of a
  target secret cannot enable a database/env fallback.
- `DEPLOY-011-R01`: NomoSmart dependent readiness stays false while bundled
  Vault is uninitialized, sealed, below Raft quorum, certificate-invalid,
  unavailable or missing required bootstrap/auth/policy evidence. Recovery to
  healthy/unsealed/bootstrap-complete state restores readiness from live
  evidence without bypass, hard-coded success or secret disclosure.
- `DEPLOY-011-L01`: start, stop, restart, upgrade and compatible rollback
  preserve the exact Raft/PVC identity and never implicitly initialize, rekey,
  rotate or destroy data. Uninstall retains Vault volume/PVC by default; an
  explicit destructive workflow requires exact-target confirmation and is not
  used for rollback.
- `DEPLOY-011-L02`: a real Integrated Raft snapshot is created, transferred to
  protected operator-managed storage and restored into an isolated compatible
  cluster. The restored cluster proves its identity, policies, auth mounts and
  representative KV references without exposing secret values; backup does not
  substitute for three-node HA or recovery-key custody.
- `DEPLOY-011-E01`: a fresh Compose bundled installation completes TLS Vault
  initialization, manual unseal, AppRole/policy bootstrap and real
  Backend/Worker resolution; restart and snapshot/restore preserve the
  evidence, and public-port/no-leak scans pass.
- `DEPLOY-011-E02`: a fresh disposable multi-node Helm production installation
  completes auto-unseal or explicit Shamir acceptance, Raft join/quorum,
  Kubernetes Auth/policy bootstrap and real application resolution before app
  readiness. One Vault Pod loss and one worker-node disruption preserve quorum
  and resolution; a rolling upgrade preserves continuous authorized access.
- `DEPLOY-011-E03`: external mode connects to a real operator Vault with the
  same TLS/auth/policy/consumer contract while proving that the NomoSmart
  release owns no Vault workload or storage. Switching modes follows a
  documented snapshot/reference/compatibility procedure and never silently
  initializes or copies secrets.
- `DEPLOY-011-E04`: dependency, static, container and SBOM checks include the
  locked Vault chart and image. High/critical findings block release unless a
  named human risk acceptance is recorded; chart/image version, digest,
  license/notice inventory and scan evidence bind to the release source state.

- `OCR-003-I01`: a pinned real Tesseract binary processes a multilingual
  image/PDF corpus in a sandboxed non-root, no-network, bounded CPU/memory/time
  execution, persists binary-version/language snapshot and normal artifact
  evidence, and removes temporary input/output on success and failure.
- `OCR-003-I02`: malformed/oversize/decompression/resource/timeout/language-pack
  failures are observable and retryable as specified, with no deterministic
  text or hard-coded success fallback.
- `OCR-003-I03`: a real SFTP server uses a private key resolved through Vault;
  key passphrase and explicit known-host pinning are validated. Correct key
  succeeds; wrong/denied/missing key, wrong host key and passphrase failure fail
  closed. SSH agent and home-key discovery are disabled, ephemeral key material
  is removed, and no key bytes enter logs, API responses or persisted rows.

### Cursor, Deferred Webhook And Internationalization

- `API-PAGE-001-B01`: Notification, authorized Audit, Pipeline, Identity Sync,
  Approval My/Pending/History/Rejected, Validation history, Graph job and
  Integration Client/API-key inventories each use the shared versioned opaque
  cursor with immutable sort key plus unique tie-breaker, documented limit and
  stable envelope; clients cannot alter internal scope/filter state.
- `API-PAGE-001-B02`: insertion/deletion/update between pages produces no
  duplicate or skipped row within the defined snapshot/order contract; cursor
  reuse with a different actor, scope, filter or sort is rejected.
- `API-PAGE-001-B03`: malformed, expired and unauthorized cursors return stable
  errors without leaking hidden row IDs/counts. Integrity protection binds
  endpoint, actor, scope, filter and sort; bounded query plans use supporting
  indexes and do not materialize the complete list.
- `API-PAGE-001-B04`: the shared cursor codec/envelope/index foundation passes
  before consumer endpoints migrate; endpoint contract tests reject a
  consumer-specific unsigned or offset-wrapped implementation.
- `API-PAGE-001-F01`: affected UIs reset cursors on filter/scope changes,
  preserve loading/error/empty states and never combine results from
  incompatible cursor chains.

- `WEBHOOK-001-G01`: no generic webhook runtime route, UI, schema, advertised
  API or passing webhook behavior test exists in v1.0.
- `WEBHOOK-001-G02`: API compatibility, docs and traceability identify
  Integrations as owner, post-v1 target and the need for an approved companion
  spec covering authentication/HMAC, timestamp/replay, idempotency, events and
  Project authorization.

- `I18N-004-S01`: the formal AST/ESLint rule inspects JSX text and string
  expressions, placeholders, title/aria-label/tooltip, button/status/loading/
  empty/error/fallback copy and fixed locale-formatting calls.
- `I18N-004-S02`: negative fixtures for Traditional Chinese and English visible
  literals, inaccessible names, placeholders and `toLocaleString("zh-TW")`
  fail; protocol/technical stable fields pass only through narrow typed,
  reviewed allowlist entries.
- `I18N-004-S03`: zh/en locale keys, interpolation parameters, plural/format
  contracts and missing-key behavior are aligned; broad wildcard allowlists or
  hard-coded model/readiness copy fail policy.
- `I18N-004-E01`: Import, Chat, Validation, Submission, Approval, API Key,
  Notification and scoped Graph surfaces switch between zh/en at runtime
  without reload and update dates, numbers, errors, loaded content and
  accessible names at desktop and narrow widths.

### Migration, Regression And End-to-End Acceptance

- `CHG-247-M01`: all additive migrations pass fresh database, prior supported
  schema upgrade, rerun/idempotency, checksum, interrupted migration and
  release-evidence checks against real PostgreSQL.
- `CHG-247-M02`: compatibility data for historical report permissions,
  notifications, approvals, chunks, cursors and encrypted secret references is
  either deterministically backfilled or explicitly remains legacy/read-only;
  no fabricated evidence, active unknown credential or broad permission is
  introduced.
- `CHG-247-A01`: additive idempotency/cursor/evidence/capability contracts match
  `API_COMPATIBILITY.md` through Backend-first expand/contract: supported old
  and new clients remain compatible under mixed replicas, telemetry proves old
  mode retirement, and a later contract identity enforces the new form.
- `CHG-247-A02`: unscoped graph removal uses blue-green cutover (or the
  documented Backend-first 404 exception), proves scoped endpoints and old-route
  404 before traffic switch, isolates the old stack, and rejects rollback images
  that would re-register the retired routes or bypass the new security contract.
- `CHG-247-E01`: authenticated Owner, Editor, Viewer, System Admin, disabled and
  multi-role users execute the complete import → extract/edit → validate/chat →
  submit → manager/Owner decision → publish → scoped graph/report/notification
  journey using real dependencies.
- `CHG-247-E02`: archive during live Worker activity, Vault outage/renewal,
  dependency degradation, graph direct-ID probes, cursor concurrent writes and
  API key close/refresh exercise negative paths without content/secret leakage
  or false success.
- `CHG-247-E03`: responsive bilingual browser acceptance covers loading, empty,
  partial, denied, conflict, failure, retry and success states with keyboard
  operation, visible focus, 40px mobile targets and text/icon status semantics.
