## CHG-248 Guided, Resumable NomoSmart Kubernetes Installer Test Design

Gate 1 completed and Gate 2 was confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-28 with
`確認 CHG-248 Gate 2，接受上述範圍`. This Gate 3 design covers `DEPLOY-012`.
Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-07-28 with
`Peter approves CHG-248 Guided Resumable NomoSmart Kubernetes Installer`.
The cases below may now be implemented and executed within the approved scope;
destructive live cases use disposable targets unless separately authorized.

### Evidence Policy

- `TEST-002` remains controlling. Installer behavior that crosses a process,
  filesystem, Kubernetes, Helm, Vault, Keycloak, directory, DNS or HTTPS
  boundary must be tested with the real implementation and real isolated
  services. Mock command runners, fake API servers, canned success output and
  fixture providers cannot close acceptance.
- Temporary inputs and receipts use owner-only directories. Live resources use
  disposable clusters/releases/namespaces and exact labels; cleanup is
  separately verified and never targets the continuing UAT release by default.
- Test output records installer/chart/source identity, target cluster UID,
  config digest, exact command, start/end time, Helm revision, evidence paths
  and SHA-256 without credential material.
- Installer Python logic must reach at least 80% measured line and branch
  coverage. Frontend and Backend retain their independent 80% release gates.
  Template/runtime acceptance is additional and cannot be replaced by coverage.

### Configuration, CLI And Secret Safety

- `DEPLOY-012-C01`: parse a complete API-versioned TOML profile and reject an
  unknown API version, unknown key, wrong type, missing cluster UID/context,
  invalid enum, duplicate PGP fingerprint, relative/unsafe custody path,
  plaintext-secret-shaped field and unpinned production image.
- `DEPLOY-012-C02`: `plan/install/resume/status/verify/finalize` expose stable
  help and exit codes `0/10/20/30/40`; no subcommand accepts password, token,
  Vault share/root token, private key, bind credential or TOTP through argv.
- `DEPLOY-012-C03`: actual exceptions, nonzero `kubectl`/`helm`/Vault/Keycloak
  output, timeout, SIGINT and SIGTERM pass through one redaction layer. Seed
  unique canary secrets through protected files/Secrets and prove none appear
  in stdout, stderr, structured output, traceback, ConfigMap, receipt, Helm
  values/release metadata, support output or repository.
- `DEPLOY-012-C04`: secret package/custody inputs refuse symlinks, group/world
  access, overwrite and repository/package-contained Vault custody
  destinations. Generated directory/file modes are exactly `0700`/`0600` and
  writes are atomic after process termination.
- `DEPLOY-012-C05`: credential inventory includes endpoint, identity, Secret
  reference, custodian, generation and lifecycle state for every generated or
  referenced account, but contains no usable value. Designated service values
  exist only in the owner-only package or approved external secret system.

### Read-only Plan And Exact Target

- `DEPLOY-012-P01`: against a real conforming cluster, capture namespaces,
  resources and API audit/resource versions before/after `plan`; verify no
  namespace, ConfigMap, Lease, Secret, Job, Helm release or other mutation.
- `DEPLOY-012-P02`: use two real disposable clusters with different UIDs.
  Correct context/API/UID succeeds; wrong context, API identity or UID returns
  `20`, names the mismatch safely and mutates neither cluster.
- `DEPLOY-012-P03`: independently remove RBAC, one Ready node,
  StorageClass, IngressClass, referenced Secret/TLS key, trusted TLS, DNS
  resolution, image digest or production HA/Vault prerequisite. The earliest
  applicable check fails and no install state is created.
- `DEPLOY-012-P04`: create real namespace/release/resource collisions,
  including an unowned Secret with the desired name. Plan reports ownership
  conflict and install does not adopt, patch or overwrite it.
- `DEPLOY-012-P05`: an existing public hostname targeting another release is
  distinguished from a not-yet-created endpoint. Installer never edits DNS and
  never treats certificate-warning bypass as success.

### Lease, State And Resume

- `DEPLOY-012-S01`: start two real installer processes for one release. The
  first holds and renews a Kubernetes Lease; the second exits without mutation.
  Normal exit, SIGINT, SIGTERM, crash/expiry and resume prove bounded ownership
  and no permanent deadlock.
- `DEPLOY-012-S02`: inspect the installer ConfigMap and local receipt after
  every stage. They contain the config digest, target UID, generation, stage,
  postconditions, Helm revision, fingerprints and safe error only; no Secret,
  ciphertext or sensitive directory content is present.
- `DEPLOY-012-S03`: send SIGINT/SIGTERM immediately before and after each of the
  nine stages, then run `resume`. The same owned resource identities/PVCs/
  Secrets remain; the first incomplete stage resumes and no completed business
  effect is duplicated.
- `DEPLOY-012-S04`: after a safe checkpoint, alter cluster UID target, config
  digest, Helm ownership annotation, Secret/TLS fingerprint, release revision
  or owned resource fingerprint. Resume returns drift exit `40`, preserves all
  state and performs no automatic reconciliation.
- `DEPLOY-012-S05`: fail a Helm Job, dependency readiness and public HTTPS
  verification in turn. Exit `30` includes a sanitized next action; PVCs,
  Secrets, Jobs and prior checkpoint evidence remain available.

### Helm Deployment-stage Gate

- `DEPLOY-012-H01`: schema/render tests accept only
  `foundation|application|operational`; missing/invalid production stage or
  attempts to combine operational identity state with incomplete deployment
  evidence fail template rendering.
- `DEPLOY-012-H02`: a real `foundation` install creates the required stateful
  dependencies, Keycloak, ClamAV, Vault and bounded bootstrap assets, but no
  Flyway/application bootstrap Job, Backend, Worker, Beat, Frontend or public
  ready application route.
- `DEPLOY-012-H03`: while bundled Vault is uninitialized or sealed, attempts to
  select `application` fail before migration/app workloads. No readiness marker
  or Helm success is fabricated.
- `DEPLOY-012-H04`: after verified Vault bootstrap, transition to `application`
  and then `operational`; StatefulSet identities, PVC UIDs, Secret
  fingerprints and retained data are unchanged across Helm revisions.
- `DEPLOY-012-H05`: the documented manual Helm path uses the same stage
  contract. It cannot bypass Vault/application ordering or finalization.

### Package, Secrets And TLS

- `DEPLOY-012-K01`: a fresh owner-only package uses the existing package
  generator, produces distinct random identities and exact newline-free scalar
  Secret bytes, and records matching fingerprints.
- `DEPLOY-012-K02`: rerun with an identical package is idempotent. A non-empty
  unrelated directory, changed manifest, existing mismatching/unowned
  Kubernetes Secret or changed TLS key/certificate stops without overwrite.
- `DEPLOY-012-K03`: trusted existing TLS and generated TLS paths validate
  certificate/key match, SAN, chain, expiry and exact Secret keys. Wrong SAN,
  CA, key or namespace fails before Helm mutation.
- `DEPLOY-012-K04`: decode Helm release metadata and all generated ConfigMaps/
  receipts/logs; general credential values are present only in designated
  Kubernetes Secrets/operator package and never in Helm values/metadata or
  normal evidence.

### Real Vault Custody And Bootstrap

- `DEPLOY-012-V01`: on a disposable three-node real Integrated Raft release,
  five distinct PGP share recipients plus a root-token recipient produce
  exactly five encrypted shares with threshold three and encrypted root output
  directly in the external owner-controlled custody directory.
- `DEPLOY-012-V02`: cluster resources, generated package, state, receipt, logs,
  process arguments and repository contain no share/root plaintext,
  custodian private key or custody ciphertext. The installer retains only
  public-key fingerprints and safe status.
- `DEPLOY-012-V03`: three custodians use protected interactive input to unseal
  all three Pods. Inputs are not echoed/persisted; Raft shows three healthy
  peers/quorum before bootstrap continues.
- `DEPLOY-012-V04`: KV v2, audit, Kubernetes Auth, Backend/Worker policies/
  roles and sentinels are created once with least privilege. A rerun verifies
  rather than widens/duplicates them, and initial/temporary root authority is
  revoked before application stage.
- `DEPLOY-012-V05`: rerun against initialized/unsealed, initialized/sealed and
  partially available Vault never initializes again. The first state verifies,
  the second requests human unseal, and loss of quorum/TLS/auth/audit/policy
  fails closed.
- `DEPLOY-012-V06`: external and operator-configured auto-unseal modes skip
  only the Shamir ceremony and still prove TLS/hostname, seal, audit, auth,
  policy and application sentinel evidence.

### Migration, Application And Identity

- `DEPLOY-012-A01`: after Vault postconditions, real Flyway and bootstrap Jobs
  execute once, app workloads become Ready and the production placement/PDB
  rules hold. Re-running resume does not create duplicate migration,
  Keycloak/S3/bootstrap evidence or business rows.
- `DEPLOY-012-A02`: force a real migration, bootstrap and workload-readiness

## CHG-249 Script-driven Production Release And Installer Hardening Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-07-29 with the final Script-driven,
CI/CD-optional choice. Gate 3 test design is complete. Gate 4 was approved by
Peter on 2026-07-30 with
`Peter approves CHG-249 Script-driven Production Release And Installer Hardening`;
the cases below may execute within the approved target/custody boundaries.

### Release Source, Gate And Package Contracts

- `DEPLOY-013-R01`: on an isolated Linux builder, checkout an exact full commit
  SHA in detached state and run the provider-neutral release CLI without any
  `GITHUB_*`, `GITLAB_*` or Jenkins variables. The manifest records the exact
  source/diff/tool fingerprint and a repeated same-input run is deterministic.
- `DEPLOY-013-R02`: independently introduce tracked modification, prohibited
  untracked `.env`, kubeconfig, registry credential, private key, symlink escape
  and ambiguous/non-full revision. Each fails before image build/package/sign
  and protected file content never appears in output.
- `DEPLOY-013-R03`: independently fail specification, plan approval, Frontend
  test, Backend test, installer test, Frontend 80%, Backend 80%, dependency
  scan, container scan, license, SPDX and image-digest gates. Production
  package/sign/publish is blocked with a stable redacted evidence classification.
- `DEPLOY-013-R04`: validate the release-manifest schema and exact chart,
  dependency, file, image, compatibility and evidence digests. Missing,
  duplicated, foreign-source or altered evidence is rejected.
- `DEPLOY-013-R05`: sign with a dedicated test release key and verify with the
  allowed public fingerprint. Wrong signer, missing signature, modified
  manifest/file, wrong checksum, expired/revoked test key policy and custody-key
  substitution all fail before installer mutation.
- `DEPLOY-013-R06`: inspect the final package recursively. It contains installer
  runtime, Helm/dependencies, safe examples, evidence and docs but no
  application source build context, `.env`, credential, kubeconfig, private key,
  Vault custody ciphertext/share or generic temp/build directory.
- `DEPLOY-013-R07`: remove Git, Docker, Podman, Buildah and CI executables/
  credentials from the installer host PATH/context. Verified package
  `plan/install/resume/verify` uses only prebuilt digest-pinned registry images.
- `DEPLOY-013-R08`: use a typed registry mirror containing the same approved
  digest and then a same-tag/different-digest image. The first passes; the
  second fails before workload rollout.

### Doctor And Reset Safety

- `DEPLOY-013-D01`: create matching, missing and independently drifted local
  state, installer ConfigMap, Namespace metadata, Lease, Helm identity and owned
  resources. `doctor` emits complete redacted JSON classifications and performs
  zero mutation.
- `DEPLOY-013-D02`: for a failed/incomplete/abandoned non-operational attempt,
  `reset-plan` binds cluster UID, namespace, release, install/config/resource
  identity, exact remove/retain inventory and canonical plan digest with zero
  mutation.
- `DEPLOY-013-D03`: `reset-apply` with the exact current plan digest removes
  only listed installer-owned transient state, archives local state with
  `0700`/`0600` protection and leaves Rancher/Kubernetes metadata, input Secrets
  and retained resources unchanged.
- `DEPLOY-013-D04`: operational Helm release, PVC/PV, Vault data/audit,
  application business data, external input Secret, foreign owner, wrong
  cluster/config/resource digest or expanded delete target is refused.
- `DEPLOY-013-D05`: stale/replayed plan, concurrent state change, active Lease
  or second reset process fails compare-and-set without partial cleanup.

### Interruption, Job And Vault Recovery

- `DEPLOY-013-S01`: send SIGINT and SIGTERM while every supported Helm/kubectl/
  Vault/GnuPG subprocess is starting, running and completing. The entire owned
  process group receives the signal, bounded cleanup occurs, matching Lease is
  released and completed-stage evidence remains resumable.
- `DEPLOY-013-S02`: force an uncatchable process termination. Lease remains
  unavailable before TTL, becomes safely recoverable after TTL and a foreign
  holder is never deleted by the new process.
- `DEPLOY-013-S03`: make migration, bootstrap, directory and finalization Jobs
  enter `Failed=True`, backoff limit and deadline/terminal Pod failure. Installer
  returns the stable redacted reason within the polling bound rather than the
  full Complete timeout.
- `DEPLOY-013-S04`: exercise real transient scheduling/container/DNS/listener/
  status visibility and permanent TLS hostname/CA, RBAC, configuration and
  policy failures. Only the transient set retries with bounded exponential
  backoff; no security side effect repeats.
- `DEPLOY-013-S05`: on a host without `curl`, the Python TLS client verifies
  public Frontend, Backend readiness and OIDC with trusted CA/hostname/SNI,
  bounded redirect/body/timeout and safe error output.

### GnuPG And Directory Boundary

- `DEPLOY-013-V01`: initialize real disposable Vault with five distinct
  GnuPG-recipient shares and threshold three. Three valid custodians complete
  unseal; two shares, wrong private key, duplicate share, reordered inputs,
  damaged ciphertext and incompatible key usage fail safely.
- `DEPLOY-013-V02`: run the supported GnuPG-version matrix and scan argv,
  process environment, temp paths, package, cluster, logs, state, receipt and
  support evidence. No plaintext share/passphrase/private material is present;
  ephemeral GNUPGHOME is owner-only and removed.
- `DEPLOY-013-I01`: against real OpenLDAP with multi-valued `cn`, installer
  reports a safe data-quality warning and still never writes directory data.
  After a separately approved operator backup/normalization, `uid`, canonical
  `cn`, `displayName`, Keycloak sync and NomoSmart identity remain correct.

### End-to-end And Regression

- `DEPLOY-013-E01`: from a clean commit, manually trigger one complete release
  on an isolated builder, transfer only the signed package, install on a clean
  operator host without source/build/CI tooling, complete real Shamir and TOTP
  checkpoints and obtain an operational receipt with services left running.
- `DEPLOY-013-E02`: repeat CHG-248 FreeIPA and OpenLDAP configuration parsing,
  stage render, full sync/mapping, interruption/resume/finalization and public

- `DEPLOY-013-E03`: render the bundled Keycloak ingress NetworkPolicy and require

### CHG-249 one-click operator wrapper

The wrapper is a thin entry point and must not duplicate installer behavior:

- `OLI-041`: `--help` works without a cluster or config, while missing
  config/unknown options fail with exit 20 and no child installer invocation.
- `OLI-042`: every invocation runs the installer `plan` first; the
  displayed `config_digest` is required for interactive `APPLY` confirmation or
  an exact `--confirm-digest`, and a non-interactive invocation without explicit
  confirmation returns action-required exit 10 without mutation.
- `OLI-043`: redacted status `not-installed` selects `install`,
  `in-progress` selects `resume`, and `complete` selects `verify`; a successful
  install/resume then runs `status` and `verify` and leaves services running.
- `OLI-044`: the wrapper exposes no factory-reset/permanent-delete path,
  never receives secret values, and is included with executable mode in a signed
  release package.

Automated coverage is `deploy/installer/tests/test_one_click.py`, shell syntax
is checked with `sh -n`, and release packaging asserts the wrapper is present
and executable. Live cluster behavior remains the responsibility of the
underlying installer acceptance cases above.

## CHG-250 AI Model Readiness And Localized Operational Messaging Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-08-03 with `三項都同意`. Gate 3 test
design is complete. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-08-03 with
`Peter approves CHG-250 AI Model Readiness And Localized Operational Messaging`;
the feature and live cases below may execute within the approved plan.

### PROJECT-007 Backend And Data Integrity

- `PROJECT-007-B01`: against real PostgreSQL and the live Backend API, submit
  Create Project independently without Chat, OCR or Embedding ID, then without
  each two-type combination and without all three. Every request returns
  `422 project_model_configuration_required`, reports the exact unique
  `details.missing_model_types` subset and request ID, and creates no Project,
  ProjectOwner, ProjectMember or success audit row.
- `PROJECT-007-B02`: independently submit inactive, soft-deleted, nonexistent and
  wrong-type IDs for each position. The Backend rejects the request using the
  stable configuration error without leaking a cross-scope/internal row and
  leaves all project-side tables unchanged.
- `PROJECT-007-B03`: create real active Chat and Embedding models that have an
  explicit incompatible pairing, then cover model-group and provider fallback
  incompatibility. The Backend returns `422 project_model_pair_required` and
  cannot be bypassed by choosing an arbitrary active Embedding row.
- `PROJECT-007-B04`: create one active non-deleted OCR model and a valid active
  Chat/Embedding pair through supported model configuration, then create a
  project. The response and PostgreSQL row contain all three IDs, the creator is
  Owner, the audit is written once and a list/read response reports 3/3 model
  completeness.
- `PROJECT-007-B05`: retain a pre-existing incomplete project row and verify it
  remains readable/incomplete without automatic assignment. Updating a complete
  project while omitting unrelated fields preserves all model references; an
  attempt to clear any required model fails without partial mutation.
- `PROJECT-007-B06`: load a valid inventory, then deactivate/delete/re-pair one
  selected model before submit. Transaction-time validation rejects the stale
  request and creates no partial project; a refreshed valid selection succeeds.

These cases must use real persisted model rows and the live API. Direct service
monkeypatching, mocked SQLAlchemy sessions or fake model adapters cannot satisfy
behavioral acceptance.

### PROJECT-007 Frontend, Permission And Accessibility

- `PROJECT-007-F01`: with the real models request delayed by a real configured
  service condition and then restored, Create Project distinguishes inventory
  loading, load failure/retry and loaded-empty states. It never labels a request
  error as "no models configured" and Create remains disabled until ready.
- `PROJECT-007-F02`: with live inventory missing Chat only, OCR only, Embedding
  only, every two-type combination and all three, the Modal shows one concise
  summary plus the matching section guidance, lists every missing type and
  exposes an accessible disabled reason. No submit request is emitted.
- `PROJECT-007-F03`: a user with live `SystemManagement.view` receives a
  keyboard-accessible action to `/system?tab=models`. A project creator without
  that grant receives localized contact-administrator guidance and no forbidden
  link. Revoking the grant and reloading auth context changes the action.
- `PROJECT-007-F04`: selecting a Chat model filters to compatible active
  Embedding models. No compatible pair, only inactive pairs and stale pairing
  errors all keep submit disabled and display a localized reason; a valid pair
  auto-selection is visible and all three IDs are sent explicitly.
- `PROJECT-007-F05`: at 1440, 1024, 768 and 375px, longest zh/en summaries and
  model names do not overlap, clip or create page-level horizontal scroll.
  Alert type/icon/text, focus order, visible focus ring, Enter/Space activation,
  close/cancel and at least 40px mobile targets remain usable; status is not
  communicated by color alone.
- `PROJECT-007-E01`: authenticated live Browser journeys cover an authorized
  System administrator/project creator and a create-only non-administrator,
  verify missing-to-ready recovery after real model creation/activation, then
  create one project and observe the 3/3 card without reload-dependent copy.

### I18N-005 Static And Contract Guards

- `I18N-005-S01`: `zh.json` and `en.json` have identical keys, interpolation
  parameters, plural and formatting contracts for every new/migrated message.
  Removing one key or changing one placeholder makes the guard fail.
- `I18N-005-S02`: negative fixtures add hard-coded Traditional Chinese and
  English JSX text, string expressions, placeholder, title, tooltip,
  `aria-label`, screen-reader copy, fallback/error text and fixed locale
  formatting. The AST/ESLint guard rejects each fixture.
- `I18N-005-S03`: the reviewed allowlist accepts only stable protocol/API/CSV

Static guards are necessary but do not replace rendered/live acceptance.

## CHG-251 Three-node OpenSearch And Internal TLS Test Design

### Gate And Evidence Policy

Peter confirmed Gate 2 on 2026-08-04 with `確認 CHG-251 Gate 2，憑證採自建
OpenSearch 私有 CA，其餘接受建議方案。` Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-04
with `Peter approves CHG-251 Three-node OpenSearch And Internal TLS，更新Project:
NomoSmart內的Namespace: Nomosmart`. The cases below may now execute against the
approved exact target and must retain their live-only evidence rules.

`TEST-002` applies without exception. Helm rendering can prove manifest shape
but cannot prove TLS negotiation, cluster formation, snapshot restore, quorum,
data preservation or disruption behavior. Those cases require real OpenSearch
2.19.6, real certificate parsing/handshakes, real RustFS/S3, real PVCs and a real
three-node Kubernetes cluster. Unavailable prerequisites are BLOCKED, never a
mocked or static PASS.

The final image gate records Peter's 2026-08-04 UAT-only acceptance of the
OpenSearch 2.19.6 base's Docker Scout residual 1 Critical/34 High results. The
exception is valid only with no public OpenSearch endpoint plus TLS,
NetworkPolicy and authentication controls, and must not pass the Production
release security gate. Any count above that accepted baseline, any new finding
introduced by the derived layer or missing evidence fails closed.

### Package And Certificate Cases

- `DEPLOY-014-P01`: package generation creates one CA certificate, one HTTP leaf
  and one transport leaf; all parse, chain to the same private CA, are within
  validity and use non-placeholder serials/keys.
- `DEPLOY-014-P02`: CA has critical `CA:TRUE`; HTTP leaf has `CA:FALSE` and
  `serverAuth`; transport leaf has `CA:FALSE`, `serverAuth` and `clientAuth`.
- `DEPLOY-014-P03`: HTTP SANs contain the actual client Service short/FQDN;
  transport SANs contain release/namespace headless short/FQDN plus all three
  StatefulSet Pod short/FQDN identities. Wrong release, namespace, ordinal or
  missing wildcard/exact identity fails preflight.
- `DEPLOY-014-P04`: transport subject DN exactly matches the rendered
  `plugins.security.nodes_dn`; an unknown DN, unknown CA, expired leaf, swapped
  HTTP/transport key or mismatched private key is rejected.
- `DEPLOY-014-P05`: the generator performs no FreeIPA/cert-manager/public-CA
  call. Network-denied generation produces the same valid local hierarchy.
- `DEPLOY-014-P06`: CA signing key exists in plaintext only in the owner-only
  ephemeral workspace, is encrypted to the selected PGP recipient, ciphertext
  fingerprint/decryptability is verified, and plaintext is removed after leaf
  issuance. Wrong recipient, failed encryption or failed decryptability stops
  package completion.
- `DEPLOY-014-P07`: recursive scans of Git status/diff, generated package,
  release archive, Kubernetes Secret render, values, installer state/receipt,
  command transcript, logs and support bundle find no plaintext CA signing key,
  PGP private key/passphrase, S3 secret or OpenSearch password.
- `DEPLOY-014-P08`: repeated normal generation does not overwrite active CA/
  leaf/custody material; explicit rotation creates a new generation/fingerprint
  and preserves the previous generation for rollback.
- `DEPLOY-014-P09`: installer examples contain simple comments and safe example
  references for CA recipient/custody destination and TLS Secret generation,
  but no real fingerprint, path, credential or private material.

### Image And Snapshot Supply-chain Cases

- `DEPLOY-014-I01`: derived image uses the exact approved OpenSearch 2.19.6 base
  digest and installs only the matching official `repository-s3` plugin during
  build; no runtime download, floating tag or unrelated plugin is present.
- `DEPLOY-014-I02`: image manifest/digest, plugin list/version, license
  inventory, SPDX SBOM and CVE report are complete and bound to the release
  evidence. High/critical findings fail unless separately accepted by Peter.
- `DEPLOY-014-I03`: production values reference the approved derived digest;
  mutable tag-only, base image without repository-s3, wrong plugin version or
  missing evidence fails before rollout.
- `DEPLOY-014-S01`: RustFS snapshot bucket and least-privilege identity are
  idempotently created/verified. Credential enters OpenSearch keystore via
  Secret/stdin, is absent from env/argv/log/API output and cannot access an
  unrelated bucket.
- `DEPLOY-014-S02`: repository registration uses `https://` RustFS endpoint,
  path-style compatibility and a truststore containing the RustFS CA. Wrong CA,
  hostname, HTTP endpoint or verify-disabled setting fails.
- `DEPLOY-014-S03`: repository `_verify` succeeds on the real nodes; a native
  snapshot reaches `SUCCESS`, contains the expected NomoSmart-owned indices and
  records no credential in snapshot metadata or operational evidence.
- `DEPLOY-014-S04`: a representative index restores under a unique temporary
  renamed name with matching mapping/document count; the temporary restored
  index can be deleted without touching the source index or snapshot.
- `DEPLOY-014-S05`: failed plugin, bucket, credential, TLS, repository verify,
  partial snapshot, failed restore or count mismatch blocks migration and leaves
  node-0/PVC/release unchanged.

### Helm Render, Schema And Preflight Cases

- `DEPLOY-014-H01`: production render has one OpenSearch StatefulSet with
  exactly three replicas, `podManagementPolicy: Parallel`, stable combined
  roles, three retained RWO PVC claims and no `discovery.type=single-node`.
- `DEPLOY-014-H02`: hard `kubernetes.io/hostname` anti-affinity separates peer
  Pods; PDB `minAvailable` is at least two. Soft affinity, fewer than three
  replicas/nodes or absent PDB fails production policy.
- `DEPLOY-014-H03`: client ClusterIP contains only HTTPS 9200 and headless
  discovery Service contains only transport 9300 with the required peer
  discovery behavior. No Ingress, NodePort, LoadBalancer, host port or 9600
  Service is rendered.
- `DEPLOY-014-H04`: container effective configuration points HTTP and transport
  TLS to the new mounted paths, sets trusted CA/node DN and transport hostname
  verification true, and has no active demo `esnode.pem`/`root-ca.pem`,
  skip-verify or hostname-verification-false reference.
- `DEPLOY-014-H05`: only empty data paths receive the exact three initial
  cluster-manager names; an existing node-0 path does not. Ordered pod startup,
  permanent initial-manager replay or a name mismatch fails.
- `DEPLOY-014-H06`: readiness performs authenticated local HTTPS with CA and
  correct hostname while permitting all Parallel peers to start. Plain TCP-only
  readiness cannot close TLS acceptance.
- `DEPLOY-014-H07`: NetworkPolicy permits allowed application identities to
  9200, same-release OpenSearch peers to 9300 and OpenSearch snapshot traffic to
  RustFS 9000; unrelated Pods, other releases and all 9600 traffic remain
  denied.
- `DEPLOY-014-H08`: values schema and template fail on missing TLS keys, SAN/DN
  identity, persistence, headless service, snapshot plugin/repository, PDB,
  anti-affinity or production replica count.
- `DEPLOY-014-H09`: cluster preflight verifies three schedulable nodes,
  StorageClass/PVC capacity, referenced generation-specific Secret keys,
  derived image identity and current installer operational phase before any
  Helm/stateful mutation.
- `DEPLOY-014-H10`: external mode renders no bundled OpenSearch StatefulSet,
  PDB, PVC, headless Service or self-issued TLS Secret; Compose remains explicit
  single-node non-HA and cannot satisfy this Helm HA requirement.
- `DEPLOY-014-H11`: Helm uninstall/rollback policies retain all three PVCs;
  scaling down does not delete claims. No lifecycle test may use PVC deletion as
  rollback.
- `DEPLOY-014-H12`: chart/install documentation gives exact fresh install,
  staged existing migration, snapshot/restore, certificate rotation, rollback,
  diagnostics and explicit cleanup procedures.

### Live TLS And Network Cases

- `DEPLOY-014-T01`: allowed Backend/Worker/bootstrap identities connect to
  `https://nomosmart-opensearch:9200` with the mounted CA and service hostname;
  certificate subject/SAN/fingerprint is the new generation.
- `DEPLOY-014-T02`: plain HTTP 9200, wrong hostname, unknown CA, expired/mismatched
  leaf and disabled verification all fail; no client warning bypass is used.
- `DEPLOY-014-T03`: every peer-to-peer 9300 connection negotiates TLS using the
  private CA transport leaf; effective settings show hostname verification true
  and the approved node DN. Demo certificate fingerprints are not active.
- `DEPLOY-014-T04`: unknown node DN/CA/hostname cannot join. An unrelated Pod
  cannot reach 9300 even with network reachability attempts; an OpenSearch peer
  from the same release can.
- `DEPLOY-014-T05`: 9600 is absent from Services and denied from another Pod;
  no plaintext monitoring request is included in acceptance.
- `DEPLOY-014-T06`: snapshot traffic reaches only TLS RustFS 9000 with verified
  CA/hostname. HTTP or an unrelated RustFS identity/bucket is rejected.

### Existing-cluster Migration And Data Cases

- `DEPLOY-014-M01`: pre-migration evidence captures cluster UUID, exact node,
  health, index/settings/mapping/document counts, current TLS fingerprints,
  StatefulSet/PVC/PV/Longhorn identities and installer operational state without
  printing Secret values.
- `DEPLOY-014-M02`: migration refuses to begin until installer onboarding/TOTP
  finalization is operational, native snapshot/renamed restore succeeds,
  quiesced volume recovery point exists and old manifest/Secret generation is
  retained.
- `DEPLOY-014-M03`: node-0 restarts on the original PVC with the same cluster
  UUID/data, formal discovery and new HTTP/transport TLS. It does not receive
  fresh initial-manager bootstrap and does not form a second cluster.
- `DEPLOY-014-M04`: node-1/node-2 each receive a distinct retained PVC and join
  node-0 with the expected names/roles/DNs. Wrong UUID, rejected certificate or
  join timeout stops before write traffic resumes.
- `DEPLOY-014-M05`: known NomoSmart index templates/existing indices use one
  replica; vendor/system indices are not broadly rewritten. Final cluster is
  green with `number_of_nodes=3`, `number_of_data_nodes=3` and zero unassigned
  shards.
- `DEPLOY-014-M06`: pre/post cluster UUID, NomoSmart index mapping/count and
  representative document/retrieval results match. Real authenticated Backend
  retrieval and index write/read succeed through HTTPS after writes resume.
- `DEPLOY-014-M07`: NomoSmart Frontend, Backend, Worker/Beat and dependent
  services return to their expected readiness and remain running for UAT. No
  OpenLDAP, RKE2, Rancher, Registry or external DNS resource changes.

### Disruption, Rollback And Retention Cases

- `DEPLOY-014-D01`: delete each OpenSearch Pod one at a time while issuing real
  HTTPS query/index traffic; remaining two keep cluster-manager quorum and
  service, recovered peer rejoins and health returns green/zero-unassigned.
- `DEPLOY-014-D02`: one controlled Kubernetes-node disruption retains two-node
  quorum and queries; recovery/rebalance preserves counts. PDB blocks voluntary
  disruption that would reduce availability below two.
- `DEPLOY-014-D03`: simultaneous two-node loss is reported unavailable/fail
  closed with safe evidence and no PostgreSQL/fixture search fallback; it is not
  claimed as an availability pass.
- `DEPLOY-014-R01`: node-0 configuration/TLS failure before peer join rolls back
  to the old manifest/Secret and original PVC without reinitialization.
- `DEPLOY-014-R02`: a post-join compatible rollback retains all PVCs and returns
  to a documented safe topology. If node-0 data is unusable, restore from the
  quiesced recovery point or verified native snapshot and revalidate UUID/data/
  TLS before reopening writes.
- `DEPLOY-014-R03`: successful migration does not automatically delete old TLS
  Secret, CA custody ciphertext, native snapshot, RustFS objects, PVC/PV or
  Longhorn recovery point. Cleanup requires an exact-target human approval.

## CHG-252 Production HA Stack And Factory Reinstall

Status: Gate 2 confirmed and Gate 3 test design written on 2026-08-04. Peter
approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-04. Repository, non-destructive release-preparation
and disposable feature/live cases are authorized; exact-UAT deletion and live
operational-release mutation remain blocked pending the separate factory-plan
approval. Static renders, mocked failover or Pod counts cannot be recorded as
passing HA evidence.

### Governance, Schema And Preflight

- `DEPLOY-015-G01`: specification/changelog/plan/test/traceability agree on the
  exact components, three existing Kubernetes nodes, RustFS `2/1/1` exception,
  Neo4j single-node exception, factory-reset boundary and Gate 4/deletion status.
- `DEPLOY-015-G02`: production values schema rejects PostgreSQL instances other
  than three, Redis data/Sentinel counts other than three, Sentinel quorum other
  than two, Beat replicas other than two, RustFS replicas other than four,
  Keycloak replicas other than three, ClamAV replicas below two and OpenSearch
  replicas other than three.
- `DEPLOY-015-G03`: render policy requires all expected PDBs, retained PVCs,
  discovery Services, stable client Services, topology controls, readiness,
  ServiceAccounts/RBAC, NetworkPolicies and digest-pinned images; it rejects
  plaintext ports, public native endpoints and secret literals.
- `DEPLOY-015-G04`: exact cluster preflight sees Kubernetes
  `v1.35.6+rke2r1`, three Ready/schedulable nodes, RKE2/Longhorn capacity,
  Namespace UID/Project ownership and CloudNativePG version compatibility.
  Missing capacity, node, StorageClass, CRD compatibility or permissions stops
  before live deletion or stateful creation.
- `DEPLOY-015-G05`: capacity evidence includes per-node requested/limit
  headroom, raw/free Longhorn space, logical and physical PVC amplification,
  data locality and correlated node/volume failures for every stateful replica.
  Static/render evidence must total exactly 22 retained PVCs and 485 GiB;
  live preflight must reject a non-Longhorn class, missing/implicit or non-one
  `numberOfReplicas`, unapproved data locality, fewer/more than three Ready
  schedulable nodes, node allocatable below 7000m/28Gi, or failure of the
  20% CPU/RAM and 25% prospective physical-storage reserve after current
  non-NomoSmart requests and exact reclaimable NomoSmart bytes are accounted.
- `DEPLOY-015-G06`: every operator/workload image has exact manifest/platform
  digest, license inventory, SPDX SBOM and CVE evidence; unresolved High/
  Critical findings prevent release absent explicit component-specific risk
  acceptance.

### CloudNativePG And PostgreSQL

- `DEPLOY-015-P01`: CloudNativePG `1.30.0` CRDs/operator render with pinned
  digest, explicit `cnpg-system` ownership, constrained watch/RBAC and live
  Kubernetes-version compatibility; floating/latest or unsupported CRDs fail.
- `DEPLOY-015-P02`: one fresh PostgreSQL 18.4 `Cluster` has three instances,
  hard hostname anti-affinity, three distinct retained PVCs, stable read-write
  Service, PDB and synchronous quorum `ANY 1`/failover quorum configuration.
- `DEPLOY-015-P03`: declarative/bootstrap database and roles create separate
  admin, NomoSmart app, migration and Keycloak identities idempotently; each
  client gets only its required privileges and repeated install changes no
  credential or owner unexpectedly.
- `DEPLOY-015-P04`: server/client/replication certificate chain, SAN, EKU,
  expiry and Secret keys pass. Backend, Worker, Flyway and Keycloak use
  `verify-full`; plain TCP, wrong hostname, unknown CA and unrelated Pod fail.
- `DEPLOY-015-P05`: real writes on both NomoSmart and Keycloak databases show
  synchronous replicas streaming with bounded zero lag and the expected
  `pg_stat_replication`/CNPG status without exposing credentials.
- `DEPLOY-015-P06`: kill the primary Pod during committed transactions; one
  replica is promoted in bounded time, the `-rw` Service moves, acknowledged
  rows and Keycloak identities persist, clients reconnect and no split primary
  exists.
- `DEPLOY-015-P07`: non-voluntary loss of each Kubernetes node repeats P06;
  recovered instance rejoins the new timeline and the cluster returns to three
  healthy instances without manual data copy.
- `DEPLOY-015-P08`: network partition, stale primary, webhook/operator restart,

- `DEPLOY-015-P09`: encrypted full backup plus WAL reaches TLS RustFS after its
  readiness, and an isolated disposable Cluster restores to a selected point
  with matching schema/count/checksum and independent credentials.
  Static evidence must additionally prove Barman Cloud CNPG-I `0.13.0`
  operator/sidecar digests, existing cert-manager self-signed plugin mTLS,
  RustFS `endpointCA`, AES256 data/WAL encryption, six-field schedule, the
  foundation bucket-before-plugin boundary and a Completed backup plus non-empty

- `DEPLOY-015-P10`: Helm/application uninstall, failed bootstrap and operator
  restart do not delete PostgreSQL PVCs/backups; explicit factory deletion is
  the only path allowed to target them.

### Redis Sentinel And Clients

- `DEPLOY-015-R01`: render/live topology has three hard-spread Redis data Pods,

- `DEPLOY-015-R02`: service ACL, admin and replication/Sentinel credentials are

- `DEPLOY-015-R09`: restart/upgrade/rollback retains AOF/PVC data, topology and

### Celery Beat Lease

- `DEPLOY-015-B07`: Lease/status/log/metrics expose holder identity, renewal age

- `DEPLOY-015-S01`: one StatefulSet renders four stable identities, four

## CHG-253 Single-node PostgreSQL Factory Reinstall

Gate 2 was confirmed by Peter on 2026-08-05. Gate 4 was approved on 2026-08-05
with `Peter approves CHG-253 Single-node PostgreSQL Factory Reinstall`.
Repository implementation and disposable tests may proceed; the exact live
factory apply still requires its own digest-bound permanent-delete approval.

### Governance, Schema And Render

- `DEPLOY-016-G01`: specification, changelog, plan, test plan and traceability
  agree that CHG-253 overrides only the exact-UAT PostgreSQL topology and full
  factory generation; Redis/Sentinel and every other CHG-252 topology remain.
- `DEPLOY-016-G02`: values schema accepts exactly one mutually exclusive
  PostgreSQL architecture. `standalone` requires replicas one and rejects CNPG
  values/resources; `cloudnativepg` retains the approved three-instance profile
  and rejects standalone-only values. Production render cannot accidentally
  include both or neither.
- `DEPLOY-016-G03`: standalone render contains exactly one `apps/v1`
  StatefulSet Pod, one retained RWO PVC, stable read-write/headless Services,
  one minAvailable PDB, probes, resources, security context, TLS mounts,
  NetworkPolicy and explicit non-HA status. It contains no namespaced CNPG
  Cluster/Backup/ScheduledBackup/ObjectStore resource.
- `DEPLOY-016-G04`: exact capacity planning proves the one PostgreSQL PVC uses
  a Longhorn three-replica class with replicas on three distinct storage nodes,
  sufficient raw capacity/reserve and safe RWO detach/reattach. Negative cases
  reject unknown class parameters, correlated placement, insufficient capacity
  and a silent fallback to one storage replica.
- `DEPLOY-016-G05`: the selected PostgreSQL and backup/helper images have exact
  linux/amd64 digest, signature, SPDX 2.3, license and accepted CVE evidence;
  release inventory omits unused CNPG/Barman runtime images for the standalone
  exact target while retaining profile source compatibility.

### PostgreSQL, TLS, Bootstrap And Recovery

- `DEPLOY-016-P01`: fresh standalone PostgreSQL initializes one data directory
  and accepts only CA/hostname-verified TLS through the stable Service. Plain,
  wrong-CA, wrong-hostname, unauthorized and fixed-Pod endpoint cases fail.
- `DEPLOY-016-P02`: administrator, NomoSmart application, Flyway, Keycloak and
  backup identities are distinct, least-privilege and sourced from Secret
  references without values in chart output, argv, logs, receipts or files.
- `DEPLOY-016-P03`: fresh bootstrap idempotently creates separate `nomosmart`
  and `keycloak` databases/owners, applies all Flyway migrations, initializes
  Keycloak realm/client/OpenLDAP federation and blocks every downstream
  readiness path on partial database, grants, migration or realm failure.
- `DEPLOY-016-P04`: real NomoSmart and Keycloak writes survive a PostgreSQL Pod

- `DEPLOY-016-P05`: kill the only PostgreSQL Pod and then interrupt its node
  under real transactions. The service becomes unavailable without a false
  promotion/HA claim; after Longhorn fencing and safe volume reattach, the Pod

- `DEPLOY-016-P06`: after fresh finalization, the new generation creates an
  encrypted logical full backup over private-CA RustFS. An isolated Namespace
  with independent read-only restore credentials restores both databases,
  globals/roles, Flyway history and representative rows with matching counts
  and checksums. Receipt states the schedule/retention, maximum scheduled RPO,
  measured RTO and absence of standalone PITR/HA.

### Factory Safety And Full-system Acceptance

- `DEPLOY-016-F01`: read-only exact inventory binds cluster/Namespace/release

  NomoSmart Helm/data/Secret/PVC/PV/Longhorn Volume/Snapshot/backup targets

## CHG-254 HOME-003 Dynamic Home KPI Helper Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-08-07 with `同意 HOME-003`; Gate 4
approved by Peter on 2026-08-07 with `Peter approves CHG-254 HOME-003 Dynamic
Home KPI Helper Correction`. Implementation and focused verification are complete.

### HOME-003 Functional And Data Contract Cases

- `HOME-003-F01`: with real `/projects` data in the authenticated user's visible
  scope, the Home active-project helper counts only `status = active` rows whose
  `last_activity_at` falls on the current browser-local calendar day. Project,
  Document and DocumentVersion activity represented by the existing Backend
  `last_activity_at` projection is included; missing timestamps are excluded.
- `HOME-003-F02`: the Home Owner helper renders the live
  `ApprovalSummary.pending_owner_review` value from the authorized summary

  synthetic fallback. Existing active-project and approval-queue cards retain

- `HOME-003-F05`: when the browser crosses local midnight and Home re-renders or
  refreshes, today’s project count uses the new calendar day. Time comparisons

## CHG-255 Keycloak Cascaded Identity Synchronization Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-08-08 with `同意 CHG-255 Gate 2`.
Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-08-08 with
`Peter approves CHG-255 Keycloak Cascaded Identity Synchronization`.
Repository implementation and non-destructive verification are authorized;
current-UAT directory/realm mutation remains separately gated.

Requirements under test: new `AUTH-017`, refined `AUTH-012`, `AUTH-014` and
`AUTH-015`, with regression coverage for `ROLE-002`, `SYS-001`, `SYS-002`,
`I18N-005`, `API-001`, `API-PAGE-001`, `DEPLOY-004`, `SEC-001` and `TEST-002`.

### Test Environment And Evidence

- Use a disposable PostgreSQL database/schema with V001-V043, isolated Redis
  namespace, real Celery worker/Beat, a disposable Keycloak realm and sync
  service account, and one or more isolated OpenLDAP subtrees/providers.
- Passing behavior must invoke real Keycloak user-storage and LDAP mapper
  fed-to-Keycloak endpoints. `MockTransport`, mocked/stubbed Keycloak clients,
  fixture LDAP inventories, eager Celery or hard-coded success cannot satisfy
  behavioral acceptance.
- Create test users/groups after a recorded earlier Keycloak sync so the test
  proves the NomoSmart button itself causes upstream refresh. Use only
  disposable directory entries and remove them, realm/provider data, Redis
  events and database rows after success or failure.
- Capture only provider IDs/names, scope, phase, status, safe counters, timing,
  stable codes and before/after identity hashes. Never capture token, bind
  credential, component JSON, endpoint, DN, Filter original value, password,
  raw Keycloak/LDAP error or directory-sensitive content.
- Frontend Browser acceptance uses real edit-capable and view-only OIDC users.
  Missing live services, principals or credentials is BLOCKED, not a passing
  static substitute.

### Migration And Persistence Cases

- `AUTH-017-M01`: fresh V043 creates constrained `requested_scope`/`phase`
  columns and provider-result table, unique run/provider identity, non-negative
  counters, indexes and FKs; Flyway rerun is idempotent.
- `AUTH-017-M02`: populated V028 history upgrades without loss. Terminal rows
  receive safe scope/phase defaults, active rows remain recoverable, and no
  fabricated provider-success row appears.
- `AUTH-017-M03`: invalid scope, phase, status, duplicate provider result and
  negative counter writes fail transactionally; existing users/groups/roles
  and successful sync history remain unchanged.
- `AUTH-017-M04`: rollback guidance retains additive V043 columns/table and
  history; an older compatible binary can be restored without destructive down
  migration or identity-data truncation.

### Keycloak Provider And Scope Cases

- `AUTH-017-K01`: one enabled OpenLDAP provider with a new user and new
  `groupOfNames` group executes user full sync then group-mapper
  `fedToKeycloak`; the fresh Keycloak snapshot and NomoSmart contain the user,
  group and membership after one NomoSmart manual run.
- `AUTH-017-K02`: `people` invokes the provider user action but not the explicit
  group-mapper action and changes only NomoSmart user-domain fields. Existing
  external groups, mappings and derived memberships remain byte-equivalent.
- `AUTH-017-K03`: `groups` invokes compatible group mappers but not provider
  user full sync and changes only NomoSmart groups/memberships/derived roles for
  already known users. User profile/lifecycle fields remain byte-equivalent.
- `AUTH-017-K04`: `people_and_groups` executes both ordered phases and performs
  one complete NomoSmart reconciliation. Parent counters equal real database
  changes; unavailable Keycloak group counts are absent, never guessed.
- `AUTH-017-K05`: two enabled providers execute in stable provider-ID order;
  each gets one result row. A disabled provider is not called and is represented
  only by safe skipped evidence if included by the response contract.
- `AUTH-017-K06`: zero enabled providers records an upstream skipped state,
  still reconciles permitted Keycloak-local users/groups and reports a localized
  warning without claiming LDAP/AD success.
- `AUTH-017-K07`: groups scope with no mapper, multiple ambiguous mappers,
  unsupported mapper/provider type or invalid Keycloak response fails with the
  exact safe code and performs no NomoSmart reconciliation.
- `AUTH-017-K08`: the sync client can perform required actions with the deployed
  approved realm-management grants; removal of a required role returns a safe
  authorization failure. No bootstrap admin, user password, Direct Access Grant
  or LDAP bind is used.

### Failure, Recovery And Consistency Cases

- `AUTH-017-B01`: manual and scheduled queueing persist the effective scope at
  acceptance and use the same cascading worker service. Changing settings
  afterward does not alter the accepted run.
- `AUTH-017-B02`: first provider succeeds and second provider fails. Parent run
  is failed, ordered partial-upstream evidence is retained, no new snapshot is
  applied to NomoSmart, and previous users/groups/roles remain equal.
- `AUTH-017-B03`: retry after repairing the second provider creates a new lease,
  re-executes the complete enabled-provider set and converges Keycloak and
  NomoSmart. Late/duplicate tasks from the first run cannot overwrite either
  terminal result.
- `AUTH-017-B04`: per-provider timeout, total run-budget exhaustion, Keycloak
  restart/unavailability, malformed response and snapshot failure yield distinct
  safe codes. Durable heartbeat keeps a healthy long call active; an actually
  abandoned run is recovered by existing AUTH-015 timeout rules.
- `AUTH-017-B05`: worker unavailable returns 503 without a row; concurrent
  submissions return one 202 plus structured 409s; queue timeout, worker crash,
  retry and duplicate delivery preserve the existing lease guarantees.
- `AUTH-017-B06`: failed upstream phases do not disable/delete NomoSmart users,
  groups, mappings or role users. A successful groups sync retains manual and
  break-glass sources while recalculating only `external_sync` membership.
- `AUTH-017-B07`: every provider phase and terminal result creates a safe audit
  record. API/log/audit/database scans find no token, Secret, password, URL, DN,
  Filter value, component payload, provider raw prose or stack trace.
- `AUTH-017-B08`: view-only, disabled or permission-revoked users receive 403
  before queue/provider mutation; a currently authorized edit user can queue
  without AUTH-013 fresh unlock. Scheduled runs have no fabricated actor.

### API, Frontend, i18n And Accessibility Cases

- `AUTH-017-A01`: existing POST method and 202/409/503 envelope remain
  compatible. Run list/detail add valid `requested_scope`, `phase` and ordered
  provider results; cursor pagination remains stable.
- `AUTH-017-A02`: provider results expose only allowlisted fields and nullable
  verified counts. Parent counters remain zero until successful NomoSmart
  reconciliation and then equal committed changes.
- `AUTH-017-F01`: pressing Sync now immediately disables duplicate submission,
  announces Keycloak provider/user/group, snapshot and NomoSmart phases, polls
  only its run, and refreshes identity/group/history views at terminal state.
- `AUTH-017-F02`: ordered multi-provider success, disabled/no-provider skip,
  mapper missing, provider failure, timeout, partial-upstream warning and retry
  use distinct aligned zh/en keys with icon/text and actionable safe guidance.
- `AUTH-017-F03`: locale switching during a running or failed job immediately
  updates progress, provider result, warning, button, retry, `aria-live` and
  screen-reader text because state stores code/params rather than formatted
  Backend prose.
- `AUTH-017-F04`: desktop and narrow layouts remain scannable without overlap;
  controls meet 40px touch targets, focus returns predictably, and status is not
  communicated by color alone.
- `AUTH-017-F05`: unknown codes show the localized generic safe message plus
  request ID. Raw Backend safe message, Keycloak text and internal details are
  never rendered as final UI copy.
- `AUTH-017-E01`: authenticated live Browser acceptance adds a real LDAP group
  after an earlier Keycloak sync, presses only the NomoSmart button, observes

## CHG-256 AUTH-018 Effective-permission Application Admission Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-08-08 with
`同意 CHG-256 Gate 2（三項皆採建議）`. Gate 3 test design is complete below.
Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-08-08 with
`Peter approves CHG-256 Effective-permission Application Admission Gate`;
repository feature-test implementation/execution is authorized. Current-UAT
identity/group/role/directory mutation remains separately gated.

Requirements under test: `AUTH-018`, the refined Home/ApprovalWorkspace/
ApiDocumentation default-access rule in `MENU-001`, existing `AUTH-009` through
`AUTH-011` error-state separation, existing role union/source rules and
API-001/i18n/audit boundaries.

### Backend Admission And API Cases

- `AUTH-018-B01`: a real active role with at least one positive permission and
  `source=external_sync` admits the synchronized active user; `/auth/me`
  returns the unchanged CurrentUser/permission/project-scope response.
- `AUTH-018-B02`: an active positive manual role admits a user with no LDAP or
  Keycloak group membership. Raw group claims are not required.
- `AUTH-018-B03`: the protected break-glass membership with its active System
  Admin positive grants admits through the same predicate and no JWT bypass.
- `AUTH-018-B04`: a synchronized active user with no role membership, only an
  unmapped external group, or only raw token groups receives exact
  `403 application_access_denied` from `/auth/me`.
- `AUTH-018-B05`: inactive roles, deleted/tombstoned roles and permission rows
  whose `can_view/create/edit/delete/execute` values are all false do not admit.
  Mixed roles use a union and one current positive grant admits.
- `AUTH-018-B06`: Project Owner/member rows and visible project IDs without a
  positive effective system-role permission do not admit or bypass the gate.
- `AUTH-018-B07`: the denial uses the API-001 envelope with stable code, safe
  message and request ID; it returns no empty-success CurrentUser payload,
  token, raw claim, group inventory or role internals.
- `AUTH-018-B08`: denial occurs before protected route-specific business
  queries/mutations. Representative Home Project, approval, notification,
  report, System Management and API Documentation dependencies return the same
  global code without exposing business data.
- `AUTH-018-B09`: removing the user's final positive grant during an admitted
  session causes the next protected request to fail with
  `application_access_denied`; adding a positive mapped/manual role then makes
  a fresh `/auth/me` succeed without a new credential exchange.
- `AUTH-018-B10`: a user who still has any positive permission but lacks the
  requested Menu/project/action continues to receive existing
  `permission_denied`/`project_scope_denied`, not global denial.
- `AUTH-018-B11`: unsynchronized and disabled users retain
  `user_not_synchronized`/`user_disabled`; invalid, expired or revoked tokens
  retain 401. No case is misclassified as application access denial.
- `AUTH-018-B12`: bootstrap, recheck and mid-session revocation audits contain
  user ID, irreversible subject/session fingerprint, stable reason and request
  ID, but no token, raw claim/group list or sensitive identity fields. One
  coalesced bootstrap/recheck transition does not create duplicate audit rows.

### Frontend Auth-state And UX Cases

- `AUTH-018-F01`: `/auth/me` returning `application_access_denied` renders the
  authenticated `/access-denied` boundary before protected children. AppShell,
  Home, Menu, search, Notification, Approval and API Documentation are absent.
- `AUTH-018-F02`: no Home/project/approval/report/notification/business fetch is
  dispatched while admission is checking or denied. React Strict Mode and
  rerender do not duplicate bootstrap or redirect.
- `AUTH-018-F03`: the denial view shows safe account identity, explanation,
  administrator guidance, recheck and logout. It never renders Backend prose,
  raw provider details, grants, groups or application data.
- `AUTH-018-F04`: recheck is single-flight and disabled while pending.
  Continued denial remains on the page with localized guidance; a successful
  CurrentUser response installs fresh permissions and returns to the validated
  in-memory same-origin target or `/`.
- `AUTH-018-F05`: recheck return validation rejects absolute/protocol-relative,
  login, callback, auth API and denial-loop paths. No token or return path is
  persisted in browser storage, readable cookies or unsafe URL parameters.
- `AUTH-018-F06`: logout from denial uses the existing Backend denylist plus
  Keycloak end-session flow. Denial itself never starts refresh, silent SSO,
  interactive login or automatic logout.
- `AUTH-018-F07`: the first mid-session global denial opens the admission
  circuit breaker and replaces the application with the same boundary; repeated
  or already-in-flight denials do not create refresh/navigation/request storms.
- `AUTH-018-F08`: ordinary page-level 403 for an admitted user remains the
  existing in-place forbidden/error UI and never redirects to access denied.
- `AUTH-018-F09`: zh-TW and English keys remain aligned; switching locale while
  denied or rechecking updates every title, status, action and `aria-live`
  message without resetting auth state.
- `AUTH-018-F10`: desktop, tablet and 375px views have no horizontal overflow;
  semantic heading/alert/live regions, keyboard order, visible focus, icon plus
  text status and 40px touch targets satisfy accessibility acceptance.

### Live Identity And Browser Cases

- `AUTH-018-E01`: in an isolated real Keycloak realm/OpenLDAP subtree and real
  PostgreSQL database, a synchronized zero-permission user logs in successfully
  at Keycloak but sees only the denial page; network evidence shows no Home,
  Notification or other business request after `/auth/me` denial.
- `AUTH-018-E02`: an LDAP group that is present but unmapped remains denied.
  Mapping it to an active positive role and completing the real identity sync,
  then pressing recheck, admits the same SSO session without credential entry.
- `AUTH-018-E03`: a no-group user with a real manual positive role is admitted;
  removal of its final grant during the session moves the next protected request
  to denial, and existing logout completes safely.
- `AUTH-018-E04`: disabled/unsynchronized users and expired sessions traverse
  their existing login notices, while an admitted user with one missing feature
  sees the existing page-level forbidden state. Run at desktop and narrow
  widths in zh-TW and English.

### Security, Regression And Coverage Cases

- `AUTH-018-S01`: focused source/config checks reject group-count admission,
  Frontend-only authorization, automatic role assignment, default-role fallback
  and any bypass that returns empty-permission 200.
- `AUTH-018-S02`: no new identity header shortcut, local password, persistent
  browser token, Keycloak Direct Access Grant, secret, environment setting or
  deployment port is introduced.
- `AUTH-018-R01`: existing positive-role `/auth/me`, logout, silent restoration,
  account-unavailable, Home/Approval/API Docs behavior after admission,
  permission union, break-glass and project-scope suites remain green.
- `AUTH-018-C01`: Backend and Frontend application-logic coverage each remain at
  least 80%. Thresholds are not relaxed; unavailable live prerequisites or
  lower aggregate coverage are reported open/blocked rather than mock-passed.

### Planned Verification After Gate 4

1. Run focused CHG-256 Backend and Frontend tests against real disposable
   PostgreSQL/OIDC identity state.
2. Run `backend:syntax`, complete Backend and Frontend suites, i18n guards,
   lint/build and authenticated real-browser E2E.
3. Run `coverage:check`, static security and Docker/Helm/config regressions even
   though no deployment contract change is expected.
4. Record commands, counts, blocked prerequisites, cleanup and coverage in this
   section and `TRACEABILITY.md`; do not substitute fixture/mock success for
   TEST-002 live cases.

### Executed Verification Results

- Focused Backend admission/error-envelope/audit-summary tests pass `10/10`
  with no coverage threshold override beyond the intentional focused
  `--no-cov` invocation. They prove every `can_*` positive flag, empty and
  all-false denial, stable API-001 envelope and non-reversible minimal audit
  fields.
- Focused Frontend contracts pass `5/5`; the rendered denial component passes
  `3/3` for safe content/actions, zh-TW to English live switching, announced
  denial/recheck state and disabled interaction. Complete Frontend regression
  passes `126/126` contracts and `14/14` components.
- Backend syntax, Frontend lint/build, governance, both i18n guards,
  high-severity Bandit, Docker Compose config, Helm lint, deployment config
  policy and `git diff --check` pass.
- `test:backend` is BLOCKED during collection because the live Keycloak token
  endpoint cannot be reached from this execution environment. Consequently
  real PostgreSQL role-source/inactive/deleted/project-only, protected-route
  pre-handler, revocation/regrant and persisted-audit cases remain open; no
  mock or fixture success replaces them.
- `test:e2e` is BLOCKED because the required isolated Frontend, Backend and
  OIDC URLs plus Peter/John live-test credentials are not configured. No
  current-UAT identity, group, role or directory mutation occurred.
- `test:frontend` executes all tests successfully but the coverage gate fails
  at `7.33%` lines, `6.52%` statements, `4.08%` branches and `5.95%`
  functions versus 80%. Backend complete coverage is unavailable because its
  live suite is blocked, so `coverage:check` remains open. Thresholds were not
  reduced or bypassed.

## CHG-260 Vault And Upload Scan Removal With Simplified Credentials And Authentication Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed by Peter on 2026-08-18 with
`同意 CHG-260 Gate 2（五項皆確認並接受列示風險）`. Gate 3 test design is
complete. Gate 4 was approved by Peter on 2026-08-18 with
`Peter approves CHG-260 Vault And Upload Scan Removal With Simplified Credentials And Authentication`;
repository implementation and non-destructive/disposable feature verification may proceed.

Requirements under test: `SECRET-002`, `UPLOAD-SEC-003`, `DEPLOY-019`,
`AUTH-020`, refined `AUTH-004/005/016`, `IMPORT-001/002/006`, `PIPE-011/013`,
`DEPLOY-006/007/012/013/015/016/017`, `TEST-002/003/005`, `AUTH-018`,
`I18N-002/003/004/005`, compatibility, retention and release-risk contracts.

### SECRET-002 Secret Reference And Migration Cases

- `SECRET-002-U01`: parse valid `k8s-secret://<name>#<key>` and
  `compose-secret://<logical-name>` references; reject empty name/key, unknown
  scheme, query/fragment ambiguity, traversal, absolute file path and control
  characters without exposing a value.
- `SECRET-002-U02`: Kubernetes runtime resolves only explicitly mounted,
  allowlisted same-namespace Secret keys. Cross-namespace references, absent or
  empty files, symlinks, writable/broad-permission mounts and unlisted keys fail
  closed. Backend/Worker ServiceAccounts have no Secret list/watch/write verbs.
- `SECRET-002-U03`: Compose resolves only declared read-only Docker Secret files
  beneath the generated/operator directory; missing, newline-corrupted scalar,
  wrong owner/mode and arbitrary environment/path fallback are rejected.
- `SECRET-002-U04`: AI model/OCR/data-source/HTTP/S3/SFTP credential create,
  reset, rotation, connection test and runtime consumers persist only canonical
  Secret references/configured state and never return values in API/log/audit/
  metric/error/receipt/support bundle.
- `SECRET-002-M01`: upgrade preflight inventories every active `vault://`, Vault
  env/value/chart/resource and legacy mode without reading or displaying the
  secret; any occurrence blocks before mutation with a stable safe code.
- `SECRET-002-M02`: after operator-created Kubernetes/Docker references are
  installed, every real consumer connects successfully and the inventory is
  empty. No NomoSmart command exports, copies, rotates or deletes a Vault value.
- `SECRET-002-C01`: mixed old Vault-dependent and CHG-260 compatibility
  identities are rejected before migration/bootstrap/application rollout;
  complete former-topology restore or roll-forward is documented, while
  code-only rollback is rejected.
- `SECRET-002-A01`: source/render/package/image/SBOM scans contain no Vault
  client, service, chart, image, port, PVC, policy, AppRole/Auth, custody,
  readiness, backup or active documentation contract outside explicitly marked
  historical evidence/migration detectors.

### UPLOAD-SEC-003 Scanner-free Ingestion Cases

- `UPLOAD-SEC-003-U01`: a valid single PDF/DOCX/TXT/Markdown upload performs all
  existing request/type/size/package/hash/key validations, writes the final
  object, atomically establishes the version pointer and dispatches one
  extraction Pipeline without `file_scan_runs`, quarantine object, scan outbox,
  Celery scanner task or `file_scan` pipeline step.
- `UPLOAD-SEC-003-U02`: a valid multi-file request independently writes each
  final object/version and leaves it `ready_for_extraction` without scan state;
  one invalid/failing sibling does not roll back successful siblings.
- `UPLOAD-SEC-003-U03`: FTP/FTPS/SFTP/S3/HTTP synchronization follows the same
  direct-ingestion boundary and never silently routes through a scanner.
- `UPLOAD-SEC-003-U04`: duplicate idempotency key/delivery, concurrent request
  and Worker redelivery do not create duplicate object/version/Pipeline effects.
- `UPLOAD-SEC-003-F01`: format/package/hash failure creates no final object or
  version. Object write, database commit or outbox failure performs bounded
  compensation and leaves no orphan or falsely extractable version.
- `UPLOAD-SEC-003-H01`: pre-existing terminal `file_scan_runs` remain unchanged
  and auditable; existing quarantine objects remain unavailable to normal
  download and are neither promoted nor deleted by the migration.
- `UPLOAD-SEC-003-H02`: any queued/running/retryable scan or scanner outbox/task
  blocks upgrade with safe non-content counts and exact operator resolution
  guidance; CHG-260 does not invent a clean/rejected result.
- `UPLOAD-SEC-003-UI01`: upload and extraction progress in zh-TW/en has no
  scanner/clean/quarantine stage or claim, retains canonical loading/error/
  retry behavior and remains keyboard/accessibility/responsive compliant.
- `UPLOAD-SEC-003-A01`: Compose/Helm/installer/package/release/readiness/network/
  image inventory includes no ClamAV or external malware-scanner config,
  workload, service, port, probe, definition database or security gate.

### DEPLOY-019 Bundled Credential Cases

- `DEPLOY-019-C01`: a fresh bundled installation without override generates
  application/runtime principal or access key `nomosmart` and password/secret
  key exact bytes `P@ssw0rd` for PostgreSQL app/migration/Keycloak DB, Redis
  ACL/replication/Sentinel, RustFS/S3, OpenSearch runtime, Neo4j runtime and
  Keycloak bootstrap according to each product contract.
- `DEPLOY-019-C02`: PostgreSQL `postgres`, OpenSearch `admin` and Neo4j `neo4j`
  remain only where the pinned upstream image requires bootstrap names, use the
  confirmed password, and are not mounted into normal application workloads.
- `DEPLOY-019-C03`: the NomoSmart first-use human remains the distinct
  `nomosmart / nomosmart` AUTH-016 principal; tests distinguish realm/user,
  Keycloak bootstrap and peripheral service identities.
- `DEPLOY-019-C04`: `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, OIDC and sync client secrets, API
  tokens, signing keys, TLS/CA/private keys and other cryptographic material are
  protocol-valid, purpose-separated and not equal to `P@ssw0rd`.
- `DEPLOY-019-C05`: operator-provided Secret overrides are preserved exactly;
  re-run/resume is idempotent and does not silently replace an existing Secret
  with defaults.
- `DEPLOY-019-X01`: external-services plan/install never creates, resets, guesses
  or tests the confirmed default against an external endpoint; it only consumes
  existing referenced Secret and validates connectivity/TLS with authorization.
- `DEPLOY-019-S01`: actual values exist only in generated Kubernetes/Docker
  Secret custody, not ConfigMap, ordinary values/env examples, SQL, image,
  command line/process list, log, audit, status, receipt or support bundle.
- `DEPLOY-019-R01`: plan/status/receipt/release notes expose only the stable
  `shared_default_peripheral_credentials_accepted` risk identity. They do not
  claim credential uniqueness, secrecy or bounded blast radius.

### AUTH-020 Password-only Authentication Cases

- `AUTH-020-K01`: fresh bundled realm Browser Flow contains username/password
  only and no OTP/TOTP execution; first-use user has `UPDATE_PASSWORD` but not
  `CONFIGURE_TOTP`; Theme exposes no OTP verify/setup page or localized prompt.
- `AUTH-020-K02`: existing bundled realm reconciliation removes only the
  NomoSmart-managed TOTP requirement and preserves LDAP federation, users,
  groups, clients, role mappings, locales and existing OTP credentials/history.
- `AUTH-020-K03`: first-use finalization succeeds only after changed password,
  successful OIDC/login evidence, System Admin mapping, directory/group sync,
  replacement admin and break-glass disable/session revocation; it does not
  wait for or report TOTP evidence.
- `AUTH-020-K04`: emergency break-glass enable/use/disable continues to require
  temporary password, logging, alerting, audit and rotation but no MFA action.
- `AUTH-020-O01`: normal login, logout, refresh/session expiry and identity
  settings fresh authentication use Authorization Code + PKCE; NomoSmart never
  receives password and password-only does not weaken state/nonce/session/
  permission/auth-time checks.
- `AUTH-020-O02`: admitted user with positive permission enters after password
  login; disabled, unsynchronized or zero-permission user still receives the
  existing localized `application_access_denied`/identity state and cannot use
  TOTP removal as an authorization bypass.
- `AUTH-020-X01`: an operator-managed external Provider that requires MFA is
  neither reconfigured nor bypassed. Browser completes the Provider-owned flow,
  and NomoSmart accepts only a valid normal OIDC token.
- `AUTH-020-UI01`: bundled Theme and demonstration login provide bilingual
  username/password/loading/error/recovery/update/session behavior, no six-digit
  OTP state, no credential persistence and no client-only formal success claim.
- `AUTH-020-A01`: source/render/package/installer/readiness/docs tests find no
  active TOTP checkpoint, required action, health evidence or new-install test;
  historical evidence is explicitly labelled superseded.

### Deployment, Compatibility And Release Cases

- `CHG-260-D01`: Compose config contains neither Vault nor ClamAV services,
  volumes, networks, ports, dependencies or healthchecks and mounts only the
  declared Docker Secrets into each consumer.
- `CHG-260-D02`: bundled Helm render contains no Vault/ClamAV chart dependency,
  workload, PVC, Service, port, NetworkPolicy or probe; runtime values come from
  named Secret references/projected files. `helm lint`, schema and production
  policy pass the new contract and reject legacy/mixed values.
- `CHG-260-D03`: external-services render contains only application workloads
  and operator-owned endpoint/CA/runtime Secret references, with no Vault,
  scanner or external-credential mutation behavior.
- `CHG-260-D04`: installer stage/state/resume/status/finalize/receipt schemas no
  longer require Vault custody, scanner readiness or TOTP checkpoints; existing
  pre-CHG-260 checkpoints receive an explicit incompatible/migration-required
  result rather than being misread as complete.
- `CHG-260-D05`: package/release allowlists, checksums, image inventory, SPDX,
  CVE/license gates, backup/restore and runbooks contain the new application and
  peripheral set and no obsolete image/resource claim.
- `CHG-260-D06`: disposable upgrade verifies retained application data, scan

- `CHG-260-E01`: real Compose journey starts dependencies, migrates, bootstraps,

- `CHG-260-E02`: real disposable Kubernetes bundled journey verifies Secret

- `CHG-260-E03`: real external-services journey uses operator-created external

## CHG-291 Exclusive Knowledge-Project Member Role Test Design

Gate 1 analysis and Gate 2 confirmation completed on 2026-09-03. Peter approved
Gate 4 with `Peter approves CHG-291 Exclusive Knowledge Project Member Role`;
the bounded repository tests in this section are authorized.

### Backend and migration cases

| ID | Scenario | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PROJECT-012-B01` | Create/replace a member with exactly one allowed role | One membership row is stored/returned, lock version increases once and audit records before/after role. |
| `PROJECT-012-B02` | Send zero, duplicate or two/three roles | Stable 422 safe error; membership, Owner rows, lock version and success audit remain unchanged. |
| `PROJECT-012-B03` | Change Editor to Viewer | Old row is atomically replaced, response has `roles=["viewer"]`, and no overlap exists. |
| `PROJECT-012-B04` | Promote/demote another eligible member to/from Owner | `project_members` and `project_owners` remain bidirectionally consistent in the same transaction. |
| `PROJECT-012-B05` | Sole Owner or signed-in Owner attempts role change/delete | Existing stable 409 protection wins; no partial write occurs. |
| `PROJECT-012-B06` | Concurrent/stale member replacements | Project row lock and `lock_version` allow only the valid request; final member has exactly one role. |
| `PROJECT-012-B07` | Search for a user already in the Project under another role | Candidate add result excludes that user; direct replacement remains the only role-change path. |
| `PROJECT-012-M01` | V049 sees Owner+Editor+Viewer, Editor+Viewer and Viewer-only members | It retains Owner, Editor and Viewer respectively according to approved precedence. |
| `PROJECT-012-M02` | Owner governance and membership differ but one side proves Owner | V049 restores one-to-one Owner parity without creating an unrelated Owner. |
| `PROJECT-012-M03` | A Project has no provable Owner | V049 fails closed before committing normalization/constraint changes. |
| `PROJECT-012-M04` | Attempt a second role after V049 | Database unique `(project_id,user_id)` rejects the write. |
| `PROJECT-012-M05` | Apply the migration logic repeatedly to an already normalized database | Counts/roles remain unchanged and migration audit evidence is not duplicated. |

### Frontend and accessibility cases

| ID | Scenario | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PROJECT-012-F01` | Render a normal member row | Owner/Editor/Viewer form one labelled radio group with exactly one checked option. |
| `PROJECT-012-F02` | Keyboard or pointer selects another role | Selection is exclusive, focus remains visible, and exactly one role is sent without an empty intermediate request. |
| `PROJECT-012-F03` | Successful role change and reload | Member moves to only the target tab; three tab counts sum to unique member count. |
| `PROJECT-012-F04` | PUT fails or returns stale-version conflict | Busy state clears and UI retains/reloads Backend-authoritative single role with an announced error. |
| `PROJECT-012-F05` | Existing member appears in candidate API results | UI filters it from every add-role tab; pending-add flow assigns only the active tab role to genuinely new members. |
| `PROJECT-012-F06` | Sole/self Owner row | All radio options are disabled/read-only, reason is textually exposed and delete action is absent. |
| `PROJECT-012-F07` | Other Owner when at least two Owners exist | Current Owner can choose one replacement role for the other Owner, subject to Backend confirmation. |
| `PROJECT-012-F08` | zh/en, 375px, keyboard and screen-reader semantics | Labels, focus, errors and exclusive state remain understandable without color alone or horizontal overflow. |

### Integration, coverage and deployment boundaries

- Run Backend API tests against disposable real PostgreSQL; mocks/fixtures cannot
  satisfy the transaction or migration acceptance under `TEST-002`.
- Retain all `PROJECT-001`, `PROJECT-002`, `PROJECT-009`, `PROJECT-010` and
  `PROJECT-011` authorization, Autocomplete, Owner-protection and concurrency tests.
- Changed Frontend and Backend application logic must each meet at least 80%
  statement and branch coverage; do not relax global thresholds.
- A later, separately approved live deployment must inventory overlapping roles,
  back up the database, apply only V049, verify unique/Owner invariants, and use
  an authenticated browser to confirm radio/tab/candidate behavior. It must not
  modify Local Roles, documents, vectors, indexes, identity or Providers.

profile. They are planned at Gate 3 and must not be run before Gate 4 approval.

HA, security supply-chain, backup/restore or independent 80% coverage gates.

  three expected Ready nodes and `arm64` architecture match the captured target.
  Context or identity drift aborts without mutation.
