## CHG-271 Local Backend OIDC Ingress Alignment

Peter completed Gate 2 on 2026-08-25 with `OK` after confirming that
phpLDAPadmin should remain on loopback port 8080 and that host Backend OIDC must
use the existing HTTPS Keycloak Ingress. These cases design verification for
`LOCAL-OIDC-001..004`. No implementation or live test result was claimed before
approval. Peter approved Gate 4 on 2026-08-25 with
`Peter approves CHG-271 Local Backend OIDC Ingress Alignment`; bounded
implementation and live tests may run after the action-time preflight.

### Governance And Configuration Cases

- `LOCAL-OIDC-G01`: CHG-271 is the active first changelog row and specification
  10.28, development plan, test plan and traceability map four unique stable
  requirements with Gate 2 and Gate 4 recorded.
- `LOCAL-OIDC-C01`: ignored `backend/.env` and the safe example use exact
  `https://nomosmart.local/identity/realms/nomosmart` issuer and
  `https://nomosmart.local/identity` Admin base URL; no host OIDC/Admin value
  points to `127.0.0.1:8080`.
- `LOCAL-OIDC-C02`: runtime change is limited to those two non-sensitive URL
  lines plus a matching owner-only public-CA path only when Python strict TLS
  requires it. Client IDs/secrets, sync credentials and every unrelated setting have
  unchanged redacted hashes and never appear in captured output.
- `LOCAL-OIDC-C03`: Docker/Helm internal Keycloak port 8080 values remain
  unchanged because they are not the phpLDAPadmin host listener. Backend source
  defaults and Frontend configuration remain outside this bounded change.

### URL, TLS And Discovery Cases

- `LOCAL-OIDC-U01`: URL parsing selects 443 for HTTPS without an explicit port,
  80 for HTTP without a port, and the literal explicit port otherwise; missing
  or invalid hosts fail with a safe assertion.
- `LOCAL-OIDC-U02`: the OIDC live prerequisite no longer supplies a fixed 8080
  default and cannot resolve the canonical issuer to phpLDAPadmin.
- `LOCAL-OIDC-T01`: strict curl and Backend Python clients retrieve the real
  discovery document without `-k`/`verify=false`; response status is successful
  and `issuer` exactly matches configuration.
- `LOCAL-OIDC-T02`: real JWKS is valid JSON from the same HTTPS realm origin and
  PyJWT can initialize against it with strict certificate/hostname validation.
- `LOCAL-OIDC-T03`: phpLDAPadmin HTML, redirect substitution, issuer mismatch,
  certificate mismatch or missing matching CA fails closed and cannot count as
  OIDC readiness.

### Live Backend And Preservation Cases

- `LOCAL-OIDC-L01`: action-time inventory confirms healthy phpLDAPadmin at only
  `127.0.0.1:8080 -> 8080`, no configured 8081 listener, healthy OpenLDAP and
  exact matching existing Docker/Kubernetes targets before mutation.
- `LOCAL-OIDC-L02`: focused CHG-271 tests and Backend syntax pass; the broad
  Backend harness proceeds beyond its former phpLDAPadmin 404/non-OIDC failure.
  Any independent later failure is recorded with the exact prerequisite and is
  not hidden by changing tests or TEST-002 policy.
- `LOCAL-OIDC-L03`: post-check proves phpLDAPadmin container/image/network/port,
  OpenLDAP container/volumes/data, Helm revision/images, Namespace, Secrets,
  PVCs, schema/data and Keycloak realm/client metadata are unchanged.
- `LOCAL-OIDC-R01`: restoring only the two ignored URL values and repository
  example/test changes is sufficient rollback; no service restart, Helm action,
  LDAP change or persistent-resource operation is required.

./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh spec:trace
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:doctor
./HARNESS/harness.sh plan:approved

## CHG-275 Chat Citation Identity, Turn Count And Loading Feedback

Gate 1 read-only diagnosis and Peter's Gate 2 confirmation completed on
2026-08-26 with `同意 CHG-275 Gate 2，採用上述建議`. These cases cover
`CHAT-CITE-001..003`, `CHAT-TURN-001` and `CHAT-WAIT-001`. Peter approved Gate 4
repository implementation and feature tests on 2026-08-26 with
`Peter approves CHG-275 Chat Citation Identity, Turn Count And Loading Feedback`.
The later digest-bound revision-20 build/Helm action was separately approved and
completed as recorded below. Provider queries and unrelated persistent
runtime-data mutations remain separately gated.

### Characterization And Backend Contract Cases

- `CHAT-CITE-C01`: content-minimized read-only evidence on the existing CHG-274
  record proves five citation objects all use one repeated document-title base,
  while every excerpt is non-empty.
- `CHAT-CITE-C02`: the same evidence proves answer markers `[1]`, `[3]`, `[5]`
  are valid citation-array source ordinals but four of five title suffixes differ
  from authoritative database `chunk_index`; no document excerpt is printed.
- `CHAT-CITE-B01`: a new real retrieval response carries nullable
  `chunk_index` from the authoritative selected Chunk, preserves citation order
  and does not derive it from the title or mutate retrieval rank.
- `CHAT-CITE-B02`: authorized legacy history/review citations missing
  `chunk_index` are hydrated by one bounded scope-filtered query, with no N+1,
  no cross-project/version disclosure, stable order and explicit missing-Chunk
  fallback; persisted JSON remains byte-identical.
- `CHAT-CITE-B03`: valid answer markers within `1..N` are preserved. A new
  out-of-range marker fails with the stable provider-response-contract error,
  creates no normal ChatRecord, records consumed provider usage exactly once and
  causes no automatic provider retry. A no-marker answer remains valid.
- `CHAT-CITE-B04`: Document Chat, Project Chat, submit-review and Approval
  response/history schemas retain backward compatibility when `chunk_index` is
  absent or null.

### Frontend Presentation Cases

- `CHAT-CITE-F01`: the shared formatter trims and normalizes whitespace, counts
  Unicode grapheme clusters, returns the first 24, appends exactly `…` only when
  longer and handles emoji, combining marks, CJK and empty localized fallback.
- `CHAT-CITE-F02`: every citation card displays its citation-array ordinal,
  excerpt preview and separate canonical Chunk number. It never shows the stale
  document title as Chunk identity and never parses its numeric suffix.
- `CHAT-CITE-F03`: each valid answer marker selects/focuses the card with the
  same ordinal by keyboard and pointer; invalid legacy markers are non-interactive
  and expose localized mismatch text without remapping.
- `CHAT-CITE-F04`: Document Chat, Project Chat, submit-review and Approval use
  the same presenter and produce identical title/ordinal/number semantics for
  the same citation payload.
- `CHAT-CITE-SEC01`: citation excerpt and answer content remain escaped through
  the safe Markdown boundary; no raw HTML/event handler, full-content diagnostic
  leak or unauthorized canonical metadata is introduced.

### Turn Count And Waiting Cases

- `CHAT-TURN-F01`: two persisted ChatRecords display `2 輪對話` in zh-Hant and
  the locale-correct English equivalent, not four messages. Zero/one/many and
  Project Chat parity are covered.
- `CHAT-TURN-F02`: a pending request, rejected provider response or failed
  unpersisted entry does not increment the conversation-turn count; successful
  history reload derives it from persisted records.
- `CHAT-WAIT-F01`: while one request is active, one visible localized status has
  a Lucide loading indicator, `role="status"`, polite live announcement and an
  `aria-busy` owner; the send action cannot submit a duplicate request.
- `CHAT-WAIT-F02`: success and error both restore controls predictably, retained
  typed input follows the confirmed interaction contract, and the error remains
  readable without a stuck busy state.
- `CHAT-WAIT-F03`: reduced-motion disables non-essential spinning/transition,
  and desktop/narrow layouts keep the status readable without overlap or layout
  shift.

### Regression, Deployment And Live Acceptance

- `CHAT-CITE-R01`: existing retrieval, prompt context, citations, review evidence,
  feedback controls, history authorization and safe Markdown behavior remain
  passing under focused and complete Frontend/Backend/E2E suites.
- `CHAT-CITE-R02`: `spec:doctor`, `spec:trace`, `plan:doctor`, `plan:approved`,

- `CHAT-CITE-L02`: exact rendered Helm preflight lists every rolled workload and
  retained Job/image. No build, Helm write, Job or rollout occurs without its
  own explicit action approval.
- `CHAT-CITE-L03`: authenticated read-only reload of the existing CHG-274 record

  mapping, canonical numbers and one-turn history without a provider call or

- `CHAT-CITE-L04`: authenticated submit-review/Approval evidence is checked only
  when an authorized existing real record/task exists; unavailable evidence is

- `CHAT-CITE-L05`: a real provider-wait animation/error lifecycle is attempted

## CHG-276 Consecutive Used Citations And Structure-Aware Retrieval

Gate 1 diagnosis and Peter's Gate 2 confirmation completed on 2026-08-26 with
`同意 CHG-276 Gate 2，採用上述建議`. These cases cover `CHAT-RETR-001..002`
and `CHAT-CITE-004..005`. Peter approved Gate 4 repository implementation and
feature tests on 2026-08-26 with
`Peter approves CHG-276 Consecutive Used Citations And Structure-Aware Retrieval`
and requested image/Kubernetes delivery. Feature cases may now run; Provider
re-query and live cluster mutation remain separately gated.

### Characterization Cases

- `CHAT-COMPACT-C01`: the persisted record
  `a0f9f83d-f38d-4b75-8802-12aaafc8bb87` has five raw candidates and raw answer
  marker `[3]`; the five stored/authoritative excerpts are headings or lead-ins,
  so the existing unable-to-confirm answer is grounded in its actual prompt.
- `CHAT-COMPACT-C02`: active Chunk #4 is the retrieved short colon-ended lead-in
  and contiguous active Chunk #5 contains the three complete principles; both
  belong to the same Project/document/version and Chunk #6 begins the next
  Markdown section.
- `CHAT-COMPACT-C03`: the current RRF implementation iterates vector hits only,
  proving that keyword-only results cannot enter the fused list. The read-only
  keyword characterization and persisted record require no new embedding or
  Chat Provider call.

### Hybrid Fusion Cases

- `CHAT-RETR-RRF01`: vector-only, keyword-only and dual-channel hits all appear
  once in the fused union with contributions only from present channels.
- `CHAT-RETR-RRF02`: duplicate identities collapse, the best channel ranks are
  retained and equal fused scores resolve by smallest channel rank then stable
  Chunk identity.
- `CHAT-RETR-RRF03`: malformed/missing hit identities are rejected or skipped by
  the safe existing boundary and cannot perturb deterministic valid ordering.
- `CHAT-RETR-RRF04`: Project, scope and document-version filters are unchanged;
  an otherwise high-ranked out-of-scope hit never reaches candidates.

### Structure-Aware Retrieval Cases

- `CHAT-RETR-STRUCT01`: Markdown-heading-only text and a single <=40-grapheme
  colon-ended lead-in are structural-only; normal prose, list/table body,
  colon-containing long prose, emoji and combining sequences classify correctly.
- `CHAT-RETR-STRUCT02`: retrieved Chunk #4 promotes its canonical contiguous
  content-bearing Chunk #5, preserving #5 ID/index/content/source mapping and
  excluding structural #4 from the final prompt candidate slot.
- `CHAT-RETR-STRUCT03`: lookahead examines at most two contiguous indexes,
  rejects gaps/inactive rows and stops at another document/version or the next
  same/higher Markdown section.
- `CHAT-RETR-STRUCT04`: a successor already present is deduplicated; the next
  fused candidate fills capacity without changing deterministic order.
- `CHAT-RETR-STRUCT05`: final prompt candidates never exceed requested `top_k`,
  a content-bearing primary hit is never replaced, and empty/missing successors
  leave safe existing behavior.
- `CHAT-RETR-STRUCT06`: authorized Chunk lookup reuses the one already-loaded
  collection and causes zero additional SQL queries, writes, OpenSearch writes,
  re-index operations or Provider invocations.

### Used-Source Compaction Cases

- `CHAT-COMPACT-B01`: raw `[3][5][3]` with five candidates produces display
  `[1][2][1]` and only original candidates 3 then 5.
- `CHAT-COMPACT-B02`: duplicate markers preserve first-use mapping; marker text
  outside the validated numeric citation-token grammar and all non-marker answer
  Markdown remain byte-identical.
- `CHAT-COMPACT-B03`: raw answer and citation objects remain byte-identical and
  unmutated; persisted ChatRecord/Validation evidence keeps full prompt
  candidates and raw ordinals after flush/commit/rollback probes.
- `CHAT-COMPACT-B04`: an already compact view is idempotent, and canonical
  `chunk_id`, `chunk_index`, excerpt order and source mapping survive compaction.
- `CHAT-COMPACT-B05`: valid no-marker answers return unchanged text with zero
  used citations; empty candidates retain safe no-answer behavior.
- `CHAT-COMPACT-B06`: `[0]`, `[N+1]` and other invalid numeric markers still fail
  through the CHG-275 provider-response contract before persistence/compaction;
  compaction never repairs, retries or bills again.

### Shared Surface And Compatibility Cases

- `CHAT-COMPACT-S01`: immediate Document/Project Chat responses and authorized
  history/feedback reloads return the same compact answer/citations.
- `CHAT-COMPACT-S02`: CSV completed result and download/export compact only the

- `CHAT-COMPACT-S03`: submit-review and Approval chat evidence share the same

- `CHAT-COMPACT-S06`: zh-Hant/en labels, empty state, exports and narrow layouts

### Live, Regression And Deployment Cases

- `CHAT-COMPACT-L01`: content-minimized PostgreSQL read-back proves the current
  record and 26 active Chunks baseline without printing unrelated content.
- `CHAT-COMPACT-L02`: a real PostgreSQL transaction proves raw evidence

## CHG-277 Safe Markdown Ordered List Structure Preservation Test Design

### Scope And Gate

- Gate 2 was confirmed on 2026-08-27 with
  `同意 CHG-277 Gate 2，採用上述建議`.
- These cases defined Gate 5 expectations and ran only after Peter approved
  Gate 4 with `Peter approves CHG-277 Safe Markdown Ordered List Structure
  Preservation`. No Provider, database mutation, image build or deployment is
  part of repository feature-test acceptance.

### Parser And Semantic DOM Cases

- `MD-LIST-F01`: raw sections `1..6`, separated by blank lines, paragraphs,
  citations and bullets like the current persisted answer, render visible and
  semantic ordinals `1..6`; source text/order is unchanged.
- `MD-LIST-F02`: a separated block beginning with `3.` renders an `ol` with
  `start=3`; a natural block beginning at 1 omits unnecessary corrective
  attributes while still announcing 1.
- `MD-LIST-F03`: consecutive source values `1,3,4` preserve the jump through
  `li[value=3]`/equivalent semantic DOM and do not become `1,2,3`.
- `MD-LIST-F04`: two explicitly separated lists that each begin at 1 remain two
  lists and each restarts at 1; no global counter leaks between SafeMarkdown
  instances or messages.
- `MD-LIST-F05`: an ordered item with indented continuation paragraph, unordered
  sub-list and ordered sub-list keeps them under the owning `li`; a following
  top-level item increments correctly and no continuation becomes a peer item.
- `MD-LIST-F06`: unindented independent paragraphs/tables/headings remain peer
  blocks in source order; the next ordered block preserves its explicit start
  without heuristic swallowing.

### Citation, Safety And Regression Cases

- `MD-LIST-F07`: `[1]`/`[2]` remain interactive citation markers mapped to the
  compact citation list when located in item text or continuation content;
  ordered markers never enter citation mapping and citations never set list
  ordinals.
- `MD-LIST-F08`: `v1.2`, `2026.08.27`, decimals, IP-like/numeric tokens and a
  sentence containing `1. text` are not split into ordered lists unless they
  occupy an allowed marker position.
- `MD-LIST-F09`: raw HTML/script remains non-executable text; bold, heading,
  table, unordered list, citation focus/accessibility and empty-source behavior
  retain their existing contracts without `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
- `MD-LIST-S01`: Document Chat, Project Chat, CSV/validation, submit-review,
  Approval evidence, Knowledge Detail rendered source and text Chunk surfaces
  continue importing the shared renderer rather than implementing local ordinal
  repair.
- `MD-LIST-S02`: zh-Hant/en and narrow-layout component evidence retains semantic
  order, readable indentation, table overflow and citation controls.
- `MD-LIST-R01`: existing CHG-273 Markdown, CHG-275 citation/interaction and
  CHG-276 compaction tests remain green; raw answer/citation arrays are untouched.

### Verification And Release Gates

- Focused executable component/parser tests must pass before the full Frontend
  suite, lint and production build.
- `spec:doctor`, `spec:trace`, `plan:doctor`, `plan:approved`, `test:plan`, Helm
  lint, deployment config policy and diff hygiene must pass after Gate 4.
- Frontend coverage remains subject to the unmodified 80% release gate. The
  existing repository-wide gap must be reported and may not be waived or reduced.
- Any later Docker Desktop acceptance must use an immutable Frontend image,
  exact hidden-Secret render, protected resource baselines and a separate action
  approval. Historical record readback is sufficient; no Provider query is
  required or authorized for this fix.

## CHG-278 Model Usage Numeric And Cost Presentation Correction Test Design

### Scope And Gate

- Gate 2 was confirmed on 2026-08-27 with
  `同意 CHG-278 Gate 2，採用上述建議`.
- Peter approved these Gate 5 repository tests on 2026-08-27 with
  `Peter approves CHG-278 Model Usage Numeric And Cost Presentation Correction`.
  They require no Provider query, Admin API Key, billing API, image build,
  Kubernetes write or existing ledger mutation.

### Frontend Table And Formatter Cases

- `REPORT-USAGE-F01`: model-usage columns begin model type, localized Model Name,
  Provider, project and purpose; an AI Model with `name=nomosmart-chat` and
  `config.model_name=gpt-5.6-luna` displays `nomosmart-chat`, not the Provider
  identifier, and no duplicate model or endpoint field exists.
- `REPORT-USAGE-F02`: model type/name cells and headers use deterministic sticky
  classes/offsets and remain readable/focus-safe under horizontal overflow in
  zh-Hant and English.
- `REPORT-USAGE-F03`: table, filter state/bar, filter-options type and summary/
  export request omit `integration_client_id`, `api_key_prefix` and the
  Integration Client/API-key selector; no removed query parameter is sent.
- `REPORT-NUM-F01`: integer `17058` renders `17,058` under the supported locales;
  zero and negative/large safe numbers retain sign/value without percent logic.
- `REPORT-NUM-F02`: latency `6224.86` renders `6,224.86`, applies at most two
  decimals and retains null fallback semantics.
- `REPORT-NUM-F03`: estimated cost `0.00421680` renders `0.0042168`, large costs
  group by locale, official numeric zero renders `0`, and missing official cost
  renders localized Not provided.
- `REPORT-NUM-F04`: `error_rate=0`, `0.66667` and `1` render `0%`, `66.667%` or
  equivalent bounded configured precision, and `100%`; costs and latency never
  receive `%` based on numeric magnitude.
- `REPORT-NUM-F05`: unknown/text/source/currency values remain escaped text and
  no key, credential, endpoint or raw provider payload is rendered.

### CSV And i18n Cases

- `REPORT-CSV-F01`: model-usage CSV contains `ai_model_name=nomosmart-chat` under
  localized Model Name and omits Provider `model_name`, `integration_client_id`,
  `api_key_prefix` and their localized headers.
- `REPORT-CSV-F02`: CSV values remain raw numeric data: `17058`, `6224.86`,
  `0.0042168` and `0.66667`, with no grouping comma inside numeric fields, `%`,
  `ms` or currency suffix.
- `REPORT-I18N-F01`: zh-Hant/en key sets align and render 模型名稱/Model Name and
  未提供/Not provided without hard-coded user-facing fallback prose.

### Backend Aggregation And Cost Cases

- `REPORT-AGG-B01`: three attempted events (one success, two terminal failures)
  plus two non-attempted failures aggregate to call=3, success=1, failure=2 and
  error_rate `0.66667`; the rate cannot exceed one.
- `REPORT-AGG-B02`: no attempted calls yields zero counts/rate; attempted timeout,
  cancelled and partial statuses are counted once; pre-provider failures remain
  ledger evidence but not Provider-call failures.
- `REPORT-AGG-B03`: otherwise identical events owned by two Integration Clients
  aggregate into one model-usage row with summed totals; response/filter options
  and CSV contain no client ID/name/prefix, while persisted ledger identities
  remain unchanged for audit.
- `REPORT-COST-B01`: provider amount/currency absent yields provider cost null;
  valid official zero retains zero/currency/source and is never replaced by an
  estimate.
- `REPORT-COST-B02`: complete positive input/output usage and OCR-model Token
  prices produce only token estimate components; missing a required positive
  component price yields unavailable rather than a partial estimate.
- `REPORT-COST-B03`: positive page/image usage with complete matching unit price
  produces only that unit basis; page/image count zero creates no component and
  cannot produce estimated zero.
- `REPORT-COST-B04`: when token and unit evidence/config coexist, deterministic
  basis selection prevents double charge; no other model row or hard-coded price
  is consulted.
- `REPORT-COST-B05`: PostgreSQL aggregation in a rollback transaction proves the
  response/CSV values and leaves existing usage/model rows unchanged.

### Regression And Release Gates

- Existing report scope, permission, project/date/status/source/model filters,
  paging and bounded export remain green. Former API-key filter-option tests are
  replaced by explicit absence and cross-client aggregation tests.
- Existing model usage normalization, pricing validation, official-zero and
  usage-ledger tests remain green.
- Run focused Frontend/Backend suites before full lint/build/test/coverage and
  governance/deployment-static checks listed in the development plan.
- Frontend and Backend coverage remain subject to their unchanged 80% gates.
  Existing global gaps must be reported and may not be waived.
- Any later image build, Kubernetes deployment, live OCR model pricing update or
  authenticated Browser acceptance requires a separately bounded approval.

  rollback-only cross-client aggregate and OCR cost-basis cases.
- Frontend contracts: `141 passed`; Frontend components: `42 passed`; focused

- Frontend lint, production build, i18n scan, Backend syntax, Helm lint,

## CHG-281 Markdown Structure-Aware Retrieval Pipeline Test Design

### Scope And Gate

- Gate 1 read-only diagnosis and Gate 2 confirmation completed on 2026-08-29;
  Peter confirmed with `同意 CHG-281 Gate 2，採用上述建議`.
- Gate 4 was approved with
  `Peter approves CHG-281 Markdown Structure-Aware Retrieval Pipeline`; repository
  implementation, additive migration and non-billable tests are authorized.
- TEST-002 integration and retrieval quality
  acceptance require real configured services; billable provider calls and pilot
  reprocessing remain separately exact-action gated.

### Parser And Raw-Trace Unit Cases

- `RAG-MD-U01 Heading`: H1/H2/H3 become typed nodes with exact spans and inherited
  `房貸 > 提前清償 > 違約金`; retrieval text contains labels/text but does not rely
  on `#`, `##` or `###`.
- `RAG-MD-U02 Inline formatting`: bold, emphasis, strike and visible HTML text
  retain business content while formatting tokens/tags are absent from retrieval
  text; canonical Markdown remains byte-equivalent.
- `RAG-MD-U03 Links/images`: link label and image caption enter semantic text;
  URL/object path remain metadata with exact source range.
- `RAG-MD-U04 Blockquote/code`: blockquote becomes a semantic note; fenced code
  content/language remain intact and raw fences are traceable.
- `RAG-MD-U05 Failure`: one malformed block becomes a warning paragraph and valid
  siblings continue; only a document with no readable text becomes failure.
- `RAG-MD-U06 Page/header/footer`: repeated boilerplate is excluded only with at
  least three reliable pages and recurrence evidence; uncertain page data keeps
  content and records warning.
- `RAG-MD-U07 Source trace`: every node/Chunk raw fragment matches canonical
  offsets/node IDs; full raw Markdown is not duplicated into every Chunk row.

### Structure-Aware Chunking Cases

- `RAG-CHUNK-U01 Lists`: ordered/unordered relationships and ordinals remain
  complete below max size; the list is not flattened into unrelated words.
- `RAG-CHUNK-U02 Small table`: `產品/利率` rows normalize to label/value units;
  separator pipes/alignment rows are not the primary representation.
- `RAG-CHUNK-U03 Large table`: batches obey row/token limits; every batch repeats
  headers and carries table id/title/row range.
- `RAG-CHUNK-U04 Heading boundary`: `提前清償` and `延遲繳款` never merge merely
  because the first is below target.
- `RAG-CHUNK-U05 Short section`: `章節：違約金` plus `免收。` stays independently
  understandable despite being below minimum.
- `RAG-CHUNK-U06 Long paragraph`: content over max first splits on sentences and
  only then a safe token boundary, without broken Unicode sequences.
- `RAG-CHUNK-U07 Overlap`: overlap applies only to split structural siblings and
  never duplicates a complete table/list/heading block.
- `RAG-CHUNK-U08 Context cap`: heading depth/prefix obey 4-level/96-token defaults
  while retaining the most relevant path.
- `RAG-CHUNK-U09 Determinism`: identical input/config/version yields identical
  UUID, stable key, sequence, ranges and texts; a processing-version change is
  traceably distinct.

### Retrieval, Hash And Index Contract Cases

- `RAG-RET-U01 Representation`: raw fragment, display text and retrieval text are
  distinct; legacy API `content` maps to display text.
- `RAG-RET-U02 Context`: document title and bounded heading path prefix semantic
  content; UUID/timestamp/page boilerplate/non-semantic URL do not.
- `RAG-RET-U03 Hash`: display-only changes do not alter the embedding hash;
  retrieval/context/model/version/dimension/tokenizer changes do.
- `RAG-INDEX-U01 Mapping`: mapping v2 declares approved metadata/vector fields;
  BM25 weights retrieval/document/heading/display and retains legacy fallback.
- `RAG-INDEX-U02 Manifest safety`: failed count/dimension/authorization/evaluation
  validation never changes the active manifest.
- `RAG-INDEX-U03 Generation`: authorized retrieval returns display/raw-reference
  metadata and LLM context uses display text, not a citation preview or retrieval
  prefix alone.

### Schema, API, Security And Compatibility Cases

- `RAG-COMP-B01`: V046 is additive/nullable and validates from schema 045 without
  rewriting existing Chunk rows.
- `RAG-COMP-B02`: legacy null-new-field Chunks remain readable/searchable through
  controlled fallback and retain CHG-273 behavior.
- `RAG-COMP-B03`: new source mappings validate raw fragment offsets; legacy
  mappings use their recorded processing-version contract.
- `RAG-COMP-B04`: reparse/rechunk creates a new extraction revision and never
  mutates an active published version in place.
- `RAG-COMP-B05`: debug API enforces existing authorization and cannot expose an
  unauthorized raw document or credential.
- `RAG-COMP-B06`: logs include IDs/counts/versions/duration but exclude raw/
  retrieval sentinel content and secrets.

### Real Integration And Retrieval Evaluation

- `RAG-LIVE-I01`: isolated real PostgreSQL rows/artifacts exercise canonical
  Markdown through normalization; cleanup leaves the existing 26 Chunks intact.
- `RAG-LIVE-I02`: disposable real OpenSearch staging index validates mapping,
  vector dimension, BM25/vector union, authorization rehydrate, counts and cleanup.
- `RAG-LIVE-I03`: with separately approved live embedding model, record exact
  model/request count and prove hash/vector/index consistency. No fake provider
  may satisfy this case.
- `RAG-EVAL-L01`: `A方案的利率是多少？` hits the table Chunk containing
  `產品：A方案` and `利率：2.1%` at expected K.
- `RAG-EVAL-L02`: `提前清償要不要收違約金？` hits
  `房貸 > 提前清償 > 違約金` at expected K.
- `RAG-EVAL-L03`: report deterministic Before/After Recall@K, MRR and Top-K Hit
  Rate with dataset/config/model identity; never claim improvement without data.

## CHG-282 Lossless Paginated Safe Markdown Rendering Test Design

Status: Gate 5 repository testing authorized. Gate 2 was confirmed on 2026-08-30
with `同意 CHG-282 Gate 2，採用上述建議`, and Peter approved Gate 4 with
`Peter approves CHG-282 Lossless Paginated Safe Markdown Rendering`. Image,
cluster, layout regeneration, authenticated Browser and Provider/data/index
actions remain separately gated.

### Requirements Under Test

- `VIEWER-003`: structure-aware continuation and a Frontend lossless paper
  safety boundary prevent clipping while preserving pages, anchors and parity.
- `MD-RENDER-001`: one CommonMark/GFM AST renderer supports the approved block
  and inline grammar across all shared rendered surfaces.
- `MD-SEC-001`: raw HTML, hostile URLs and unauthorized images remain inert,
  while semantic/accessibility behavior is retained.
- `MD-COMPAT-001`: raw source, legacy API/data, CHG-273/277/281 behavior and the
  non-Provider/non-index boundary remain unchanged.

### Backend Unit And Contract Cases

| ID | Input / action | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VIEWER-PAGE-B01 | A CJK/Latin paragraph whose estimated size exceeds one page, including punctuation and Unicode code points | Continuations join to the exact original visible text with no lost/duplicated code point; sentence/newline boundary is preferred and each part shares the source anchor. |
| VIEWER-PAGE-B02 | Ordered list beginning at 3, jumping to 7, containing nested unordered children and one oversized item | Page continuations preserve source order, start/value/nesting and stable continuation metadata; oversized child is split losslessly only after item boundaries are exhausted. |
| VIEWER-PAGE-B03 | Pipe table with header plus enough rows to span three pages | Every page batch repeats the same header, row order/count is exact and no separator/header becomes a data row. |
| VIEWER-PAGE-B04 | Fenced code with language, blank lines, backticks, `[1]` and enough lines for two pages | Split only on line boundaries; concatenated code and language metadata match input; code text is not interpreted as citation. |
| VIEWER-PAGE-B05 | Identical structure/config/version executed twice | Page numbers, block ordering, continuation IDs/ordinals/ranges and pagination metadata are deterministic; every normal page stays within budget. |
| VIEWER-PAGE-B06 | Legacy artifact without new fields, malformed block, and one unsplittable oversized unit | Legacy validates unchanged; malformed content falls back losslessly with warning; unsplittable unit gets a dedicated growable page rather than failure/clipping. |
| VIEWER-PAGE-B07 | Documents and approvals API read the same v2 and legacy artifacts | Both surfaces return equivalent page/block/source metadata without mutating stored artifact/data. |

The Backend suite must cover the new paginator module at least 80% line and
branch coverage. It must be pure/non-Provider and must assert that importing or
running the focused suite does not create database, index or artifact writes.

### Frontend Component And Security Cases

| ID | Input / action | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MD-RENDER-F01 | `` `vllm:num_requests_waiting` `` and `` `minReplica: 1` `` | Two semantic inline `<code>` nodes contain only the code text; visible backticks are absent. |
| MD-RENDER-F02 | Fenced `yaml`/`sql` blocks containing Markdown, HTML and `[1]` | Semantic `<pre><code>` preserves literal lines/language; no nested emphasis, HTML execution or citation control appears inside code. |
| MD-RENDER-F03 | H1-H6, soft/hard breaks, bold, italic, strikethrough, blockquote, horizontal rule, nested ordered/unordered/task lists, pipe table, safe link and image caption | Semantic DOM and expected text/order are present with no grammar-specific data loss. |
| MD-RENDER-F04 | CHG-277 list starts/jumps/restarts and a normal-text `[1]`/invalid `[9]` citation | Existing `ol[start]`, `li[value]`, citation labels/click/mismatch/focus behavior remains exact. |
| MD-SEC-F01 | `<script>`, `<img onerror>`, event attributes, raw iframe/style and malformed HTML | No dangerous DOM element/attribute executes or appears through an HTML path; safe surrounding text still renders. |
| MD-SEC-F02 | `javascript:`, control-character and protocol-relative links/images plus approved safe link | Unsafe targets do not become navigable/fetched resources; alt/caption remains visible; safe external links carry the required relation. |
| VIEWER-PAGE-F01 | Legacy page with a final selected block taller than the old fixed content row | Paper grows, complete text and highlight are visible, footer follows content and no vertical clipping/overlay selector remains. |
| VIEWER-PAGE-F02 | One source anchor represented by two continuation blocks on different pages | Mouse and Enter/Space selection highlight both blocks, toggle clears both, and Knowledge Detail/Approval Evidence maintain equivalent source navigation. |
| VIEWER-PAGE-F03 | Wide table/code at 1440, 1024, 768 and 375px plus 400% zoom | Horizontal scroll stays inside the content wrapper; paper, right panel, page number and 40px controls do not overlap or create page-level clipping. |
| MD-COMPAT-F01 | Same Markdown through rendered original, Chunk, Chat and Approval; canonical source through raw source view | Rendered surfaces share grammar/security behavior; raw source text remains byte-equivalent and unrendered. |
| MD-COMPAT-F02 | Existing CHG-273 canonical mapping, CHG-277 ordered list and CHG-281 display/retrieval fixtures | All retained regressions pass without source offset, citation, list or representation changes. |

Component tests must verify semantic elements and accessible behavior, not only
source-code Regex. The new shared Markdown/layout components must each exceed
80% line and branch coverage; repository coverage remains a separate release
gate and may not be relaxed.

## CHG-283 Markdown-Faithful Display And Retrieval-Only Embedding Test Design

Status: Gate 5 bounded repository testing completed with the release/integration
gaps recorded below. Gate 2 was confirmed with
`同意 CHG-283 Gate 2，採用上述建議`, and Peter approved Gate 4 with
`Peter approves CHG-283 Markdown-Faithful Display And Retrieval-Only Embedding`.
Non-Provider/disposable feature tests and additive V047 verification may run.
Provider, live data/index, image and deployment actions remain separately gated.

### Requirements Under Test

- `MD-DISPLAY-001`: full-content reading surfaces use a deterministic Markdown
  display projection, while canonical/raw fragments remain exact and
  `display_text` remains a distinct compatibility/LLM projection.
- `MD-STYLE-001`: shared semantic Markdown nodes, especially inline code, have
  equivalent DOM and core presentation across rendered surfaces.
- `RAG-EMBED-001`: every new/rebuilt vector and v2-ready index document uses
  validated `retrieval_text` only and fails before side effects when it is
  missing or inconsistent.
- `RAG-MANUAL-001`: manual create/edit/split uses the same parser, display
  projection, normalizer, token/version and hash boundary as automatic chunks.
- `MD-EMBED-COMPAT-001`: V047/API changes are additive; legacy rows stay
  read-only compatible and no existing data/vector/index is changed by
  repository implementation.

### Backend Representation Cases

| ID | Input / action | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MD-DISPLAY-B01 | Heading plus paragraph containing bold, emphasis, strikethrough, inline code, safe link and blockquote | `markdown_content` is the exact source fragment; `display_markdown` preserves Markdown semantics; `content` is the exact visible-text projection; `retrieval_text` contains bounded document/heading prefix plus normalized semantic body. |
| MD-DISPLAY-B02 | Ordered list with non-1 start, jumps, nested children and enough items for multiple Chunks | Every display projection contains only its selected items, preserves source ordinals/nesting and does not duplicate the complete parent list; combined visible content preserves source order. |
| MD-DISPLAY-B03 | Large pipe table split across three Chunks | Each display projection repeats the exact header and contains only its assigned rows; exact raw trace remains available; retrieval text preserves header/value relationships without pipe/separator noise. |
| MD-DISPLAY-B04 | Fenced code with language, blank lines, Markdown-like tokens and enough lines for multiple Chunks | Each display projection has a valid fence/language and only its lines; code bytes/indentation are preserved; retrieval body preserves code text and does not interpret it as Markdown/citation. |
| MD-DISPLAY-B05 | Same canonical input, config and processing versions run twice | Raw/display/text/retrieval projections, stable key and applicable hashes are deterministic; display-only version change leaves retrieval hash unchanged. |
| MD-DISPLAY-B06 | Malformed Markdown block followed by valid content | Fallback remains readable and traceable, records a safe warning and never rewrites OCR business text. |

| ID | Input / action | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RAG-EMBED-B01 | Valid structure-aware Chunk with raw/display sentinels and expected retrieval text | The strict resolver returns exactly `retrieval_text`; no raw/display-only sentinel or formatting token is present in the resolved Provider input. |

## CHG-287 Project Detail Owner Authorization Consistency Test Design

Status: Gate 2 confirmed on 2026-09-02 and administratively renumbered from the
provisional CHG-286 to CHG-287 because the repository already contains CHG-286.
Gate 3 test design is complete; Gate 4 is pending.

Requirements under test: specification section 10.44, `PROJECT-002` and
`PROJECT-008`.

### Backend Response Projection Cases

| ID | Scenario | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PROJECT-008-B01 | Active user is present in both `project_owners` and `project_members.owner`; serialize single-project detail | `is_owner=true`, roles contain one `owner`, and Owner capabilities remain true. |
| PROJECT-008-B02 | Same Owner reads list and detail for the same Project | `is_owner`, sorted role union and capabilities are identical across endpoints. |
| PROJECT-008-B03 | User has editor/viewer membership but no `project_owners` row | `is_owner=false`; scoped read remains available and Owner-only mutation is denied. |
| PROJECT-008-B04 | Owner also has editor or viewer membership | Response roles are a deterministic deduplicated union; Owner is not duplicated. |
| PROJECT-008-B05 | Successful create/update/archive/member-removal returns ProjectResponse | Every response path uses the shared projection and never falls back to schema defaults. Existing lock/status semantics remain unchanged. |
| PROJECT-008-B06 | Non-Owner calls PUT/DELETE member mutation directly | Backend rechecks governance and returns the existing safe 403 without a partial write. |
| PROJECT-008-B07 | Owner request uses stale `lock_version` or would remove the last Owner | Existing 409 guard remains authoritative and all membership/Owner rows are unchanged. |
| PROJECT-008-B08 | Inspect queries/logs for projection | Query is scoped to current Project/user and logs contain no token, credential or full LDAP DN. |

Tests must use real SQLAlchemy/PostgreSQL behavior in the configured disposable
test environment. A static source assertion or mocked authorization result may
supplement but cannot satisfy `PROJECT-008-B01..B07` under `TEST-002`.

### Frontend Contract Cases

| ID | Scenario | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PROJECT-008-F01 | Live-shaped Project detail has `is_owner=true` | Permission Management button appears to the right of Chat Test and opens the Modal. |
| PROJECT-008-F02 | Live-shaped Project detail has `is_owner=false` | Owner-only button/modal is unavailable; UI does not infer Owner from system role or unrelated capability. |
| PROJECT-008-F03 | Owner loads members, saves a role change and receives a fresh Project response | Modal stays usable, members and `lock_version` refresh, and corrected Owner state does not disappear. |
| PROJECT-008-F04 | Backend returns 403/409 for mutation | Localized error is visible and UI does not claim success or mutate the displayed authoritative state. |

Production Frontend behavior is expected to require no change. These regressions
prove the corrected Backend contract is consumed correctly; if they expose a
second defect, that scope must be recorded before changing Frontend code.

| PROJECT-008-L03 | Compare protected state before/after read-only acceptance | Project/Owner/member/role counts and digests, schema, documents, vectors/indexes and Provider usage are unchanged. |

### Backend Candidate Search Cases

| ID | Scenario | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PROJECT-009-B01 | Project Owner searches one eligible active user by display name, family/given name, full Email, employee ID and Email local part | Every alias returns the same safe user summary exactly once with deterministic ordering. |
| PROJECT-009-B02 | Active synchronized `user02`/`user05` has no effective `KnowledgeProjects.can_view` | User is absent from `items`; safe `ineligible_match_count` indicates a matching but ineligible identity without exposing its details. |

| PROJECT-009-B05 | Non-Owner, invisible Project, disabled actor or missing authentication calls the endpoint | Safe 401/403/404 policy applies and no candidate/ineligible identity evidence leaks. |

| PROJECT-009-B08 | Inspect item schema and logs | Only assignment-safe fields appear; no token, credential, full LDAP DN or full raw query is logged. |

| PROJECT-009-B11 | Apply V048 to a V047 disposable database | Exactly one active non-system `knowledge-project-user` and one `Menu.KnowledgeProjects` view-only permission exist; zero user/group assignments are created and schema columns/indexes are unchanged. |

### Backend Protected Owner Cases

| PROJECT-010-B01 | Project has exactly one effective Owner and an Owner attempts any role-set change on that row | Stable 409 last/protected-Owner error; all Owner/member roles and `lock_version` remain unchanged. |
| PROJECT-010-B02 | Sole Owner attempts DELETE on their membership | Stable 409; no row is deleted or partially changed. |
| PROJECT-010-B03 | Project has multiple Owners and actor attempts to change/delete their own Owner row | Stable self-Owner 409 for role-set and delete; entire row remains unchanged. |

| ROLE-UI-002-F03 | Viewport height exceeds or falls below 820px | Computed height is bounded by `min(86dvh, 820px)` with `vh` fallback and remains inside the backdrop safe area. |
| ROLE-UI-002-F04 | Middle content exceeds available height | Overflow scrolls vertically inside the dialog; outer dialog and background page remain stable with no horizontal overflow. |
| ROLE-UI-002-F05 | Scroll from first search control through the last checkbox/action | Header and footer remain stable, every control can receive visible focus, and no keyboard trap or obscured focused control occurs. |
| ROLE-UI-002-F06 | Open user, role, mapping, model, API-key and delete dialogs | Existing shared sizing remains unchanged; no CHG-290 fixed-height class applies. |

### Responsive And Live Browser Cases

- `ROLE-UI-002-E01`: desktop viewport, compare empty, eight-row and expanded
  draft-summary outer/header/footer bounding boxes.
- `ROLE-UI-002-E02`: 375px wide and short-height viewport, prove containment,
  internal scrolling and no horizontal/background-page overflow.
- `ROLE-UI-002-E03`: 400% zoom and keyboard-only traversal, prove reachable
  controls, visible focus and usable close/save actions.
- `ROLE-UI-002-E04`: confirm ROLE-UI-001 filter counts, pending add/remove,
  retained-source badges and manual-only save payload remain unchanged.
- `ROLE-UI-002-L01..L04`: repeat E01-E04 through a real authenticated Browser
  and live Backend after separately approved image/deployment; static markup,
  fixture UI or CSS source inspection is not live acceptance under `TEST-002`.

abort is not evidence of an artificially late-resolving promise; that historical
assertion remains explicitly unproven in the case ledger. No deployment is allowed.
